description:
Are your abrasive belts hanging on nails in your workshop? Print these premium belt storage hangers with swappable and customizable nameplates that are easy to swap out.

To make multi color name plates, perform a color swap around layer 4, I used a .6 nozzle at .3 layer heights, so if a .4 nozzle at .2 layer heights is used, I recoomend changing the color around the 5th or 6th layer. 

Comes with the following cards and CAD files so you can create your own:
- 36
- 60
- 80
- 120
- 200
- 240
- Fine
- Coarse
- Used


For the hanger itself, supports touching buildplate are recommended.

**This project was a comission and may be subject to minor changes to improve user experience, any customers will have immedeate access to any changes that may occur. Additional photos are coming soon**, (as soon as I get more filament).
  

Print orientation
![Print orientation](https://www.pinterest.com/pin/670966044513162599/)
details:
Approximately 75g of filament per hanger  (which is nearly half the material requirement of other belt hanger designs using similar slicer settings) 

**.6mm nozzle recommended but not required**

- - -

PETG - any color
Tree supports recommended
2 walls
25% infill
3 top
3 bottom

**Interchangable cards**
PLA or PETG (I happen to have more PLA colors and the interchangable card is not load bearing)
99 walls (better than 100% infill)

Filament change level for colored cards
- if using .30mm layer heights, color change at layer 4
- if using .25mm layer heights, color change at layer 5
- if using .20mm layer heights, color change at layer 6

name: AC MICRO CLAMP G-CLAMP G 25
description:
Mold for metal casting of a micro clamp in G-Clap style.

TENSION RANGE: 25-28mm

MATERIAL REQUIRED:

M5 threaded rod

Brass tube 6mm with 0.5mm wall thickness

(approx. 24mm for clamp and approx. 30mm for handle)

M5 tap and thread cutter

Insert the brass tube into the openings provided in the mold. The threaded nut and the clamping head must be drilled M5 and the thread must be cut accordingly.

Personally, I do not screw the head completely tight so that there is some movement play.

With the handle, the threaded rod can either be glued in or also fastened using an M5 thread (in the latter case, the brass sleeve should be shortened slightly and only inserted into the handle as a drilling jig protruding approx. 5mm, then close the end of the sleeve here).

ATTENTION: Due to shrinkage, the dimensions change slightly depending on the metal used for casting.

I recommend a resolution, layer height of 0.1mm to simplify reworking.

The model is normally smooth enough for casting with 2-3 layers of varnish.

DIMENSION: 97x43x18mm (for the entire ferrule)

Matching match plate for the iDN 80 cast iron piston enclosed.

Link to the cast iron piston:

https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/ac-gussform-formsandkasten-idn-80mm

Matching match plate for the iDN 100 cast iron flask enclosed.

Link to the cast iron flask:

https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/ac-gussform-formsandkasten-idn-100mm

Please use a fine casting sand for this casting, but it is still advisable to rework  a little if necessary, e.g. with a fine drill grinder (Dremel) or a file.

ATTENTION METAL CASTING as a HOBBY:

Please note that casting metals of all kinds involves risks to life and limb.

Always ensure that work paths and work surfaces are clear and wear the appropriate protective equipment (heat shield, goggles, gloves, aprons, protective masks, etc.).

Always work in well-ventilated or open spaces!

No liability is accepted for improper handling!

If you are a professional, I assume that the necessary safety measures will be taken anyway.

Please also take a look at my MetalCasting collection: https://cults3d.com/en/design-collections/AC-Design/metal-casting

Also have a look at my other designs:

https://cults3d.com/en/users/AC-Design/3d-models

name: Round Gear Shift Knob for BMW Vehicles
description:
Introducing the latest redesign of my gear shift knob, tailored originally for the BMW E36 but now offering improved design features for a superior driving experience. With a tighter fit from improved internal clearances, this iteration eliminates any unnecessary movement, ensuring optimal control during gear shifts.

This rounded gear knob should comfortably fit in your palm, as if you are holding a ball like a tennis ball. I had this design in PLA in my BMW for a number of years, though due to the heat distortion it kind of got a little stuck..

Crafted for durability, comfort, and ease of replacement, this gear shift knob boasts an ergonomic design and printable construction. Compatible with a wide array of BMW models, from classics to contemporary vehicles such as (E24 E28 E30 E31 E32 E34 E36 E39 E46 Z3 Z4 E38 E39 E53 X5 X3 E60 E61 E81 E82 E87), it ensures seamless integration across the board. Installation is effortless on all manual BMW models: simply pull upward to remove the old shift knob, place the new one on the metal shift rod, align the notch, and firmly press to secure it in place. 

Upgrade your BMW with our latest gear shift knob revision, prioritizing both comfort and performance for an unparalleled driving experience.

name: Chaka Can - The Lazy Person's Spray Paint Can Shaker
description:
The "Chaka Can" is a practical 3D-printed gadget designed to simplify mixing paint in spray cans. It's powered by your cordless drill, spinning a rotor that moves an arm back and forth. The arm securely holds the spray can, utilizing its built-in ball bearing to mix the paint thoroughly.

See it in action here ...   https://youtu.be/4KDTXzfLpUo

Base Unit
This sturdy foundation keeps everything stable while you work, ensuring reliable performance. It can be clamped to a tabletop or bench if needed, especially for lighter drills.

Rotor Assembly
The rotor, connected via the spindle to the drill, turns smoothly to aid in even paint mixing.

Mixing Arms
Assembled with included hardware, the arms extends to hold the spray can securely with clips. The rotor's motion causes the arm to move, activating the can's ball bearing for thorough mixing.

Operation
Using the Chaka Can is simple. Attach your cordless drill to the rotor assembly, clip the spray can onto the arm, and start the drill at a low speed (not exceeding 120 rpm to avoid damage). The spinning motion efficiently mixes the paint.

Benefits
Saves Time and Effort: No more manual shaking; let the Chaka Can do the work for you, saving time and effort.

Consistent Mixing: With a steady motion, the Chaka Can ensures thorough and consistent paint mixing every time.

Easy Setup and Use: Perfect for DIYers and Handymen, the Chaka Can simplifies painting projects.


Summary
The Chaka Can offers a practical solution for easier and more efficient mixing of spray can paint.

Assembly
1)	Begin by placing the provided bearings into the slots in both the Base Unit and Arm 1.
2)	Carefully insert the center rotor spindle into the base unit bearing, as shown.
3)	Place the washer onto the offset spindle on the opposite side of the rotor.
4)	Press the bearing on Arm 1 over the offset rotor spindle, ensuring a snug fit.
5)	Secure the arm by pressing the retaining clip over the spindle to lock it in place.
6)	Slide Arm 2 into the slot of Arm 1, aligning the holes on each. Ensure the Spray Can holder faces upward.
7)	Insert the 50x4 slotted screw through the upfacing hole, taking care not to force it. You may need to ream out the holes for smoother insertion.
8)	Place the supplied metal washer and bolt, ensuring not to over tighten.
9)	Attach your drill to the center spindle, ensuring not to over-tighten the chuck, which could cause damage.

Usage
Now that assembly is complete, clip in the Spray Can and slowly start your drill rotating until it reaches roughly 1 revolution per second. Then, gradually increase the speed to about 2 revolutions per second, the optimal speed for effective mixing. Avoid attempting to speed up the process, as this may damage the Chaka Can.
details:
Print using PLA. 
The unit uses 2x RS-608 bearings and 
1 x M4x40 Screw, washer and nut.
The ROTOR is printed on its edge.
The first arm prints flat and the Second on the edge so that the bracket faces upward. 
The Base prints best when both edges lie flat on the plate. 
Modify the spindles to be 70%. 
Standard infills, 
Use tree supports.

name: Drone Challenge Drop/Pickup Mechanism
description:
This project contains three parts that can assist you in creating a drop/pickup mechanism for drone challenge competitions. It has a base that attaches to the underside of your mini drone. It has a finger or claw that swings from the base. It contains a pivot from which you can attach links of various lengths to accommodate varying payload sizes. This mechanism was designed to use the following actuator (https://www.servocity.com/hitec-linear-servo-1-2-stroke-1-2-sec-6-8lb-thrust/). It provides 3kg of torque and a 30mm stroke to facilitate your payload pickup. All it needs is a PWM signal, a few fasteners and your linkage and you are set!

The best material to use for this build is a polycarbonate filament. The source for the hardware used for this project: Linear servo: www.servocity.com Claw ring: 40mm binder ring (any office supply) Linkage: 7mm wide aluminum strips (any craft store) Nuts and bolts: www.mcmaster.com

Contact me for more details and for a simpler way to acquire the additional parts.

name: Primer  feeder clip for LEE ACP (AUTOMATIC CASE PRIMING PRESS) 91610
description:
The  Lee ACP or AUTOMATIC CASE PRIMING PRESS (91610) is a fantastic reloading press created by Lee Precision to insert primer in brass cases of ammo before reloading.
To use pre-primed case in Lee presses  simplify a lot reloading operations as completely remove the known issue of Lee press priming system (especially on Lee Pro 1000)
Lee ACP is a new tool released by Lee precision, it works like the Lee APP press, having either a Case feeder than a primer feeder, and making case priming very  very fast.
Unfortunately this is a new product and have some defect, one of this is that primer not always flow properly. Primer feed needs to be moved often to let primer flow from the  tray to the die. 
In addition seems that the alignment between the primer chute and the die is not always fine, preventing the primer to go in the correctl position under the case.
The issue can be easily fixed, pushing the tray and the primer chute, in order to move it up a bit.

So this clip simply push the primer chute  at each movement of the leverge, ensuring proper flow of the primers, without any additional attention or manual effort!

I found it very useful, so uploading it here 

il video qui: 
https://youtu.be/eKW7j68zpEI?si=a6ZTsu4dfSOKFIB7

Enjoy!

name: Ducati Hypermotard 939
description:
The Ducati Hypermotard 939 was a naked machine part of the Hypermotard series in Ducati's range, manufactured from 2016 to 2018. The bike was presented at the 2015 EICMA Motorcycle Show in Milan, Italy, and replaced the Hypermotard 821 model.





In 2018, the Italian motorcycle manufacturer launched the Ducati Hypermotard 939, featuring several cosmetic and mechanical modifications. The new machine featured a Star White Silk paint job, combining the satin white color with the red frame and wheels, enhancing the bike's style.





The 2018 Ducati Hypermotard 939 was also available in an SP version, while both machines packed as standard equipment the Ducati Safety Pack (DSP), which included three-level ABS, eight-level Ducati Traction Control (DTC), and three riding modes. Each mode had different settings for better control in any road conditions.





In the appearance department, the bike was similar to its predecessors, packing the same duck beak-shaped front cowl, handguards, a one-piece dual seat, small side panels, a single-sided swingarm, and 10-spoke red-finished lightweight aluminum wheels.





The 2018 Ducati Hypermotard 939 was powered by a 937cc four-stroke liquid-cooled L-twin engine fed by an electronically controlled fuel injection system, boasting 113 hp with a peak at 9,000 rpm and 98 Nm (72 lb-ft) torque at 7,500 rpm.





In 2023, the 2018 Ducati Hypermotard 939 was for sale with an average price of $9,500, depending on its condition.

A funnel set designed to be compatible with plastic and steel 55-gallon drums. Use to refill, dump excess, or use the drums for waste oil and coolant. Wall Mount - designed to hold either funnel (or both, when stacked), this mount has 2 mounting holes and a sealed bottom to collect drips. Drill a hole in the bottom and a drain hose can also be attached (pictured).

name: Phelps3D 5 gallon bucket Mouse Trap
description:
This was designed in FreeCAD for a Christmas present for my father. It requires a 5 gallon bucket with lid to be modified into this mouse trap. You will also need a small board to create the mouse ramp. The bolt used for a counter weight was 18 grams (according to Google a typical mouse weighs between 20 and 35 grams). The hole for the bolt is 12 mm diameter so any that fit and weigh the right amount should work. I used 1 inch wood screws to attach the parts to the lid. There is a cutting template included. You will need to super glue the  bait basket to the underside of the teeter part near where the 2 slit vents reside. 

This can be used for humane catch-and-release or you can fill the bucket up with about 1/3 water and the rodents will drown. These may be ideal if you have a lot of possible mice to catch say in a farm barn or shed. The bait basket should be large enough to put cheese and/or peanut butter, etc. inside it. 

A full assembly video can be found at: https://youtu.be/lqns2983zks?si=-QBzCI4WFNDVDq6p
details: I suggest using PETG or ABS if you are going to place this anywhere the Summer heat can warp the parts, otherwise PLA should do. I printed most of the parts at 0.28mm layer height and 10% infill. I used 25% infill on the hinge parts. I used an 8 mm brim on all parts and supports on the teeter and hood.

name: TTN Chip Clip
description:
Important: 
1. LET COOL COMPLETELY BEFORE SQUEEZING. (I usually run them under cold water before ever attempting to open them.
2. PETG /+ WORKS MUCH BETTER THAN PLA /+. PETG IS NOT SO BRITTLE AND HOLDS ITS SHAPE BETTER. It also has a higher temperature tolerance, such as storing these in a camper or using them in a car.

This is just another chip clip. I printed several from Thingiverse and couldn't find one that held its flexibility to my liking so I designed my own. Some were really stiff and either broke or didn't return to their original position if opened too far. Others were really clever designs with locking cams but I wanted something that just worked quickly and easily.

So I went back to basics and my standby saying that sometimes less truly is more. Behold the TTN Chip Clip.

There are 4 versions. Two are medium-sized clips with 8mm and 10mm thicknesses respectively. Two are Larger sized clips with 8mm and 10mm thicknesses respectively. I've found the medium-sized clips work well for just about everything. The 8mm thick versions work fine but if you want more grip for some reason, the 10mm versions are a bit stiffer. You can always just adjust the Z in your slicer if you want to customize.

Print with 100% infill and/or have your wall thickness set to 2.4mm or greater.

As always, with anything with tight clearances, your printer and your slicer filament flow rate need to be calibrated properly. Make sure your printer prints are dimensionally accurate. I've left 0.30 clearance between the jaws which should be more than enough. It prints perfectly every time on my printers so if you have problems sticking, look at your flow rate percentage and make sure you're extruder E-Steps are properly calibrated. 

Again, Resist the temptation and LET THEM COOL BEFORE SQUEEZING.

description:

Click on Fusion to access the parameters:


In DESIGN > MODIFY > fx change parameters


A table appears, with the variable name in the "NAME" column and an explanation in the "COMMENT" column.


All you have to do is modify the values in the "Expression" column


All values are in mm


The following parameters can be modified:


Small coil diameter


Stop height (space between the two coils)


Width of stops (not necessarily necessary, but present in case there is a thickness offset in the center of the coil)


In the event of a problem: exit the model without saving, and reload it to start again with the default values.

description:
Two sets of Allen Wrench handles in the five most popular sizes. 
 
4mm, 3mm, 2.5mm, 2mm and 1.5mm

1.  Long handles -  130mm

2.  Stubby Handles - 85mm

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Neither set requires glue or any hardware to assemble.  The parts are a press fit so they can be disassembled at any point in the future to replace a worn Allen Wrench.

The holes on the back of the handles are not for hardware.  They are for inserting a punch to punch out the plugs holding the Allen Wrenches in place.

Print the Stubby version first, they are much handier, at least for me.  

GCODE:  The GECODE provided should work on almost all common printers, even those with auto bed leveling or not.  The .3mf files are for PrusaSlicer and are included if you need to change any parameters.

Filament:  PLA works fine, so should PETG.  However the provided GCODE was compiled using PLA temperatures (210°C) so if your filament needs more or less heat, load the .3mf file into PrusaSlicer and change the temperatures.

Enjoy.

name: Magnetic Wrist Clipper Guard Holder – 3 Slot Barber Quick Access Wristband
description:
A compact magnetic clipper guard holder designed to be worn directly on the wrist.

Instead of going back to the barber station every time you need to change a clipper guard, this wrist-mounted design keeps your three most frequently used guards right next to your hand.

The holder features 3 magnetic positions for quick access. Each position uses two magnets to help keep compatible clipper guards securely in place while still allowing them to be removed quickly during work.

The adjustable wrist strap makes it easy to fit different wrist sizes, and the slim design keeps the holder practical without becoming too bulky.

This design is intended for barbers, hairstylists, and anyone who frequently changes clipper guards during a haircut.

Main features:
• 3 clipper guard positions
• Wrist-mounted design
• Magnetic quick-access system
• 2 magnets per position
• 6 magnets required in total
• Adjustable wrist strap
• Compact and lightweight
• Designed for fast guard changes
• Suitable for everyday barber use

Important:
The clipper guards must contain metal or magnetic-compatible parts in order to attach to the holder.

Please check compatibility with your own clipper guards before printing.
details:
Recommended material: TPU

Nozzle: 0.4 mm

Layer height: 0.20 mm

Wall loops: 3 or more

Infill: 20–30%

Top / Bottom layers: 4 or more

Supports: Usually not required when the parts are printed in the recommended orientation

Brim: Optional

Print orientation:
Place the main wrist holder flat on the build plate whenever possible.

TPU is recommended if you want better impact resistance and slightly more durability for daily professional use.
1. Print all supplied parts using the recommended orientation.

2. Prepare 6 magnets in total.
Each of the 3 guard positions uses 2 magnets.

3. Before gluing the magnets, carefully check their polarity and make sure they are installed in the correct direction.

4. Press the magnets into the designed recesses.
If the fit is loose, use a small amount of CA glue / super glue to secure them.

5. Install the adjustable hook-and-loop wrist strap through the strap openings.

6. Adjust the strap so the holder sits securely on the wrist without being too tight.

7. Test your clipper guards before use.
The guards must contain metal or magnetic-compatible parts for the magnetic holding system to work.

8. Make sure all magnets are fully secured before professional use.

Magnets required: 6 pcs, Ø5 × 5 mm

Hardware required:

• 6 magnets5x5
• 1 adjustable hook-and-loop wrist strap
• CA glue / super glue (optional)

Finalmente siamo riusciti a pubblicare il nostro primo progetto. Sono davvero felice di presentarvi il mio telaio **WZ-1**, un progetto nato dopo numerosi test, prove e modifiche, con l'obiettivo di creare una piattaforma versatile e personalizzabile.

*** Deadbolt all'anteriore**

160 WHEELBASE con questo setup +\- in base al setup

Puo essere montata la nuova trasmissione di injora WG24 senza nessun tipo di problema

Naturalmente, è possibile utilizzare anche il **carrier bearing**, disponibile all'interno della cartella del file del progetto.

File e stampa
All'interno della cartella troverete il file STL completo, già pronto per essere importato direttamente nel vostro programma di slicing e stampato.
Il telaio è stato progettato per essere stampato **in un unico blocco**, non richiede supporti e non necessita di particolari procedure aggiuntive.

Sentitevi assolutamente liberi di sperimentare e creare il setup più adatto alle vostre esigenze.
Non vedo l'ora di vedere il **WZ-1** in azione e, soprattutto, di scoprire le configurazioni che riuscirete a realizzare!

Vi chiedo solamente di non vendere, distribuire o commercializzare il telaio o i file del progetto senza il mio consenso.

name: Mazda MX-5 NC Ducktail (Soft Top only)
description:
MX-5 NC Ducktail Spoiler

Printing, Post-Processing & Installation Guide

Important Notice

This model requires post-processing to achieve a finished, automotive-quality result.

By purchasing and using this model, you acknowledge that the printed parts will require additional work to achieve the final shape, strength and surface finish. The post-processing process may require the use of fiberglass, resin, body filler, primer and automotive paint.

The final fit, surface quality and appearance of the finished spoiler depend on the printer, printing material, print settings, post-processing technique and installation process used by the customer.

⸻

1. Preparing the Model for Printing

The model is provided as a large-scale spoiler and may need to be divided into multiple parts depending on the available build volume of your 3D printer.

Before printing:

Import the model into your preferred slicing software.
Divide the spoiler into the required number of sections according to your printer’s build volume.
Make sure that all sections are properly aligned and that the joining surfaces are clean and suitable for assembly.
Keep the original model orientation and geometry wherever possible.

The exact number of printed sections will depend on the size of your printer’s build plate.

⸻

2. Recommended Printing Materials

For automotive use, PETG should be considered the minimum recommended material.

For improved temperature resistance and dimensional stability, ABS or ASA is recommended.

Use appropriate printing settings for your chosen material and printer.

⸻

3. Possible Gaps After Printing

After printing and assembling the individual sections, gaps may appear between the parts, particularly in areas where the spoiler geometry becomes narrower.

This can occur due to:

Plastic shrinkage during cooling
Thermal deformation
Print warping
Differences between individual printed sections
Printer calibration and dimensional accuracy

Small gaps are therefore not necessarily a defect in the model and can be corrected during the post-processing stage.

⸻

4. Test-Fitting the Spoiler on the Vehicle

Do not permanently glue the printed sections together before test-fitting them on the vehicle.

First, place all printed sections together directly on the MX-5 NC trunk lid and check the overall curvature and fit.

Once the sections are positioned correctly:

Temporarily align the individual sections on the trunk lid.
Use a small amount of suitable adhesive to hold the sections together.
Allow the assembled spoiler to follow the curvature of the trunk lid.
Check the fit along the entire length of the spoiler.

Important

It is strongly recommended to assemble and initially bond the sections while they are positioned on the vehicle.

Do not fully assemble the spoiler away from the vehicle before checking the fit.

Plastic shrinkage and thermal deformation during printing can cause individual sections to slightly change shape. Permanently bonding the entire spoiler away from the vehicle may result in an incorrect overall curvature, preventing the finished spoiler from fitting the trunk lid correctly.

⸻

5. Fiberglass and Resin Reinforcement

Once the individual sections have been aligned and temporarily bonded into the correct shape, the spoiler can be reinforced and structurally unified.

Apply fiberglass and suitable resin to the appropriate surfaces of the printed spoiler.

During this stage:

Reinforce the joints between printed sections.
Cover and reinforce areas where necessary.
Use resin to fill remaining gaps caused by printing shrinkage.
Allow the resin to fully cure according to the manufacturer’s instructions. The fiberglass and resin reinforcement also helps create a stronger, more continuous structure between the individual printed sections.

Use appropriate personal protective equipment and follow the safety instructions provided by the manufacturers of the resin and fiberglass products.

⸻

6. Rough Sanding and Body Filler

After the fiberglass and resin have fully cured, inspect the entire spoiler.

If you find:

Depressions
Uneven areas
Unwanted protrusions
Visible print imperfections
Remaining gaps
Uneven joints

Begin with coarse sanding to remove major imperfections.

Body filler may be used where necessary to correct deeper imperfections and achieve a smooth surface.

Do not attempt to achieve the final surface finish with primer alone. Larger imperfections should be corrected with sanding and body filler before priming.

⸻

7. Final Surface Preparation

Once the overall shape has been corrected:

Sand the entire surface progressively using finer abrasives.
Remove all remaining imperfections.
Make sure all joints and transitions are smooth.
Clean the surface thoroughly.
Apply automotive primer suitable for your chosen finishing system.
Allow the primer to cure completely.
Sand the primed surface as required.

Repeat the filling, sanding and priming process if necessary until the desired surface quality is achieved.

The final result should have a smooth, uniform surface suitable for automotive paint.

⸻

8. Painting

Once the surface has been properly prepared and primed, the spoiler can be painted using any suitable automotive painting method available to you.

Depending on the desired finish, this may include:

Spray paint
Automotive basecoat and clearcoat
Professional automotive paint systems
Other suitable automotive finishing systems

Always ensure that the paint system is compatible with the primer and underlying materials.

Allow the paint and clearcoat to fully cure before final installation.

⸻

9. Final Installation

After the spoiler has been completely finished and the paint has fully cured:

Perform one final test fit on the trunk lid.
Confirm that the curvature and positioning are correct.
Mark the final mounting positions.
Use an appropriate automotive-grade mounting method.
Ensure that the spoiler is securely attached before driving the vehicle.

The exact mounting method may depend on the customer’s preferred installation method and any modifications made during post-processing.

⸻

Final Notes

This is a 3D-printable project intended for further fabrication and finishing. It is not supplied as a ready-to-install, finished automotive component.

The final result will depend heavily on:

3D printer accuracy
Material selection
Print settings
Assembly
Fiberglass reinforcement
Sanding and filling
Priming
Painting
Installation technique

Take your time during the fitting and finishing stages. Proper preparation is essential for achieving a professional-looking result.

PLA is not recommended for this application due to its relatively low heat resistance. A spoiler installed on a vehicle can be exposed to high temperatures, especially when the car is parked in direct sunlight.

This is a 3D printable replacement model for the linkage lever used in the center dashboard air vent assembly of the Ford Focus Mk3.

The linkage lever is part of the mechanism that opens and closes the center air vents. A broken lever can cause the vent control to stop working properly, resulting in loose, stuck, or non-functioning air vent flaps.

This replacement part is intended to repair a damaged or broken Ford Focus Mk3 center air vent mechanism. It may be suitable for vehicles where the dashboard air vent control no longer operates correctly due to a failed vent linkage lever.

Minor design modifications have been made to improve printability and durability while maintaining proper functionality. The design has been tested in a vehicle and verified to operate correctly in the intended application.

Recommended printing method: Resin (SLA/MSLA) 3D printing. Due to the small size and fine details of the part, FDM printing may not provide sufficient dimensional accuracy or long-term durability.

Possible symptoms of a damaged linkage lever:
•	Center air vents do not open or close correctly
•	Vent control feels loose or disconnected
•	Air vent flaps remain stuck in one position
•	Vent adjustment mechanism no longer operates as intended

Before purchasing, please compare your original part with the photos provided and verify compatibility with your specific vent assembly. The buyer is responsible for confirming fitment before purchase.

name: Case Starlink Mini - Suporte Magnético Starlink
description:
Esta é uma case de proteção e suporte magnético de alta resistência desenvolvida especificamente para a Starlink Mini. O projeto foi estruturado de forma inteligente para ser dividido em partes, facilitando a impressão e garantindo máxima robustez mecânica na fixação.

O conjunto é composto pela case principal de proteção e 4 suportes de canto independentes que se encaixam firmemente nas extremidades inferiores para travar a antena no lugar.

Para garantir que a antena possa ser fixada com segurança em superfícies metálicas (como o teto de veículos ou motorhomes), cada suporte de canto foi projetado para abrigar um ímã emborrachado com rosca macho M8. A ancoragem dos ímãs na peça impressa é feita através do uso de buchas roscadas (insertos latão M8) aplicadas a quente com ferro de solda, eliminando o risco de a rosca espanar no plástico.

Um projeto limpo, funcional e indispensável para quem viaja com a Starlink Mini e precisa de agilidade na instalação.
details:
Lista de Materiais Necessários (BOM):
4x Buchas roscadas / Insertos de latão para plástico (Rosca interna M8).

4x Ímãs de neodímio emborrachados com haste roscada macho M8.

Ferro de solda (para aplicação dos insertos a quente).

🖨️ Configurações Recomendadas de Fatiamento:
Material: Altamente recomendado imprimir em PETG, ABS ou ASA. Como é um projeto que frequentemente ficará exposto ao sol e calor no teto de veículos, o PLA não deve ser utilizado (irá deformar).

Altura de Camada: 0.2mm ou 0.24mm.

Paredes (Wall Line Count): No mínimo 4 a 5 perímetros (essencial para dar material suficiente ao redor do furo onde a bucha roscada será derretida).

Preenchimento (Infill): Mínimo de 30% a 40% (Giroide ou Grade) nos suportes de canto para aguentar o esforço mecânico dos ímãs.

Suportes: sem suporte

🔧 Passo a Passo da Montagem:
Instalação dos Insertos: Com o ferro de solda aquecido, posicione a bucha roscada M8 no furo guia localizado na parte inferior de cada um dos 4 suportes de canto. Pressione levemente com a ponta do ferro até que o inserto derreta o plástico uniformemente e fique alinhado com a superfície da peça. Deixe esfriar completamente.

Encaixe dos Cantos: Encaixe os 4 suportes nas extremidades inferiores da case principal.

Fixação dos Ímãs: Rosqueie os ímãs M8 diretamente nos insertos de latão recém-instalados até dar o aperto final.

Finalização: Encaixe a sua Starlink Mini na case e o sistema magnético estará pronto para uso.

name: Bair Hugger Adapter
description:
**Note: I thought it was called a "Bear Hugger" and it wasn't until WAY late I realized it was Bair Hugger, so you might see it in random places in the files XD. I'm not the veterinarian.**

This is my take on the WILDLY popular Bair Hugger adapters. I created this one to work with a 1 1/2 inch water hose. It's a tight fit even with the settings dialed in, so be warned, but the hose is optional. 

The three key features are the kennel adapter for the Bair Hugger hose, the interior air flow adapter, and the pillowcase air diffuser. If you don't want to make your own air distribution system, the kennel adapter will do wonders for you and your clinic. 

The pillowcase is a great way to spread out the warm air without it costing the clinic too much. Get the vet to do the sewing, they are good with needles! I hear they're okay with that. 

Link for the hose: https://www.amazon.com/JED-Pool-Tools-60-345-03-Connecting/dp/B000UOBHY4/ref=sr_1_3?dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.ejsPbc7btwWqz1sma9JxQo6Vqbef6wGrFJs_vgXGW1fbRtTAuyJTmbJx7oy034XumQZh11g3oOo8e-LsWTQhvVamVqcoWw0ZBN3_c3Ow0PdtpJRAZBUluJ74a6Rg7-fgrq4sMmz2dZU83rzKiaEIsC9yvYUEBpvAiRuuNsqMe2riQ4PPr_SSjk57zTrKrrPqZ-eKlXBtH5_gwjvAhJLTyF4qQhd3tS8U5T7qOkz4zek.trFXimTHYJYfOL9nTNOUogv73yZ8LRmPjbqjcYcsgXs&dib_tag=se&qid=1776736819&sr=8-3&srs=3230204011&th=1
details:
I would suggest using ABS/ASA or another higher temperature filament. Although the air shouldn't get very high, it's good to have something that wont off gas at lower temperatures. 

ALWAYS MAKE SURE YOU KNOW WHAT TYPE OF MATERIALS YOU'RE USING WHEN PRINTING FOR A CLINIC. 

I would also suggest increasing the wall loops vs infill. Several sources have shown that the wall loops give way more strength than infill percentages. 

I designed this model to not require any supports. Find the correct orientation and you shouldn't either!

name: Joint-O-Mator 127 - Professional Magnetic King Size Cone Knockbox
description:
Joint-O-Mator 127 – Professional Magnetic King Size Cone Knockbox

Designed for professional users and high-volume pre-roll production. The Joint-O-Mator 127 is a heavily engineered batch cone filler built for scale, consistency, and a zero-friction workflow. This is not a flimsy stacking toy—it is a tightly integrated 5-part system built around an ultra-tight mechanical friction fit and a highly modular, polarity-guided magnetic core.


The Joint-O-Mator Ecosystem comes in 7 capacities: 
37 · 61 · 85 · 127 · 169 · 217 · 271 


⚙️ The Foundation: Ultra-Tight Friction Fit (Parts A, B & C)

The structural integrity of the main body does not rely on magnets. Instead, the core assembly is mechanically locked:

	•	Part A (The Honeycomb Tray): Holds 127 King Size cones.

	•	Part B (The TPU Damping Ring): Absorbs vibration shock and stops the unit from walking across your table.

	•	Part C (The Outer Hex Frame): The rigid exoskeleton.

When you slide Parts A, B, and C together, the tight tolerances create a permanent friction fit. They become a single, rock-solid block capable of handling heavy vibration without rattling apart. No screws, no glue, no play.


🧲 Modular Magnetic Interaction: Parts D & E

While the base is mechanically locked, the interaction with the knockbox is entirely magnetic. During slicing, you will schedule pauses to drop 8x3 mm neodymium magnets directly into the print. The polarity is strictly mapped so that parts will only snap together in the correct orientation.

The modularity of Part D (Lid / Base Plate) & Part E (Magnetic Insert): Both parts can be magnetically attached to either the top or the bottom of the solid A/B/C base, depending on your current workflow step.

	•	Manual Filling / Tapping Mode: Snap the Lid (Part D) to the top to prevent material from spilling while manually tapping the unit. Alternatively, snap it to the bottom to act as a solid base.

	•	Press-Fill Mode: Snap Part E magnetically under the Lid (Part D), then attach both to the top. As you push down slightly, Part E applies uniform downward pressure to manually pack and settle the material evenly across all 127 holes.

	•	Ejector Mode: Once filling is done, remove the Lid and snap Part E under the solid A/B/C base block. The perfectly aligned geometry pushes the entire batch of cones approximately 15 mm upward simultaneously. You get clean, tool-free extraction without crushing or individually digging out a single joint.


⚡ The “Shake it” Vibration Add-on (Sold Separately)
Manual tapping is obsolete in a production environment. The Shake it is an independent, heavy-duty magnetic vibration module powered by a 3650 motor and an 8x AA battery pack. Because it is fully battery-operated, your entire knockbox system remains 100% portable—no wall outlets or restrictive cables tying you to a desk.

Thanks to the universal magnetic layout, the Shake it snaps dead-center onto the lid (Part D) of any Joint-O-Mator size from 37 up to 271. Turn it on, and it violently but evenly shakes the solid A/B/C base to pack your cones perfectly in seconds.

https://cults3d.com/de/modell-3d/werkzeuge/shake-it-magnetic-vibration-add-on-for-joint-o-mator

🖨️ Technical Print Specifications

Build Volume Requirements:

	•	Sizes 37 / 61 / 85 / 127: Fit comfortably on any standard 256 x 256 mm bed (e.g., Bambu Lab X1C / P1S / A1).

	•	Sizes 169 / 217 / 271: Require a large-format printer with a minimum true build plate of 320 x 320 mm (e.g., Bambu H2D/H2S, Voron 2.4 350, Prusa XL).

🛒 Hardware Bill of Materials (BOM)

You will need standard 8x3 mm round neodymium magnets. A visual polarity guide is included in the project files.

	•	Joint-O-Mator 37 / 61 / 85 / 127: Requires 27x magnets total.

	•	Joint-O-Mator 169 / 217 / 271: Requires 45x magnets total.

	•	(If building the Shake it module: Requires an additional 20x magnets).

With this purchase you only receive the print files for the Joint-O-Mator version in the titel; no other sizes are included.

name: 125mm to 150mm Duct Adapter — Reducer Increaser with Hose Clamp Grooves | 5 Inch to 6 Inch HVAC Extraction Van Camper Workshop
description:
5 inch to 6 inch — the closest-tolerance large-bore transition in the series, and the one that looks deceptively simple until you try to source it. A 25mm step across two large standard sizes that appear constantly in the same installation.
125mm / 5 inch and 150mm / 6 inch are both high-volume duct standards in residential, commercial, and industrial HVAC. They coexist in the same systems regularly — a 5 inch branch feeding a 6 inch extraction main, a 150mm centrifugal fan stepping down to 125mm flexible ducting, a commercial kitchen canopy running 6 inch main trunk with 5 inch branch connections. The gap between them is modest but precise, and forcing one into the other without a proper fitting always results in a leaking, rattling joint that fails under sustained airflow pressure.
The squat, wide-rimmed profile of this adapter reflects the geometry accurately — a 25mm differential across a large base diameter produces a broad, low-profile cone where both the 125mm and 150mm ends are visually close in size but mechanically distinct. Every millimetre of that transition is handled with 4mm wall thickness, proper hose clamp grooves, and a smooth internal bore that keeps the 6 inch airflow capacity intact through the fitting.

✅ What Makes This Different

4mm uniform wall thickness — consistent through the full wide shallow cone, critical at large diameter where even modest flex at the rim creates clamp seal failure
Dual hose clamp grooves — positive mechanical seat at both the 125mm and 150mm ends; both grooves are carrying large-circumference clamp load and are dimensioned for it
Smooth internal bore — the shallow taper across a large diameter produces one of the lowest flow restriction profiles in the series; the airflow barely knows the transition happened
Both ends clean imperial — 125mm / 5 inch to 150mm / 6 inch; full global coverage across every market that uses either sizing convention
Large-bore close-tolerance fit — the 25mm differential at this diameter range is the closest step-up available in large-bore ducting; serves installations where only a modest size increase is needed
Bidirectional — 125→150 increaser or 150→125 reducer depending on install direction
Support-free print — large end down, no support structures required


🔧 Application Examples

Commercial and residential HVAC 5 inch branch to 6 inch extraction main
Large grow tent ventilation — 5 inch carbon filter or fan to 6 inch trunk ducting
Industrial workshop extraction — 125mm branch outlet to 150mm main collector port
150mm / 6 inch centrifugal fan stepping down to 125mm / 5 inch flexible duct
Commercial kitchen extraction — 5 inch branch to 6 inch main canopy trunk
Marine commercial vessel ventilation — large-bore branch to trunk connection
Heat recovery ventilation systems — 5 inch distribution branch to 6 inch main unit port
Server room and data centre cooling — 5 inch supply branch to 6 inch plenum main

📦 What's Included
1× STL file — 125mm → 150mm (5 inch to 6 inch) duct adapter, print-ready, no supports required, pre-oriented for optimal layer adhesion through the wide shallow bowl geometry.
details:
🖨️ Print Settings — Read This Before You Slice
Wide shallow bowl, large base diameter, 25mm differential — the shallow taper across a large circumference makes this one of the most surface-area-intensive prints in the series despite the modest diameter step.
PETG is the correct material for this adapter across all functional applications. ASA for outdoor, industrial, sustained-heat, or UV-exposed installs — strongly recommended given the large surface area at both the 125mm and 150mm ends. PLA+ is not appropriate for any functional application at this diameter.
Use a 0.2mm layer height, 7–8 walls minimum, and 5–6 top/bottom layers. Infill at 0–15%. Large-end-down orientation is mandatory — the 150mm rim must build upward from the plate. The wide, shallow cone means there is almost no taper angle to assist with overhang management if oriented incorrectly; print it the right way up without exception.
The shallow taper at large diameter is the defining print challenge of this adapter. The cross-section changes slowly across a wide area, which sounds forgiving but actually means the slicer is producing long, large-circumference wall loops at near-constant diameter throughout most of the build. This is exactly the geometry that wall-count printing excels at — consistent loop length, consistent bond quality, uniform layer adhesion from base to rim on both the 125mm and 150mm ends. Seven to eight walls, minimal infill, large end down. The finished part will be one of the most uniformly constructed in the series.

name: 75mm to 100mm Duct Adapter — Reducer Increaser with Hose Clamp Grooves | 3 Inch to 4 Inch HVAC Diesel Heater Van Camper RV
description:
3 inch to 4 inch — one of the most frequently searched duct transitions on the planet, and one of the hardest to find as a clean, properly engineered fitting. This is it.
75mm / 3 inch and 100mm / 4 inch are the two most common duct sizes in residential and commercial HVAC worldwide. They appear together in almost every ducted system — a 3 inch branch feeding into a 4 inch trunk, a 100mm inline fan stepping down to 75mm flexible duct, a diesel heater outlet transitioning into a large-bore main run. The 3-to-4-inch adapter is one of those fittings that every builder eventually needs, and finding one that's properly constructed rather than thin-walled and floppy is harder than it should be.
The DT3D 75→100mm holds 4mm wall thickness across the full transition cone, carries dual hose clamp grooves at both ends, and delivers a smooth internal bore that handles the 25mm diameter differential without creating a turbulence trap. Built to stay installed.

✅ What Makes This Different

4mm uniform wall thickness — maintained across the full cone, including the mid-transition zone where thinner designs flex under clamp load
Dual hose clamp grooves — positive mechanical seat at both the 75mm and 100mm ends; no slip, no rotation under vibration or thermal cycling
Smooth internal bore — the 25mm diameter step is handled with a gradual taper; clean airflow with minimal pressure drop through the transition
Global standard sizing — 75mm / 3 inch to 100mm / 4 inch covers the most common branch-to-trunk transition in residential HVAC worldwide
Bidirectional — 75→100 increaser or 100→75 reducer depending on install direction
Support-free print — large end down, no support structures required


🔧 Application Examples

Residential and commercial HVAC 3 inch branch to 4 inch trunk duct
Diesel heater 75mm / 3 inch outlet to 100mm / 4 inch flexible trunk run
Campervan and van build main heating circuit transitions
100mm / 4 inch inline fan stepping down to 75mm / 3 inch flexible duct
Marine cabin ventilation — 3 inch to 4 inch trunk connection
Workshop dust extraction — 75mm hose to 100mm collector port
Grow tent ventilation — 3 inch port to 4 inch ducting or vice versa


📦 What's Included
1× STL file — 75mm → 100mm (3 inch to 4 inch) duct adapter, print-ready, no supports required, pre-oriented for optimal layer adhesion through the transition cone.
details:
🖨️ Print Settings — Read This Before You Slice
Mid-to-wide angle cone geometry, 25mm diameter differential — solid settings matter here, particularly through the transition zone.
Print in PETG for best all-round performance. ASA for outdoor, marine, or exhaust-adjacent installs where UV and moisture resistance are required. PLA+ for indoor ambient-temperature applications only — not recommended near diesel heater ducting.
Use a 0.2mm layer height, 6–8 walls, and 5–6 top/bottom layers. Infill at 0–15% — the walls carry all structural load. Orient large-end-down on your build plate; no supports needed, and this orientation puts layer lines perpendicular to clamp stress at both ends where the hose clamps will seat.
The 25mm diameter differential gives the slicer a steadily expanding cross-section to work through. High infill through this geometry produces increasingly short direction-reversing passes as the bore widens — slow, poorly bonded, and structurally redundant compared to solid walls. Six to eight wall loops track the cone cleanly from bottom to top, bond consistently through the transition, and deliver a part that handles clamp load at both ends without delamination. Print it right the first time.

name: 3D Printable Mug Casting Tool for Resin & Plaster
description:
Manufacture your own classic mugs or create perfect master models with this professional-grade Split Cup Mold system. Engineered for precision and ease of use, this multi-part casting tool features a solid base plate with perfectly toleranced hemispherical registration keys (alignment domes) to ensure the two side halves lock together flawlessly every time.

Whether you are 3D printing this to cast resin or plaster, using it as a master for silicone mold making, or CNC machining a durable production mold out of tooling board, these high-quality CAD files provide exactly what you need.

Key Features:

    Classic Mug Design: Features a timeless, smooth coffee cup silhouette with a comfortable, ergonomic handle.

    Precision Split Mold System: Designed as a 2-part block mold with an interlocking base plate to prevent shifting and leaking during the casting process.

    NURBS Precision: Created natively in Plasticity. The included STEP file ensures flawless, mathematically perfect curved surfaces for CNC machining, completely free of the low-poly faceting found in standard mesh files.

    Versatile Manufacturing: Ideal for casting resin, plaster, jesmonite, concrete, or as a master for ceramic slip-casting workflows.

Included File Formats:

    STL: High-resolution meshes, ready to slice and 3D print.

    OBJ: Standard format compatible with most 3D rendering and visualization software.

    STEP / STP: Solid CAD file, perfect for CNC CAM toolpath generation or parametric editing.

    Plasticity: The original source file, allowing you to easily adjust tolerances, add custom logos to the mug, or scale the design.
details:
For FDM / Resin 3D Printing:

    Print Orientation: * Base Plate: Print flat on the build plate.

        Mold Halves: Print resting on their flat outside faces (the backs of the blocks) so the inner mug cavity faces upwards. This ensures the smoothest surface finish for the casting area.

    Supports: You will not need supports for the main cavities if oriented correctly. You may need minor supports if your printer struggles with the bridging inside the alignment dimples.

    Layer Height: 0.12mm to 0.16mm. A finer layer height is highly recommended to minimize layer lines inside the mug cavity, reducing the need for post-sanding.

    Infill: 20% - 30% (Cubic or Gyroid pattern). A sturdy infill is required to withstand the clamping force when tying the mold halves together.

    Walls/Perimeters: Use at least 4 walls to ensure the mold is completely watertight.

    Usage Tip: Always apply a suitable mold release agent (like petroleum jelly, paste wax, or silicone spray) to the inner walls and alignment keys before pouring your casting material. Use strong rubber bands or trigger clamps to hold the two halves securely together.

For CNC Machining:

    Software: Import the .STEP file directly into your CAM software (e.g., Fusion 360) for exact geometry recognition.

    Tooling: Use a flat end-mill for roughing out the block and clearing the main cavity. Switch to a ball-nose end-mill for the 3D finishing passes to capture the smooth curves of the mug and the round registration domes perfectly.

    Material: Renshape (tooling board), Delrin, or Aluminum are excellent choices for creating a permanent, heavy-duty production mold.

name: lautux Turbotastic Pro 2 Holder
description:
This is a universal holder for the lautux Turbotastic Pro 2 and all of its accessories. The vacuum itself simply snaps into the round opening. The pieces that make contact with the Turbotastic are printed in TPU 90A to avoid scratches from hard plastic-on-hard plastic contact, and they should also help with the snap fit and overall grip. The accessories / nozzles are inserted from below with another snap fit. There is also a small hook to store the charging cable. (The two colors in my photos are just because one filament roll ran out and I switched to another color mid-print.)

The holder consists of multiple parts that need to be glued together. Two pieces make up the main body; they’re split so the large top surface can be printed flat on the bed for a nicer finish. The other two pieces are the TPU 90A contact pads that touch the Turbotastic.

By selecting a “Holder” variant, you can choose your preferred mounting method:

- Screw: Any 4 mm countersunk screw
- [MultiBoard](https://www.printables.com/model/1074671-raised-multiconnect-generic-connector-for-multiboa) *`mc25`*: Using the Multiconnect interface (25 mm spacing)
- [openGrid](https://www.printables.com/model/1214361-opengrid-walldesk-mounting-framework-and-ecosystem) *`mc28`*: Using the Multiconnect interface (28 mm spacing)
- 3M Command Strip: A 20 x 70 mm strip will fit, with a recess that lets it sit almost flush against the wall
- Combinations with screws: Even more universal, but experimental
- Blank: Backplate without holes or cutouts

For the Multiconnect connections (for MultiBoard or openGrid spacing), I usually like using [this snap](https://makerworld.com/en/models/1307474-opengrid-multiconnect-snaps) or [this anti-rotation snap](https://makerworld.com/en/models/1898333-multiconnect-anti-rotation-snaps-for-opengrid). Note the small recess in the middle that helps secure the holder in place when fully engaged.

I enabled support for the two main body pieces. For the “Top” piece, supports are only needed on the surface where the “Contact Top” piece sits (that area might need a bit of cleanup). For the main “Holder” piece, support is only needed for the cable hook. I also enabled the Arachne wall generator for that part, because otherwise a tiny section of a wall wouldn’t have printed. Other than that, the default settings should work fine. In general, everything is designed to be easy to print: the holes have a teardrop shape, and the upper edge of the Command Strip cutout is angled.

You will get not only the standard `.stl` files for 3D printing, but also `.step` files for easier modification.

I designed a newer version than the printed one shown in the photos. Improvements:

- Different placement of the accessory slots to make room for one larger nozzle
- Moved the USB-C cable holder to a more convenient spot, closer to the center
- The pieces that are meant to be glued together now have a notch for easier alignment
- Improved snap fit of the accessory slots

For **commercial use**, please take a look at [this page](https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/lautux-turbotastic-pro-2-holder-commercial-use).

name: Precision Clay Roller (240 x 150 mm) ( Pølseruller )
description:
For English scroll down. 

Præcisions-Pølserulle til Keramik (240 x 150 mm)
Er du træt af at rulle lerpølser, der aldrig bliver helt jævne, eller som ender med at blive tyndere på midten? Dette værktøj er designet til at give dig en perfekt, ensartet tykkelse hver eneste gang – hurtigt og uden besvær.

Gennemtænkt design til pottemageren
Dette er ikke bare et simpelt bræt, men et komplet system udviklet til præcision i keramikværkstedet. Med et arbejdsareal på 240 x 150 mm er rullen stor nok til de fleste opgaver (hanke, flagstænger, coil-building), men samtidig kompakt nok til at passe på de fleste standard 3D-printere.

Hvad gør dette design unikt?

Flex-Snapfit: Afstandsstykkerne monteres med et smart, fleksibelt snapfit-system. Det sikrer, at de sidder klippefast under brug, men er lette at klikke af og på, når du skal skifte tykkelse.

16 størrelser inkluderet: Der medfølger afstandsstykker fra 5 til 20 mm, så du er dækket ind til alt fra fine detaljer til kraftige hanke.

Fuld frihed (CAD-filer): Jeg har inkluderet både Fusion 360 (.f3d) og STEP-filer. Det betyder, at du har fuld mulighed for at tilpasse designet eller lave dine helt egne afstandsstykker, hvis du har specielle behov.

Sådan bruger du den:
1 - Klik de ønskede afstandsstykker på brættet.

2 - Form en grov pølse af ler med hænderne.

3 - Læg brættet oven på leret på et fladt bord.

4 - Rul frem og tilbage med et jævnt pres, indtil afstandsstykkerne rører bordpladen. Giv den et par ekstra rulle-ture for at sikre, at pølsen er helt rund.
Resultat: En perfekt, snorlige lerpølse i præcis den tykkelse, du har valgt!




English
-

Precision Clay Coil Roller (240 x 150 mm)
Tired of rolling clay coils that end up uneven, flat, or thinner in the middle? This precision tool is designed to give you perfectly consistent thickness every single time—quickly and effortlessly.

Smart Design for the Pottery Studio
This isn't just a simple board; it’s a complete system developed for accuracy in the ceramics workshop. With a working surface of 240 x 150 mm, the roller is large enough for most tasks (handles, mugs, coil-building) while remaining compact enough to fit on almost any standard 3D printer.

What makes this design unique?

Flex-Snapfit: The spacers are mounted using a smart, flexible snap-fit system. This ensures they stay firmly in place during use but remain easy to click on and off when switching thicknesses.

16 Sizes Included: The set comes with spacers from 5 to 20 mm, covering everything from fine decorative details to sturdy mug handles.

Total Freedom (CAD Files): I have included both Fusion 360 (.f3d) and STEP files. This means you have full access to modify the design or create your own custom spacers if you have specific needs.

How to Use It:

4 - Roll back and forth with even pressure until the spacers touch the table. Give it a few extra rolls to ensure the coil is perfectly round.
Result: A flawless, uniform clay coil in exactly the thickness you chose!

name: MINI VOLT: Small Size, Massive Power | Ultra-Compact 22.5W DIY Power Bank
description:
🌍 The Eco-Hacker Manifesto: Why You Need to Build This
We live in an era of disposable tech and planned obsolescence. Every year, millions of perfectly healthy 18650 lithium-ion cells are thrown into the e-waste abyss just because a cheap laptop motherboard or a power tool BMS failed. It’s a tragic waste of potential. 

But true makers and tech geeks don't buy into that. We salvage. We upcycle. We build. 

The Mini Volt isn't just a power bank; it’s a middle finger to e-waste and a badge of honor for the modern "cyber-scavenger". Extracting those forgotten 18650 cells, testing them, and giving them a second life in a custom, 3D-printed PETG armor is the ultimate geek rite of passage. It perfectly aligns with the Right to Repair and Zero Waste movements. Plus, pulling out a pocket-sized, 22.5W fast-charging reactor that you *built yourself* is the ultimate EDC flex. 

♻️ Built for Recycling & Upcycling
Depending on the condition of the salvaged cells you use, you can easily achieve a capacity of around **6,000 mAh** in a form factor that easily fits in the palm of your hand.

⚡ Advanced & Affordable Electronics
The enclosure is tailored for an extremely compact 22.5W fast-charging module that can be found on AliExpress for **only around $3!** ([Link to the exact module used](https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005007232950866.html)). This module features:
- Power Delivery (PD) for fast charging modern smartphones.
- Built-in temperature control** for safe operation.
- Digital display** showing the exact battery charge percentage.

⚠️ Important Print Warning: Because of the heat generated by the 22.5W fast charging and Power Delivery, you must print this in PETG (or ABS/ASA). Standard PLA will warp and deform over time!

🔋 Battery Safety & Discharge Calculations
To safely deliver 22.5W of output power, your battery pack needs to handle the internal current draw. 
Factoring in boost-converter efficiency (~85%) and low-battery voltage states (down to ~3.0V), the internal power draw can reach around 26.5W.
26.5W ÷ 3.0V = ~8.8 Amps.
Conclusion:  For a safe margin, your complete parallel battery pack should be rated for at least 10A continuous discharge. Since we are using two 18650 cells in parallel, each individual cell must have a minimum continuous discharge rating of 5A (10A per cell is even better). Always check your cells' datasheet!

⚠️ CRITICAL VOLTAGE WARNING:  Before permanently connecting your two 18650 cells in parallel, use a multimeter to ensure they are at the exact same voltage (e.g., both at exactly 3.60V). If there is a significant voltage difference, a massive equalization current will flow between them, which can cause overheating or a fire!

Required Hardware & Components (BOM):
- 1x Compact 22.5W Power Bank Module with Display - [Buy on AliExpress](https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005007232950866.html)
- 2x 18650 Li-Ion cells (connected in parallel to achieve 3.7V)
- 1x Nickel strip & spot welder (to safely connect the cells)
- 2x 18 AWG wires (Crucial! Thinner wires might melt or limit the 22.5W output)
- 5x M2x4 or M2x6 screws (3x for securing the PCB, 2x for closing the enclosure)
details:
3D Printing Settings:
Material: PETG (Strictly required for heat resistance!)
Layer Height: 0.12 mm (For a smoother finish and better tolerance fit)
Infill: 15% - 20% (Gyroid pattern used and recommended for a great strength-to-weight ratio and stress distribution)
Wall loops / Perimeters: 3 to 4 (for structural integrity)
Orientation:Print flat on the build plate. No supports needed.
- Print Time:  ~2h 30m (tested on Bambu Lab A1 Mini)
- Print Weight: ~28g (very lightweight and cost-effective)

Assembly Notes:
1. Print all 3 parts: `miniVOLT_Bottom.stl`, `miniVOLT_Top.stl`, and `miniVOLT_Button.stl`.
2. Ensure both 18650 cells have the exact same voltage.
3. Use a spot welder and a nickel strip to connect the cells in parallel (positive to positive, negative to negative).
4. Solder the two 18 AWG wires from the battery pack to the module (keeping the wires as short as practically possible). 
5. Secure the PCB inside the bottom case using three M2x4 or M2x6 screws.
6. Place the button in the top cover, align the electronics and battery pack inside the enclosure.
7. Close the case and secure it using the remaining two M2x4 or M2x6 screws.

name: Model Paint Stand Turntable
description:
This is a Turntable Base I made for painting my Gundam, Miniatures and 3D Prints. I usually just lay them flat but sometimes I use Alligator clips.

There two versions: holes are 2mm OR 3mm wide and 7mm deep.
You need a single 608RS or 608ZZ bearing (22m wide, 8mm inner diameter, 7mm height).
For Testing if your Alligator clips work I added some Test pieces that you can quickly print if you don't have a caliper to measure the diameter of the alligator clips wire.

Press the bearing firmly into the plate (should be flush) and then carefully clip it onto the Bottom piece. If attached firmly it doesn't wiggle (additionally you should add some superglue).

On the Bottom Part you can put 6 rubber feet to prevent slipping. I used 8mm wide, 1mm high ones.

Optionally you can print the pyramids to stick them into the holes (just make sure not to break them). When you paint obejcts with flat surfaces on the bottom it helps covering as less surface as possible.

EDIT: Some users had trouble with tolerances and wobbly so I tightened down the tolerances on the 3mm version to make it fit to snap with the bearing. You can still add some superglue but you WILL need to use rubber feet now to prevent the bottom to slip when to rotate the plate (logically its now bit more harder to turn)
Feel free to check out the update and give some feedback :)

name: Modular WE M4 / 416 / Scar L HPA Adapter (M4 / MP5 magazines)
description:
SUMMARY OF THE ADAPTER
This is a modular HPA adapter designed for the WE M4/416 platform, letting you run different AEG magazine styles – M4 or MP5 – depending on your loadout.

https://youtu.be/E9SgqZyVLgU

When purchasing, you'll receive all the files necessary to print this HPA adapter. you'll receive both the M4 modular base and MP5 modular base. When printing, you can choose wether you'd like to print the Mp5 base or the M4 base. 

Key Features:
Swappable bottom base – Choose between M4 or MP5 mag compatibility.
BB stopper
Adjustable shim system: Customize how snug the adapter fits against your nozzle.

Note: Airsoft guns shown in photos/videos are not included – they’re only for demonstration purposes.
Do not exceed 130 PSI with this adapter.

This adapter is the result of extensive real-world testing and multiple design iterations & complete redesigns, refined to ensure consistent feeding, proper sealing, and long-term durability. 

This adapter was designed by me, inspired by many other adapters on the market – but refined over multiple design iterations and months of prototyping. It’s been thoroughly tested to ensure reliable and consistent performance. Absolutely no AI has been used to design this adapter - this is all manually calibrated and designed by me. 

This adapter must be printed using tough, functional materials.
 Weak filament or standard brittle resin will fail.
Due to the nature of 3D printing, material choice, printer calibration, and assembly methods, I make no guarantees regarding strength, durability, or safety.
By purchasing and using this file, you acknowledge that you are using it entirely at your own risk.
The designer assumes no responsibility or liability for any damage, malfunction, injury, or loss resulting from the use, misuse, or inability to use this file or any printed parts produced from it.
This adapter was primarily designed and tested around resin printing.
 FDM printing may work, but it has not been fully validated and performance cannot be guaranteed.
Before proceeding with this you need to calibrate your 3d printer settings.

UPDATE:
Added an M4 adapter base that is better designed for specifically the WE m4 platform. It is only cosmetically designed in a way for the adapter base to be more flush with the lower receiver. This is only for the WE m4 platform and not for the 416. If you have the 416, please print the file "M4 Base/m4adapterbase.stl" instead.
details:
🖨️ Recommended Printing Method
I printed and tested this adapter using:
Resin printing


0.05 mm layer height


Design optimized for resin-level detail and tolerances


Because resin is naturally brittle, different parts must be printed in different materials based on mechanical stress.

🧪 Recommended Materials (Resin Printing)
If you are using resin only, use the following material setup:
Main HPA adapter body: ABS-like resin


Adapter base (M4 / MP5): ABS-like resin


Feed lips: Nylon-like resin (highly recommended – under constant stress)


Mag catch: PC-like resin
 (ABS-like will flex and fatigue over time under spring tension)


Pins: PC-like resin


Valve extension: ABS-like resin


Shims: ABS-like resin


Gas router: Elastic resin (~50A shore hardness)


BB feed: ABS-like resin


BB stopper: ABS-like resin


Feed lips and mag catch are the most stressed components.
 Do not print them in standard or brittle resin.

🧵 Hardware & Additional Parts Required
You will also need the following non-printed parts:
Output Valve
The adapter may work with a stock WE M4 valve, however it is designed around this valve:
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005002770947507.html?spm=a2g0o.order_list.order_list_main.5.246c1802u7hAZT

Input Valve
22-2 Outer, 1/8 NPT
https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005007551310123.html?spm=a2g0o.order_list.order_list_main.10.246c1802u7hAZT
Threaded Inserts
Top of adapter (feed lips + shims):
M3 threaded inserts


5 mm outer diameter


4 mm length


Bottom of adapter (modular base):
M6 threaded insert


9 mm outer diameter


8 mm length


Installation requires a soldering iron to heat-set the inserts.

Screws
M6 screw to attach the bottom base to the adapter.
M3 screws to attach feed lips and shims to the adapter




2 Springs are needed. I suggest buying a spring box set from your local store and using tiny springs, or you can get springs from pencils. 
☀️ Post-Processing (Resin Prints)
If printing in resin, I strongly recommend UV protection to prevent long-term brittleness and over-curing.

🛠 Printing & Assembly Instructions

1. Printing the parts
Print all parts using appropriate materials for each component.
If using resin printing, follow the material recommendations listed above for each specific part.


If using FDM, you may be able to print most parts in a single tough filament, and a rubber-like filament for the gas router.


If you cannot print flexible material, an original gas router should work.


After printing:
Resin: Wash and fully cure all parts.


FDM: Cleaning and curing is not required.



2. Initial pressure test (before full assembly)
Before assembling the adapter, it is strongly recommended to perform an initial pressure test.
Install the input and output valves only.


Lightly lubricate the O-rings and the threads of the valves.


Do NOT lubricate the adapter threads. Excess lubricant can weaken resin over time.


Once installed, pressure test the adapter.
If it leaks or fails, stop and correct the issue before proceeding.


If it passes, depressurize and continue.



3. Installing threaded inserts
Prepare a soldering iron for installing the threaded inserts.
Inserts are required at:
Top of the adapter (feed lips)


Bottom of the adapter (modular base)


Sides of the adapter (shims)


Optional but recommended:
 Apply a small amount of glue on the inserts for extra security.
Heat-set the inserts carefully into the adapter.
If you cannot use threaded inserts, parts can be glued together instead (feed lips, modular base, shims).
 Note: the adapter is designed for inserts, gluing is only a budget workaround.

4. Feed lips & valve extension
Install the gas router into the feed lips.


Screw the feed lips onto the top of the adapter.


Install the original shim onto the adapter.


Insert the valve extension into the adapter.
The letter “W” must face the output valve.


Insert the valve extension pin to secure it.


Test the movement:
Press the extension in — it should return smoothly on release.


Now pressure test again.
If it leaks:
Remove the pin


Lightly file material from the “W” area


Reinstall and retest


If the extension does not return:
Apply a very small amount of lubricant


If still stuck, your print tolerances are likely incorrect.


Only proceed once the adapter is sealed and moving correctly.

5. Fitment test
Insert the adapter into your GBBR.
If the fit is too tight or it does not seat fully, install shorter shims.


Test the adapter by firing the gun.
Once confirmed functional, continue.

6. Modular base assembly
You will need two springs:
one for the BB stopper


one for the mag catch


BB feed & stopper
This is the most tedious step. Be patient.
Insert the BB feed part into the modular base.


Make sure it is fully seated (side holes must line up).


Insert the spring into the BB stopper.


Insert the BB stopper into the BB feed.


Press down and align holes.


Insert the BB stopper pin.


Test:
Press and release the stopper.


It must return freely.


If not, remove the pin and realign the spring

Mag catch
Place the spring into the modular base.


Align the mag catch.


Press it down and insert the mag catch pin.


Wiggle slightly if needed.


Test with an AEG magazine:
It should lock in and release correctly.



7. Final assembly
Attach the modular base to the adapter using the M6 screw from the bottom.
Tighten fully.


The screw must be flush with the BB feed.


It must not protrude, or magazines may not insert.



Your HPA adapter is now assembled and ready for use.

name: RA3 Rotary Protractor + Centering Spacers for xTool F2 Ultra UV and F2 Ultra MOPA
description:
If you do rotary engraving with the RA3, you’ve probably spent more time than you’d like guessing alignment, wasting blanks, or running test frames just to see if a wrap will actually close.

This set was designed to remove that guesswork.

Included are two versions of spacer blocks to accurately centre the RA3 chuck in the machine, along with dedicated rotary protractor. The protractor lets you physically see degrees of rotation so you can confirm positioning before you engrave, not after.

This is especially useful when:
You’re engraving bespoke items that already have existing artwork
You need to place a design exactly 180° opposite a mug handle
You want to confirm a wrap will go full circumference without burning a test piece
You want repeatable, measurable rotary setups instead of “close enough”

Also included is the SVG file for engraving the degree increments directly onto the protractor, so you can laser-mark it for long-term use and clear visibility.

What’s included

Protractor design (2 variants)

RA3 centring spacer blocks

SVG file for engraving degree markings

Files optimised for easy 3D printing

Why it’s paid

These files come from real-world testing and a fair bit of design time aimed at reducing wasted materials and setup frustration. Pricing is simply to help recoup some of that time while making the files available to others who’ll get practical use from them.

Designed and tested with the RA3 on the F2 Ultra, but useful anywhere accurate rotary alignment matters.

If you have suggestions or improvements, feel free to reach out. This came from solving a problem I kept running into myself.
details:

Manufacturing method

FDM (FFF) 3D printing

Recommended materials

PLA (easy, stable, perfectly suitable for workshop use)

PETG (recommended if the tool will live near heat or in a shed)

ABS optional, but not required

Layer height

0.2 mm recommended

0.28 mm acceptable for faster prints

Finer layers offer no functional benefit for this part

Infill

20–30% gyroid or grid

Higher infill offers no measurable accuracy gain

Walls / perimeters

3–4 perimeters recommended

Supports

None required

Build orientation

Print flat on the bed as supplied

Tolerance & accuracy

Designed to rely on machine geometry, not flex

No post-scaling required

Print at 100% scale

A matte filament finish improves engraving contrast

Optional: light sanding on the engraving face before laser marking

Spacer blocks are designed to be used as-is.

This Swedish chuck (Longworth chuck) is a sophisticated, practical solution for woodturners who value maximum holding power, precise centering and easy handling. Developed as a 2D milling template for the front and back plate, this system combines classic turning technology with modern production and durable materials.

Diameter of the chuck 430mm

The principle of the cams running against each other means that the workpiece is automatically centered when turning. This makes the Swedish chuck ideal for reworking almost finished shells, especially for fine-cutting parting off and cleanly turning out the base.

The front and rear panels are made of multiplex, screen printing or MDF and have a recommended material thickness of approx. 16-21 mm to ensure optimum function and rigidity. The clamping pins made of TPU and PETG ensure a secure hold, high friction and gentle contact with the workpiece.

The clamping range can be adjusted easily and evenly thanks to the friction-angle-optimized cams. Clamping is done without tools using wing nuts, quickly, conveniently and reliably.

Assembly & compatibility:
Can be clamped in any conventional lathe chuck
Can also be mounted directly on a face plate
Self-centring thanks to the cam disc principle
Maximum holding force with gentle clamping


Special advantages:

Ideal for finishing bowl bottoms

Cost-effective thanks to in-house production

Proven Longworth principle in modern implementation

name: AE86 lower passenger vent
description:
**LHD & RHD files included!**

This is the passenger side dashboard vent for a Toyota AE86 (the single aim-able vent on the passenger side).

It is modeled off the factory vent and retains the up/down and left/right direction controls and can be rotated closed as per factory

As the functional vent can be a little tricky to post process and put together, i've also included a non-functional vent model (will still allow up/down movement, but does away with the left/right adjustment), especially got if you're just looking to fill the gap in your drift car dashboard
details:
Recommended print settings:

    ABS/ACA (vapor smoothing is recommended if you're after a factory look) or PETG
        0.1mm layer height
        Supports required, brim recommended

Post processing required to get functional vents to articulate

For a fully adjustable vent, print out:
* 1 x outer frame
* 1 x inner frame
* 1 x centre flap
* 1 x Left flap
* 1 x right flap
* 1 x drag link

If printing the non-functional vents, just print out 
* 1 x outer frame
* 1 x inner frame 
and slap together

Files are in correct orientation for printing, clean up supports & brim, pay careful attention to the pivots on the flaps, do any vapor smoothing now.

Insert the centre flap into the case 1st, followed by the left and right flaps, check they all rotate freely.
align all the flaps, then carefully insert the draglink over the smaller pivots (don't press too hard as the small pivots are rather delicate), do a little extra sanding on the pivots until they will press into the draglink.

Spin the flap assembly gently by hand a few times until they move freely, then insert the inner frame into the outer frame.

Make sure you can fully close and open the flaps using only the thumb control before installing onto the dashboard.

The whole thing just presses into the dash as per the factory vent

If you have a brown/maroon dash, the Sunlu 'Roasted Chestnut' ABS is a fair approximation of the factory colour.

Please let me know if you have a good filament option for the factory blue dash!
