name: 6-Slot Clipper Guard Storage Box | Magnetic Barber Guard Organizer Case
description:
6-Slot Clipper Guard Storage Box

A compact storage case designed to keep clipper guards organized, protected, and easy to access.

This model holds up to 6 clipper guards in individual slots, helping prevent them from being scattered around the barber station or mixed together inside a drawer or tool bag.

The box features a clean geometric exterior with a magnetic closing system. Open the lid and all 6 guards are clearly visible and easy to remove.

The compact enclosed design also makes it suitable for carrying clipper guards between workstations, barber shops, events, or mobile barber setups.

FEATURES

• Holds up to 6 clipper guards
• Individual storage slots
• Magnetic lid closure
• Easy to open and close
• Quick access to each guard
• Compact and portable
• Keeps the barber station clean and organized
• Modern geometric barber-style design
• Designed for FDM 3D printing

The internal layout is designed for common barber clipper guards. Please compare the dimensions of your guards before printing if you are using a different type or brand.

This is a DIGITAL DOWNLOAD only.
No physical product, clipper guards, magnets, or accessories are included.

Commercial production or resale of printed products is NOT permitted unless a separate commercial license has been obtained from the designer.
details:
HINGE ASSEMBLY

Use a short piece of 3D printer filament as the hinge pin.

Insert the filament through the hinge from both sides, then trim it flush.

Glue the small square retaining block into place inside the box. This locks the filament pins in position and hides the cut ends for a cleaner finish.

MAGNET INSTALLATION

This model requires 2 × 5×5 mm magnets.

Check the magnet polarity before gluing.

Insert the magnets into the reserved holes and secure them with a small amount of CA glue / super glue if needed.

PRINTING SETTINGS

Recommended printer:
FDM / FFF 3D printer

Recommended nozzle:
0.4 mm

Layer height:
0.20 mm recommended
0.16 mm can be used for a finer surface finish

Wall loops:
3–4 walls

Top / Bottom layers:
4–5 layers

Infill:
15–25%

Recommended materials:
PLA / PLA+ / PETG

For normal indoor barber-shop use, PLA or PLA+ works well.
PETG can be used if you want better heat resistance and durability.

SUPPORTS

The model is designed to minimize the need for supports.

Depending on your printer, orientation and slicer settings, small support areas may still be required.

Check the slicer preview before printing.

ASSEMBLY

1. Print all included parts in their recommended orientation.

2. Remove any brim or support material and clean the mating surfaces.

3. Test-fit all parts before using glue.

4. Install the magnets into the reserved magnet holes.

IMPORTANT:
Always check the magnet polarity before gluing them permanently.

5. Use a small amount of CA glue / super glue to secure the magnets if necessary.

6. After assembly, open and close the lid several times to make sure the movement is smooth.

7. Insert the clipper guards into the individual slots and check the fit.

PRINTING TIPS

• Do not use excessive elephant-foot compensation on the internal guard slots.
• If the slots feel too tight, check your printer dimensional accuracy and flow calibration.
• Different brands of clipper guards may have slightly different dimensions.
• Print the main body slowly enough to keep the outer geometric details clean.
• A clean first layer is important because several visible surfaces depend on dimensional accuracy.

Magnets and clipper guards are not included.

description:
SF Mount-style modular phone mounting system.

The complete system can be assembled without screws by using a strong, plastic-compatible super glue. I personally use ARKA Kraftprotz, and it has worked very well for me in several applications.

However, I recommend using screws whenever possible for maximum durability.

🔩 Assembly & Hardware

The design includes mounting holes for M3 screws and nuts throughout the system.

The only exception is the rails, where you will need to add the corresponding holes to the plate yourself if you want to screw them in. This is a very simple modification, and I plan to update this in a future version.

You can therefore choose between:

Glued assembly
M3 screw + nut assembly
A combination of both
📱 Setup & Customization

On my personal setup, I added:

Fabric/wrap to the folding plate
Black elastic bands
Several Velcro sections around the phone area
Velcro on the rear for adding a team/unit patch
Bungee cord for additional retention
Pull tab attached to the bungee cord for easier and faster operation

To secure the phone, you’ll need hook-and-loop (male and female Velcro), or you can simply integrate the system into a plate carrier or pouch, depending on your setup.

⚙️ Hinge Options

The included hinge is print-in-place and does not require separate hardware.

With PLA, the printed hinge works well immediately after printing. With materials such as ASA or PETG, the first movement may be quite stiff, but it should gradually become smoother after operating the hinge several times.

For increased durability, the design can also be easily adapted to use a separate, more robust hinge instead of the printed one. If you prefer not to rely on the print-in-place hinge, you can modify the mounting area to fit the hinge of your choice.

This makes it easy to upgrade the system for heavier or more demanding use.

description:
# 3D Printable Packout Compact Organizer Insert for Milwaukee M12 3404-20 + 3453-20

This is a custom-designed 3D printable insert for a very complete Milwaukee M12 compact toolkit setup. It is designed to hold not only the drill and impact driver, but also the most commonly needed drill/driver accessories in one organized Packout box.

The insert is designed specifically for:

- **Milwaukee M12 Hammer Drill/Driver 3404-20**
- **Milwaukee M12 Impact Driver 3453-20**
- **M12 CP batteries attached**
- **Milwaukee Packout Compact Organizer 48-22-8435**

Please note: this insert is model-specific. It is not guaranteed to fit other similar Milwaukee M12 drills, impact drivers, batteries, or Packout boxes.

---

## What This Insert Holds

This insert is designed as a complete compact toolkit organizer. It includes storage for:

- Milwaukee M12 Hammer Drill/Driver 3404-20 with CP battery attached
- Milwaukee M12 Impact Driver 3453-20 with CP battery attached
- Removable tray for eight 2-inch driver bits
- Two removable stackable trays for 1-inch driver bits, 9 bits per tray
- Third removable tray for loose small accessories
- Four long slots under the impact driver for 6-inch bits
- Slot for a hex adapter
- Large 30 × 185 mm deep accessory pocket

The large deep pocket can be used in two different ways:

### Option 1

Custom enclosure for the **DeWALT DW1361 21-piece drill bit kit**

### Option 2

Three stackable long trays for loose long drill bits or other long accessories

This gives the user two different accessory-storage configurations depending on their setup.

---

## Included Print Options

This model includes two print configurations:

### 1. Full One-Piece Insert

For users with a large-format printer, the main insert can be printed as one complete piece.

### 2. Split Two-Piece Insert

For smaller printers, the insert is also provided as two separate halves. This version is suitable for printers with a 256 × 256 mm build plate, such as the **Bambu Lab P1S**.

Please choose the correct file version for your printer before slicing.

---

## Included Files

The download includes files for the main insert and accessory trays, including:

- Full one-piece insert file
- Split left/right insert files
- Removable 2-inch bit tray
- Stackable 1-inch bit trays
- Loose accessory tray
- Long accessory trays
- DeWALT DW1361 drill-bit enclosure option
- Alignment/assembly parts, where applicable
- ReadMe / instructions

File formats may include STL and/or 3MF depending on the included package.

---

## Important Notes

This is a **digital 3D model file**.

No physical product, tools, bits, Packout box, or accessories are included.

This design was created for a specific tool setup and is intended for users who want a compact but complete M12 drill/driver kit with organized accessory storage.

For best results, check the fit of trays and accessory parts before final assembly. Slight printer/material differences may affect fit, especially with removable trays and sliding parts.

---

## Recommended Use

This insert is ideal for anyone who wants a compact, organized Packout setup with:

- Drill
- Impact driver
- CP batteries attached
- 1-inch bits
- 2-inch bits
- 6-inch bits
- Hex adapter
- Drill bits
- Small loose accessories

It is designed to make the Packout Compact Organizer function like a complete grab-and-go M12 drill/driver kit.

## License / Use

For personal use only unless otherwise agreed in writing.

You may print this model for your own use.

You may not resell, redistribute, share, upload, or modify and resell the digital files.

Selling printed copies is not allowed without written permission.

---

## Trademark Notice

Milwaukee, M12, Packout, DeWALT, and related product names are trademarks of their respective owners.

This is an independently designed 3D printable accessory. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by Milwaukee Tool, DeWALT, or their parent companies.

Brand names and model numbers are used only to describe compatibility.
details:
## Print Settings / Manufacturing Instructions

### Recommended Material

Recommended materials:

- **PLA+** — easiest option and suitable for most users
- **PETG** — good option if the insert will be used in a hot garage, car, or work vehicle
- **PLA** — usable, but PLA+ is preferred for better toughness

For most users, **PLA+ is recommended** because it prints cleanly, has good strength, and is easy to work with.

---

### Recommended Print Settings

Suggested settings for the main insert and trays:

- Layer height: **0.20 mm**
- Wall loops / perimeters: **3**
- Top layers: **4–5**
- Bottom layers: **4–5**
- Infill: **15–25%**
- Infill pattern: **Gyroid, Grid, or Cubic**
- Supports: **Not required for most parts**, depending on orientation
- Brim: **Optional**, recommended for small pins or narrow parts
- Nozzle: **0.4 mm**
- Print orientation: use the provided orientation in the 3MF files where available

For smaller removable trays and accessory parts, 0.20 mm layer height is usually sufficient. For cleaner detail, 0.16 mm may be used.

---

### Main Insert Print Options

This model includes two main print configurations:

#### 1. Full One-Piece Insert

Use this option if your printer has a large enough build plate to print the complete insert as one piece.

#### 2. Split Two-Piece Insert

Use this option for smaller printers, including printers with a **256 × 256 mm build plate**, such as the **Bambu Lab P1S**.

The split version is designed so the insert can be printed in two halves and assembled after printing.

---

### Assembly Notes for Split Version

If printing the split version:

1. Print both insert halves.
2. Print the included alignment pins, if provided.
3. Test-fit the two halves before applying adhesive.
4. Insert alignment pins into the matching holes.
5. Join the two halves together.

Adhesive is optional depending on your preference and how the insert will be used. If adhesive is used, a small amount of CA glue, epoxy, or suitable plastic adhesive may be applied at the joint.

Do not apply excessive glue near tray pockets or accessory pockets.

---

### Removable Trays

The design includes removable accessory trays.

Before final use:

1. Test-fit each tray inside the insert.
2. Remove any small strings or rough edges from the print.
3. Lightly sand tight edges if needed.
4. Make sure trays slide in and out easily before loading accessories.

Small differences in printers, filament, and slicer settings may affect fit. If a tray feels too tight, lightly sanding the sides is usually enough.

---

### DeWALT DW1361 Drill Bit Option

The large deep accessory pocket can be used with the custom enclosure designed for the **DeWALT DW1361 21-piece drill bit kit**.

This option is intended to hold the DeWALT drill bit inserts removed from the original DeWALT case and placed into the printed enclosure.

Before final assembly:

1. Test-fit the DeWALT inserts into the printed enclosure.
2. Check that the drill bits are held securely.
3. Test-fit the assembled drill bit container into the main insert pocket.

Depending on printer tolerances, light sanding may be needed for sliding or snap-fit areas.

---

### Alternative Long Tray Option

Instead of the DeWALT DW1361 drill bit enclosure, the same large deep pocket can be used with three stackable long trays for loose long drill bits or accessories.

This gives two possible configurations:

- DeWALT DW1361 drill bit container
- Stackable long accessory trays

Choose the configuration that best matches your setup.

---

### Supports

Most parts are designed to print without supports when oriented correctly.

Supports may be needed only if the user changes the orientation or modifies the model.

For best results:

- Avoid printing large flat ledges as unsupported 90-degree overhangs
- Use the provided 3MF orientation when available
- Review the sliced preview before printing

---

### Tolerance and Fit

This model includes removable and sliding parts, so printer calibration matters.

Recommended checks:

- Make sure your printer is well calibrated
- Use dry filament
- Check bed adhesion
- Review first layer quality
- Clean up small strings before assembly

Tight areas may be adjusted with light sanding or a hobby knife.

---

### Suggested Print Order

Recommended print order:

1. Accessory trays or small test parts first
2. Main insert half or full insert
3. Second insert half, if using the split version
4. Alignment pins
5. Optional DeWALT DW1361 enclosure or long trays
6. Final test fit and assembly

Printing smaller parts first is a good way to confirm filament, color, and fit before printing the main insert.

---

### Important Manufacturing Note

This is a 3D printable digital model. The final quality and fit depend on the printer, filament, slicer settings, and calibration.

No physical tools, bits, batteries, Packout organizer, or accessories are included.

name: Pain Stim ADHD Fidget
description:
I designed this based on the little ouchie one for myself to help with managing dermatillomania. The slight amount of pain from squeezing it is just enough to keep my hands occupied so I don't pick at myself, and offers a degree of stimulation and the spinny head is great for AuDHD stimming. 

Requires one skateboard bearing and electrical or honestly any plastic/ papery tape.
details:
This should be printed in two seperate goes to prevent stringing.
I printed mine on an Ender 3 V2 with 100% infill for maximum weight.

It's designed to fit a 608 skateboard bearing. The bearing just pushes into the top, you can use a mallet but I just lean mine into the floor and it fits fine. I added an access hole at the top of the head to spray Q20 into the bearing after it's been fitted for a super smooth glide.

The base has a long shaft and I suggest printing it with the bottom side down and slightly in the bed and adding a brim to allow it to print with minimal cleanup. Afterwards add a tiny piece of electric tape around the shaft (Just enough to wrap a bit over half the circumference) and fit into the ball bearing. The reason there's space for tape to be added is for easier removal should you want to replace the head at any point or access the ball bearing.

name: Russian PG-7VLT Tandem HEAT Rocket - Full & Cutaway Technical Training Aid
description:
An exceptionally detailed, highly accurate 1:1 scale replica of the PG-7VLT Tandem High-Explosive Anti-Tank (HEAT) rocket, engineered specifically for modern technical training, EOD/UXO identification, and classroom instruction.

This premium model kit includes both full external replicas and highly detailed structural cutaway versions, providing an unprecedented look into the physics and engineering of modern tandem-charge anti-armor technology.

The PG-7VLT is a specialized rocket designed to defeat vehicles protected by Explosive Reactive Armor (ERA). This 3D printable training aid meticulously recreates the critical spacing and layout of both the forward precursor charge and the main primary warhead, making it an invaluable tool for instructors demonstrating how modern infantry countermeasures defeat advanced armored hulls.

Key Features:
Dual-Version Kit: Includes the Full Assembly (ideal for field identification, load-bearing drill training, and static displays) and a Mechanical Cutaway (for internal classroom instruction on dual-stage explosives).

True Tandem Architecture: The cutaway version explicitly details the unique physical separation between the small forward precursor charge (designed to detonate ERA) and the massive main shaped charge behind it.

VP Nose Fuze Assembly: Features a multi-part, highly accurate replica of the nose fuze element, complete with realistic threading to allow complete removal from the tip of the rocket.

Stabilizer & Rocket Motor Interface: Meticulously duplicates the mid-section motor integration and the base connection designed to interface with standard rocket-propellant booster tubes.

Technical Context & Operational Logic
Introduced to provide infantry units with a viable countermeasure against modern main battle tanks equipped with reactive plating, the PG-7VLT utilizes a two-stage detonation sequence:

The Precursor Charge: Upon impact, the sensitive nose fuze instantly detonates the small forward shaped charge. This initial blast is designed specifically to trigger and clear away the target's Explosive Reactive Armor (ERA) tile without prematurely compromising the main warhead.

The Main Charge: Following a precise millisecond delay, the larger primary shaped charge detonates against the now-exposed baseline armor steel. This projects a high-velocity metallic jet capable of penetrating deep into the tank's interior.

EOD Relevance: Because of its unique, elongated multi-stage profile, the PG-7VLT is a critical target for modern UXO recognition. Training teams to identify the distinct shape of tandem munitions is vital for safe handling and disposal procedures in modern combat theaters.

name: Chinese Type 63 107mm Rocket with MJ-1 Fuze - Full & Cutaway Technical Training Aid / Inert Replica
description:
An incredibly detailed, highly accurate 1:1 scale replica of the iconic Chinese Type 63 107mm artillery rocket equipped with the MJ-1 nose fuze, engineered specifically for technical training, EOD/UXO instruction, and historical military displays.

Comes with Textured Grain HE BP and Rocket Fuel or Simple. Complex and Simple MJ-1 Fuze added

This premium model kit includes both full external replicas and highly detailed structural cutaway versions, providing an unparalleled look into one of the most widely proliferated rocket systems in modern history.

Known for its simplicity, reliability, and devastating effectiveness, the Type 63 rocket has been utilized in global conflicts for decades. This 3D printable kit meticulously recreates the internal and external geometry of the ordnance, allowing instructors to demonstrate its mechanical design, ignition system, and aerodynamic features safely in a classroom environment.

Key Features:
Dual-Version Kit: Includes both the Full Solid Assembly (for field identification and deployment handling training) and a Mechanical Cutaway (for internal classroom instruction).

Detailed MJ-1 Fuze Architecture: Features a highly accurate, multi-part replica of the MJ-1 nose fuze. The cutaway version exposes the internal striking pin, booster pellets, and the true mechanical threads allowing the fuze to be entirely unthreaded from the warhead body.

Internal Rocket Motor Geometry: The cutaway version exposes the interior of the combustion chamber, displaying the configuration of the solid propellant grain geometry and the electrical igniter positioning.

Canted Nozzle Base Plate: Meticulously duplicates the base plate featuring the iconic canted (angled) rocket nozzles. These nozzles spin-stabilize the rocket in flight, eliminating the need for folding fins.

Historical Context & Combat Service
First introduced in the early 1960s by the People's Republic of China, the Type 63 107mm rocket system became the "AK-47 of the artillery world." Highly portable and robust, the rockets were originally designed to be fired from a 12-tube towed launcher, but their true tactical legacy lies in their ability to be fired independently from improvised launchers, dirt berms, or even crude wooden troughs.

The Soviet-Afghan War: The rocket saw massive proliferation during the 1980s when it was supplied in vast numbers to the Mujahideen. Its light weight allowed insurgent forces to transport the ordnance through rugged mountain passes on pack animals, launching devastating hit-and-run attacks against static Soviet installations.

Iraq and the Post-2003 Era: Following the 2003 coalition invasion, the 107mm rocket became one of the most frequent indirect-fire threats faced by multinational forces in Iraq. Insurgent groups heavily utilized them for improvised, timer-delayed attacks against Forward Operating Bases (FOBs) and the Baghdad Green Zone due to their ease of concealment and rapid setup.

Global Proliferation: Beyond Afghanistan and Iraq, variations of the Type 63 rocket (including Iranian, Sudanese, and North Korean copies) have been recovered in conflict zones across Africa, the Middle East, and Southeast Asia, making it a critical item for modern EOD recognition and UXO clearance training.

⚠️ DISCLAIMER
This is an inert, non-functional training aid. It contains no energetic materials, no pyrotechnics, and no functioning electronics. It cannot be made functional and is intended strictly for display, educational, and simulation use only.

🛑 FILE USE POLICY
You may not sell, redistribute, or modify these files for resale. For commercial licensing or custom development, contact:
📩 RedwireSolutions.info@gmail.com

name: Pige de Calage d'Allumage Moteur
description:
Cet outil est conçu pour régler précisément l’avance à l’allumage sur les moteurs anciens deux-temps (Peugeot 103, MBK 51, Motobécane, Solex et bien d'autres). Initialement créé pour mes propres besoins, je l’ai perfectionné pour qu’il soit le plus pratique, robuste et précis possible.

Grâce au pas de vis M12x1 de la partie supérieure, le fonctionnement est d'une simplicité absolue : 1 tour de vis = 1 mm d'avance a l'allumage.


###  Contenu du téléchargement :
- Fichiers STEP : Les deux pièces au format STEP si vous souhaitez adapter l’alésage central en fonction de votre pige ou des tolérances de votre imprimante (conçu initialement à Ø4,45 mm pour un axe de 4 mm).
- Fichiers STL : Prêts à être glissés dans votre slicer.
- Fichier 3MF (Bambu Studio) : Profil d'impression pré-configuré pour un résultat parfait.

###  Matériel nécessaire :
Une pige de 4 mm : Vous pouvez utiliser un foret de 4 mm , une clé Allen, ou un gros clou. Ou n'importe quelle axe compris entre 3 et 8mm  (Le modèle est modifiable jusqu'à 8 mm via le fichier STEP si besoin).
Une vis M6 (longueur minimale de 20 mm).

---

###  Notice d’utilisation :
1.  -  Préparation : Démontez votre bougie. Vissez la partie basse de l’outil à la main puis bloquez-la légèrement dans le puits de bougie à l'aide d'une clé à bougie de 21 mm (filetage standard M14 x 1.25).
2.  - Trouver le PMH : Placez votre pige dans le perçage central. Faites tourner votre vilebrequin à la main pour trouver le Point Mort Haut (PMH)  (le moment où la pige est au plus haut, juste avant que le piston ne redescende).
3.  - Mise à zéro : Vissez la partie supérieure de l’outil de quelques tours pour aligner le "0" en face du repère visuel, puis bloquez la pige avec la vis M6.
4.  - Réglage de l'avance : Faites tourner votre moteur de quelques degrés dans le sens inverse de son fonctionnement. 
5.  - Mesure : Vissez la partie supérieure du nombre de tours correspondant à l'avance souhaitée. (Exemple : pour 2 mm d'avance, vissez de exactement 2 tours complets, chaque graduations représentent 0.1mm).
6.  - Calage : Tournez le moteur dans son sens de marche normal jusqu’à ce que le piston vienne en butée contre la pige. Votre moteur est positionné pile à 2 mm avant le PMH. Il ne vous reste plus qu'à caler votre rotor/volant moteur sur son point d'allumage !
details:
### ⚙️ Paramètres d’impression recommandés :
- Le fichier 3MF est fourni avec ces paramètres optimisés :
- Matériau : PETG fortement recommandé pour une meilleure résistance mécanique et thermique.
- Hauteur de couche : 0.16 mm ( pour la précision et la qualité des filetages).
- Parois (Walls) : Augmenté à 3 ou 4 pour garantir la solidité des filetages sous contrainte.
-Remplissage : Au moins 40% pour la solidité, principalement pour la parte qui vient se visser sur la culasse.
- Supports : Activer les supports uniquement sur la zone en porte-à-faux qui vient en appui sur la culasse. Le reste s'imprime sans supports.
- information : Environ 1h40 d'impression sur Bambu Lab P1S pour seulement ~18g de filament.

name: Skadis Modular Storage Organizer | Storage Box
description:
**Skadis Modular Storage Organizer | Storage Box** is a compact and customizable storage system for your **IKEA Skadis board**. Thanks to its modular design, you can build any tower height you need. Perfect for storing **screws, nuts, washers, hardware parts, electronics components, craft items, office supplies or even jewelry** 🔧. A clean, flexible way to keep all your small items organized. ✨

- **Modular design** – Build your storage tower as tall as you want. Each module adds **two boxes**.
- **Left & right opening profiles** – Choose between left-opening or right-opening boxes. Perfect for placing **two rows side-by-side**.
  - **Scadis-Storage_Tower-Left** - left-opening boxes
  - **Scadis-Storage_Tower-Right** - right-opening boxes
- **Label or no-label box option** 🔑 – Select boxes with labels (**03_Box**) for quick organization or without labels (**03_Box-Without_Label**) for a clean look. *(Both variants can always be found in the print profile or in stl files)*
- **Box size: 89 × 55 mm** 📦
- **Easy assembly** 🔧 – No glue needed. Everything simply **screws together** for a solid build.
- **Optional box divider** – Use the included **09_Box_Partition** to divide a box into **two separate compartments** for even better organization.

🔧 **How to Build the Main Tier**

1. Choose from two print profiles - Left/Right (L/R)
2. **Start with 01_Base (L/R)** – this is always the foundation of your tower.
3. Begin stacking: place **03_Box (L/R)** on the base, then add **04_Partition** on top of it. 03_Partition **has a small latch that needs to be inserted** into the rectangular cutouts in 01_Base.
4. Place 03_Box (L/R) on **04_Partition**
5. Insert **06_Pivot** through the center and **screw it into the base** to lock the whole tier together 🔩.
6. Place **05_Roof(L/R)** on the very top.
7. Finish by attaching **07_Plug** – screw it onto the Pivot to secure the entire organizer. I recommend tightening the **07_Plug** slightly to eliminate the clearance between the **03_Box(L/R)** parts — this prevents the boxes from opening on their own.

🔧 **How to Add a Second Tier and Other...**

1. Instead of 01_Base, print **02_Base_Modular (L/R)** for the next level!! (01_Base_Modular has a hole instead of a thread!)
2. Place **02_Base_Modular** directly on top of your completed first tier.
3. For each additional tier, print again:
  - 2× **03_Box (L/R)**
  - 1× **04_Partition**
  - 1× **06_Pivot**
4. Build it the same way as the main tier and close it with **05_Roof + 07_Plug** on top.

---

description:
D3P BOTTOM RISER FOR CREALITY SPARKX i7 by Darren 3d Print

NOTE - Model is for the bottom riser only - the overhead is available as a separate model. Both models can be used separately or together.

To find out more about the SparkX i7 D3P overhead mount click here on this link: https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/creality-sparkx-i7-d3p-overhead-mount

D3P overhead mount for the SparkX i7

I have been asked about designing bottom risers for some time. I wanted to make it worthwhile to print. I had my checklist and held off until I could check them all off. I believe this design should offer an interesting and worthwhile addition to your printer.

Find out more here: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BRP7ik6L2w8


FEATURES

Features of the SparkX i7 D3P bottom riser system:

• Integrated poop chute and deflector that directs all the poop into the drawer;

• Poop drawer featuring a unique bottom cutout to allow easy poop disposal without having to remove the drawer. I even added a "poop pan" that is held in place when not in use;

• An innovative LED channel that is integrated into the side of the printer for a COB LED. The LED light shines through the side of the riser and gives a cool glow effect. The color is dependent on the color of filament you choose for the highlight accent. You customize the color by changing the color of the filament or the LED. You can also widen the accent to further personalize the design.

• An innovative build plate holder for up to 2 build plates. The system features a lever which holds the build plate in a staggered configuration. The builds plates are held in place by magnets and stay in position on the lever when pulled out or pushed in;

• Two drawers with my own custom gridfinity style base. These are the same I use in all my risers so you can use any of my custom drawer inserts to customize your drawers to your liking;

• Stay in place drawers - The drawers feature magnets to hold them in place so no sliding out while printing;

• Maximum interior space - the design of the bottom riser was carefully done to maximize interior drawer space;

• Sturdiness and filament efficiency - the design minimizes filament use while maintaining structural strength;

• Modular integration with the SparkX i7 D3P overhead mount. The SparkX i7 D3P bottom riser is interchangeable and can be used with my SparkX i7 D3P overhead mount system;

• Custom drawer inserts - I have added custom drawer inserts for the drawers that can be downloaded for free (see the Addons section below);

• Detailed pdf instructions with pictures and steps;

• Printing requires little or no support.

EXTERNAL COMPONENTS

The following external components are optionally required. Links and further details are provided in the assembly instruction pdf:

1x - 8 mm wide, 2-meter-long COB LED - 5 V;
1x - 5v External power supply for the COB LED;
15 x - 10 mm x 3 mm Neodymium round magnets;
1x - Non-skid rubber pads (Optional);


INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

You are prohibited from sharing, sub-licensing, selling, renting, hosting, transferring, reproducing or distributing the digital file or 3d printed versions of this object, as well as any other derivative work in either digital or physical form (including remixes or copying/reproducing the design by any means).you are not allowed to use the objects in any manner that involves charging money or collecting fees without permission.

ADD-ONS

Coming soon


I will be adding to these so be sure to check back from time to time.

TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS

For the bottom riser (approximates):

Footprint: The footprint of the base riser is the almost the same as the printer. No extra rear or side space is required.

PRINT SETTINGS

name: Audi Honeycomb Grille Removable License Plate Holder
description:
Supporto portatarga rimovibile per griglie Audi a nido d'ape.

Il supporto si attacca dietro la targa con biadesivo ad alta tenuta. La parte ad anello va stampata in TPU o in un materiale flessibile: si comprime leggermente per entrare nella griglia e, una volta rilasciata, rimane incastrata all'interno della maglia.

Pensato per griglie Audi in stile honeycomb / nido d'ape, dai modelli S3 fino a R8 e modelli con griglia compatibile. Verificare sempre le dimensioni della propria griglia prima dell'uso definitivo.

Guida all'installazione:
Step 1 - Pulire accuratamente il retro della targa.
Step 2 - Applicare il biadesivo sulla parte piatta del supporto.
Step 3 - Scegliere la posizione corretta sulla griglia in base a dove si vuole posizionare la targa.
Step 4 - Incollare il supporto dietro la targa e premere bene per far aderire il biadesivo.
Step 5 - Comprimere leggermente l'anello flessibile e inserirlo nella griglia.
Step 6 - Rilasciare il supporto: il TPU tornera' in forma e restera' incastrato. Per rimuoverlo, schiacciare di nuovo l'anello e sfilarlo.

---

Removable license plate holder for Audi honeycomb grilles.

The holder is attached to the back of the license plate with strong double-sided tape. The loop must be printed in TPU or another flexible material: it can be compressed slightly to fit into the grille and, once released, it locks inside the honeycomb opening.

Designed for Audi honeycomb-style grilles, from S3 up to R8 and other compatible Audi grilles. Always check the dimensions of your grille before final use.

Installation guide:
Step 1 - Carefully clean the back of the license plate.
Step 2 - Apply double-sided tape to the flat side of the holder.
Step 3 - Choose the correct position on the grille depending on where you want the plate to sit.
Step 4 - Stick the holder to the back of the plate and press firmly so the tape bonds well.
Step 5 - Slightly squeeze the flexible loop and insert it into the grille.
Step 6 - Release the holder: the TPU will return to shape and stay locked in place. To remove it, squeeze the loop again and pull it out.
details:
Materiale consigliato: TPU o altro filamento flessibile.
Usare biadesivo automobilistico ad alta tenuta.
Verificare compatibilita' e tenuta prima dell'utilizzo su strada.

Use strong automotive-grade double-sided tape.
Check fitment and holding strength before road use.

name: Mechanical Differential Assembly for RC Cars & Education
description:
High-Quality Functional Differential Gear System

This is a professionally designed mechanical differential assembly, originally modeled in CATIA. It is perfect for RC vehicle projects, educational purposes, or mechanical enthusiasts who want to understand automotive drivetrain systems.

Technical Features:

Complete Assembly: Includes sun gears, planet gears, ring gear, and pinion.

Realistic Movement: Designed with proper gear ratios and clearance for smooth operation.

Versatile Use: Ideal for 3D printing (PLA/PETG/ABS) or integration into larger CAD projects.

What You Get:

STL Files: Ready for 3D printing (high resolution).

STEP (.stp) File: Industry-standard format for easy editing in any CAD software (SolidWorks, Fusion 360, CATIA, etc.).

Organized Structure: All parts are named and oriented correctly.

Printing Tips:
I recommend using a minimum of 3-4 wall loops and 20% infill for durability. For the gears, a layer height of 0.16mm or lower will provide the smoothest motion.
details:
3D Printing & Manufacturing Instructions
Recommended Settings:

Material: PLA+, PETG, or ABS (For durability and smooth gear operation).

Layer Height: 0.16mm or 0.20mm (Lower is better for gear teeth precision).

Wall Line Count: 3 or 4 (Essential for the mechanical strength of the shafts and gears).

Infill: 20% - 30% (Gyroiod or Cubic pattern recommended for structural integrity).

Supports: Required for the main housing (case) and possibly for some gears depending on orientation.

Build Plate Adhesion: Brim is recommended for the gears to prevent warping at the edges.

Post-Processing & Assembly:

Cleaning: Remove supports carefully, especially from the gear teeth and bearing seats.

Lubrication: Use a small amount of silicone grease or PTFE lubricant on the gear contact points for a much smoother motion.

Tolerances: The model is designed with standard mechanical clearances. If parts fit too tightly, check your "Horizontal Expansion" or "Elephant Foot" settings in your slicer.

Hardware: The assembly is designed for 3D printing, but the provided STEP file allows you to modify it for real bearings or metal shafts if you prefer a hybrid build.

name: 3.00 Inch Mandrel Bend Y Cutting Jig
description:
🔧 Product Description

This jig kit is designed for securely holding and cutting 3.00" mandrel-bent tubing to create accurate Y-connections from either 90° or 180° bends. It provides a stable and repeatable setup for precise fabrication, whether using a clamp or a bandsaw.

The jig features integrated alignment pins to assist when applying clamping pressure, as well as provisions for two M6 Allen bolts when a more controlled fastening method is required—ideal for bandsaw use.

Unlike standard jigs limited to 90° cuts, this design includes three additional angle options: 45°, 60°, and 75°. These angles are measured per side, meaning the final included angle of the completed Y will be double the selected value (e.g., 45° per side results in a 90° total angle).

⚠️⚠️Only 1.5D jig will cut with material all the way round the bend using the 45 degree mark properly, smaller CLR bends will not work.⚠️⚠️

🛠️ How to Use

Creating a 90° Y:

Position the bend so that the end of the tube sits flush against the face of the jig on the side that will remain uncut. Secure the tube using either a clamp or the M6 bolts. The exposed section of the bend can then be cut using a bandsaw, ensuring the blade removes only the visible excess material.

Creating Y-connections with smaller angles (45°, 60°, 75°):

⚠️ Take extra care when working with reduced angles. As the angle decreases, less of the tube is retained within the jig, reducing overall grip. Ensure the tube is firmly secured before cutting to prevent movement or dislodging during operation.

Setting the angle:

Insert a 1.6mm filler rod or tungsten through the corresponding alignment holes
Slide the tube into the jig until it contacts the rod
The offset hole positioning ensures the correct final angle is achieved
Tighten the jig bolts securely

Once positioned, the excess material extending beyond the jig can be marked(for tracking any movement) and removed. Cutting is best performed on a bandsaw.

📏 Included CLR Options

3.00" (76.2mm) CLR – tight radius for compact routing
3.60" (91.44mm) CLR – balanced radius for general applications
3.75" (95.25mm) CLR - mid-radius for an ideal balance of flow and fitment
4.50" (114.3mm) CLR – wider radius for smoother flow

📦 Additional Parts Required

2 × M6 x 73–80mm Allen socket head bolts
2 × M6 nuts

name: Scooter Segway Max G3 - JBL Flip 4,5,6 and 7 Speaker Holder
description:
Designed specifically for the Segway Max G3, this speaker holder allows you to mount your speaker on the mast of the scooter in a secure and stylish way. With an internal diameter of 7.2 cm, it is compatible with most versions of the JBL Flip series (Flip 4, Flip 5, Flip 6 and Flip 7), as well as other cylindrical speakers of similar dimensions.

The mounting system is optimized for a 4.2 cm diameter fork, such as the one on the Segway Max G3. If your scooter is of another brand but has a mast/fork of the same size, it will also be compatible.

The design combines robust structure and honeycomb pattern, offering strength, lightness and a modern look. The ends feature circular brackets that secure the speaker and facilitate installation on the mast without the need for permanent modifications.

Features
📏 Internal dimensions: 7.2 cm diameter.

🎵 Compatibility: JBL Flip (4-7) and other similar cylindrical speakers.

🛴 Specific use: Segway Max G3, adaptable to scooters with 4.2 cm fork.

⚙️ Functional design: ventilated honeycomb structure for lightness and aesthetics.

🔒 Secure mounting: reinforced ends with fixing points.

🖤 Minimalist style: contrasting colors and clean finish.

Benefits
Take your music with you while riding your scooter.

Keep the speaker steady and protected, even on long journeys.

Design thought for 3D printing, easy to produce and customize.

Compatible with cylindrical speaker cases and accessories.
details:
Internal diameter: 7.2 cm (compatible with JBL Flip 4-7).

Total height: ~18 cm.

Wall thickness: 3-4 mm.

Perimeters: 5-6 layers recommended.

Filling: 20-40%, preferably in Giroid pattern.

Orientation: no supports required, only correct positioning of the model on the printing bed.

⚙️ Printing materials
Main body: PETG, ABS, ASA or other technical materials (PLA not recommended).

Flexible cap/fixing: TPU for better fit and vibration absorption.

🔩 Additional hardware required
12 M3 × 6 mm brass inserts

8 M3 × 14 mm Allen bolts

4 M3 × 10 mm Allen bolts

🛠️ Mounting instructions
Insert the M3 brass inserts into the provided cavities of the design.

Place the speaker inside the speaker holder and tighten the TPU cover.

Attach the assembly to the scooter mast using the Allen bolts according to the indicated layout.

Check that the speaker is tight and free of play before using the scooter.

⚠️ Safety notes
Do not use with speakers larger than 7.2 cm in diameter.

Periodically check the tightness of the bolts to avoid vibrations.

Avoid prolonged exposure to the sun if printed on ABS without UV treatment.

name: 60mm to 75mm Duct Adapter — Diesel Heater Step-Up | Autoterm Planar 2D | Hose Clamp Grooves | HVAC Van Camper RV
description:
The Autoterm Planar 2D outlets at 60mm. Standard flex duct starts at 75mm / 3 inch. This adapter bridges that gap — and the step-up isn't just convenient, it's the right thing to do for your heater's combustion quality.

Restricting a diesel parking heater's exhaust outlet creates backpressure that forces the combustion chamber to work against its own airflow. The result is incomplete combustion — a sooty, rich burn that deposits carbon on the glow plug, heat exchanger, and combustion chamber surfaces. That means more frequent servicing, shorter component life, and the kind of black exhaust smoke that tells you the heater is running badly. Stepping up from the Autoterm Planar 2D's 60mm outlet to a 75mm / 3 inch flex duct removes that restriction entirely. The larger orifice reduces backpressure, the heater breathes properly, combustion stays clean, and maintenance intervals stay where they should be.
This adapter makes that step-up clean and permanent — 4mm walls throughout, dual hose clamp grooves at both ends, smooth internal bore through the transition. The 15mm diameter differential produces a moderate, well-proportioned cone that handles the step-up without creating any new restriction of its own.

✅ What Makes This Different

Engineered for diesel heater applications — specifically bridges the Autoterm Planar 2D 60mm outlet to standard 75mm / 3 inch flex duct available at any hardware store
Backpressure-free step-up — the larger outlet orifice reduces exhaust restriction, protecting combustion quality and reducing carbon build-up on heater internals
4mm uniform wall thickness — structural integrity through the full transition cone under sustained hose clamp load
Dual hose clamp grooves — positive mechanical seat at both the 60mm heater outlet and the 75mm duct end; stays sealed under vibration
Smooth internal bore — no turbulence-inducing geometry through the transition; clean airflow from heater to duct
Bidirectional — works equally as intake step-up or exhaust step-up depending on your install direction
Pre-oriented for printing — open the file, slice, print; no rotation or support setup required


🔧 Application Examples

Autoterm Planar 2D exhaust outlet to 75mm / 3 inch flexible exhaust duct
Autoterm Planar 2D intake step-up to larger bore intake ducting for improved airflow
Webasto, Eberspächer, and compatible 60mm outlet diesel heaters to 75mm flex duct
Campervan and van build diesel heater ducting — exhaust and intake circuits
RV and boat diesel heater installations where 60mm outlet meets 75mm duct infrastructure
Any diesel parking heater install where outlet restriction is causing combustion or sooting issues

📦 What's Included
1× STL file — 60mm → 75mm duct adapter, 4mm walls, hose clamp grooves, smooth internal bore, pre-oriented, no supports required.
details:
⚠️ Material Selection — Read This First
Material choice for this adapter depends entirely on where in the heater circuit it is installed.
Intake side — the intake duct sees ambient or slightly elevated temperatures only. PETG, ASA, or ABS are all appropriate. PETG for most installs; ASA for outdoor or UV-exposed intake routing; ABS where chemical resistance or higher ambient temperature is a factor.
Exhaust side — diesel heater exhaust ducting carries hot combustion gases and can reach temperatures that will soften or deform standard FDM materials over time. For exhaust applications, Nylon (PA) or Polycarbonate (PC) are the correct material choices. PETG, ASA, and ABS are not suitable for exhaust-side use on diesel heater installations. Do not use PLA under any conditions in a diesel heater duct circuit.
Print with whichever material suits your specific install location. If in doubt, use PC — it handles the full temperature range of both sides.

🖨️ Print Settings — Read This Before You Slice
Shell geometry, moderate cone — standard high-wall-count strategy applies.
Use a 0.2mm layer height, full wall count, 5–6 top/bottom layers, 100% infill. Orient large-end-down — 75mm end on the plate, no supports required. For Nylon and PC specifically: dry your filament thoroughly before printing, use an enclosure, and follow your specific filament manufacturer's temperature and bed adhesion recommendations. Both materials reward careful print preparation.

name: Shake it - Magnetic Vibration Add-on for Joint-O-Mator
description:
Shake it – Magnetic Vibration Add-on for Joint-O-Mator

Stop tapping. Start shaking. The Shake it is a heavy-duty, motorized vibration module designed exclusively for the Joint-O-Mator ecosystem. If you are running high-volume pre-roll batches, manual tapping is inconsistent and wastes time. This module automates the settling process, packing your material evenly and densely into every single cone in seconds.

Because it is fully battery-powered, your entire knockbox system remains 100% portable. You can run commercial batches anywhere without being tethered to a wall outlet. This is the universal power unit for your knockbox—whether you are running the compact Joint-O-Mator 37 or scaling up to the massive 271, the Shake it handles them all.

🧲 Universal Magnetic Coupling

The Shake it module is built around the same polarity-guided magnetic core as the Joint-O-Mator itself.

It does not require clamps or straps to attach to your knockbox. You simply drop it onto the Lid (Part D) of any compatible Joint-O-Mator. The embedded neodymium magnets instantly grab hold, dead-centering the module and locking it down tight enough to transfer heavy vibration through the entire solid base assembly below.

Compatibility:
	•	Works with all current-gen Joint-O-Mator sizes: 37 / 61 / 85 / 127 / 169 / 217 / 271

⚙️ The Assembly: Print-in-Place Hardware

This module is built to withstand aggressive vibration without shaking its own fasteners loose. To achieve this, hex nuts are embedded directly inside the plastic during the printing process.

	•	Part A (Motor Housing): You will schedule a pause to drop 4x M6 hex nuts directly into the print. Once sealed, these provide indestructible threads to mount the heavy SL-3650C motor using four M6x15 hex bolts.

	•	Part B (Cover / Shell): A second pause allows you to embed 2x M4 hex nuts, which are later used to secure the cover to the base using two M4x15 socket head screws.

	•	Part C (Battery Mount Plate): This flat plate is glued (via CA glue / superglue) directly to the bottom of the 8x AA battery case. It houses the top-facing magnets, allowing the battery pack to snap magnetically onto the top of the Shake it module.


🛒 Complete Hardware Bill of Materials (BOM)

To complete this build, you will need to source the following components:

Plug & Play Electronics:

	•	1x SL-3650C Vibration Motor (12V)
	•	1x 8-Slot AA Battery Case (12V)
	•	Note: Ensure both the motor and battery case use the standard 5.5 x 2.1mm DC barrel connector. They plug directly into each other—no soldering or wiring required.

Magnetic Core:

	•	20x Round neodymium magnets (8x3 mm) (Embedded during print; see visual polarity guide)

Fasteners (Metal Hardware):
	
	•	4x M6x15 Hex Bolts (To secure the motor) with hex nuts
	•	2x M4x15 Socket Head Screws (To secure the cover) with hex nuts

Other:
	•	CA Glue / Superglue (To attach Part C to the battery 
case)

With this purchase you only receive the print files for the Shake it add-on; all Joint-O-Mator knockboxes must be purchased separately.

Extrusion & Slicer Settings: This part houses a heavy motor and handles violent, constant vibration. Do not compromise on structural integrity. Use these minimum settings:

	•	0.8 mm nozzle (Optimal): 4 wall loops / perimeters, 25% Gyroid infill.

name: Joint-O-Mator 85 - Professional Magnetic King Size Cone Knockbox
description:
Joint-O-Mator 85 – Professional Magnetic King Size Cone Knockbox

Designed for professional users and high-volume pre-roll production. The Joint-O-Mator 85 is a heavily engineered batch cone filler built for scale, consistency, and a zero-friction workflow. This is not a flimsy stacking toy—it is a tightly integrated 5-part system built around an ultra-tight mechanical friction fit and a highly modular, polarity-guided magnetic core.


The Joint-O-Mator Ecosystem comes in 7 capacities: 
37 · 61 · 85 · 127 · 169 · 217 · 271 


⚙️ The Foundation: Ultra-Tight Friction Fit (Parts A, B & C)

The structural integrity of the main body does not rely on magnets. Instead, the core assembly is mechanically locked:

	•	Part A (The Honeycomb Tray): Holds 85 King Size cones.

	•	Part B (The TPU Damping Ring): Absorbs vibration shock and stops the unit from walking across your table.

	•	Part C (The Outer Hex Frame): The rigid exoskeleton.

When you slide Parts A, B, and C together, the tight tolerances create a permanent friction fit. They become a single, rock-solid block capable of handling heavy vibration without rattling apart. No screws, no glue, no play.


🧲 Modular Magnetic Interaction: Parts D & E

While the base is mechanically locked, the interaction with the knockbox is entirely magnetic. During slicing, you will schedule pauses to drop 8x3 mm neodymium magnets directly into the print. The polarity is strictly mapped so that parts will only snap together in the correct orientation.

The modularity of Part D (Lid / Base Plate) & Part E (Magnetic Insert): Both parts can be magnetically attached to either the top or the bottom of the solid A/B/C base, depending on your current workflow step.

	•	Manual Filling / Tapping Mode: Snap the Lid (Part D) to the top to prevent material from spilling while manually tapping the unit. Alternatively, snap it to the bottom to act as a solid base.

	•	Press-Fill Mode: Snap Part E magnetically under the Lid (Part D), then attach both to the top. As you push down slightly, Part E applies uniform downward pressure to manually pack and settle the material evenly across all 85 holes.

	•	Ejector Mode: Once filling is done, remove the Lid and snap Part E under the solid A/B/C base block. The perfectly aligned geometry pushes the entire batch of cones approximately 15 mm upward simultaneously. You get clean, tool-free extraction without crushing or individually digging out a single joint.


⚡ The “Shake it” Vibration Add-on (Sold Separately)
Manual tapping is obsolete in a production environment. The Shake it is an independent, heavy-duty magnetic vibration module powered by a 3650 motor and an 8x AA battery pack. Because it is fully battery-operated, your entire knockbox system remains 100% portable—no wall outlets or restrictive cables tying you to a desk.

Thanks to the universal magnetic layout, the Shake it snaps dead-center onto the lid (Part D) of any Joint-O-Mator size from 37 up to 271. Turn it on, and it violently but evenly shakes the solid A/B/C base to pack your cones perfectly in seconds.

https://cults3d.com/de/modell-3d/werkzeuge/shake-it-magnetic-vibration-add-on-for-joint-o-mator

🖨️ Technical Print Specifications

Build Volume Requirements:

	•	Sizes 37 / 61 / 85 / 127: Fit comfortably on any standard 256 x 256 mm bed (e.g., Bambu Lab X1C / P1S / A1).

	•	Sizes 169 / 217 / 271: Require a large-format printer with a minimum true build plate of 320 x 320 mm (e.g., Bambu H2D/H2S, Voron 2.4 350, Prusa XL).

🛒 Hardware Bill of Materials (BOM)

You will need standard 8x3 mm round neodymium magnets. A visual polarity guide is included in the project files.

	•	Joint-O-Mator 37 / 61 / 85 / 127: Requires 27x magnets total.

	•	Joint-O-Mator 169 / 217 / 271: Requires 45x magnets total.

	•	(If building the Shake it module: Requires an additional 20x magnets).

description:
Ein stilvoller und funktionaler Mod für Ihre Kaffeestation! Bei diesem 3D-Modell handelt es sich um einen Gewindeadapter, mit dem Sie eine handelsübliche Illy-Kaffee-Dose umfunktionieren und als einzigartigen, auffälligen Bohnenbehälter für Ihre Mühle verwenden können. Das ist eine tolle Möglichkeit, schöne leere Dosen upzucyclen und Ihrer Ausrüstung einen individuellen Café-Look zu verleihen.

Dieses Design ist speziell auf gängige gewerbliche Espressomühlen mit einer Einfüllöffnung von ca. 58 mm zugeschnitten. Dazu gehören die Fiorenzato-Modelle (F5, F64 Evo, F83), beliebte Nachbauten wie die Jiehui (JX-600) und viele andere OEM-Mühlen.

Abmessungen des Befestigungskegels / des Einfüllstutzens:
Der untere Teil ist leicht konisch geformt, um einen festen Reibungssitz im Einfüllstutzen der Mühle zu gewährleisten. Bitte messen Sie Ihre Mühle vor dem Drucken aus:

Außendurchmesser unten: ~57,2 mm

Außendurchmesser oben (nahe am Flansch): ~58,9 mm

Innendurchmesser der Durchgangsbohrung: 50 mm

Besonderheit (einschließlich .STEP-Datei!):
Besitzen Sie eine andere Mühle (wie beispielsweise die Mazzer Super Jolly / Mini, die einen Einlauf von ~60 mm hat)? Kein Problem! Eine .STEP-CAD-Datei (.stp) ist enthalten! Sie können den Entwurf ganz einfach in Ihre bevorzugte CAD-Software importieren und den Durchmesser des unteren Einsatzes feinabstimmen, um eine perfekte Passform für Ihre spezifische Maschine zu erzielen.

⚠️ HINWEIS ZUM DRUCKEN UND ZUM MATERIAL:
Der Motor und die Mahlscheiben der Kaffeemühle erzeugen während des Betriebs Wärme, die auf das Metallgehäuse übertragen wird.
❌ Verwenden Sie KEIN PLA-Kunststoff! Dieser verzieht sich mit der Zeit und verformt sich.

name: Toyota Avensis Switch Panel Bezel (OEM 55446-20120) - 3D Printing Restored
description:
High-quality 3D model of the interior switch panel bezel for Toyota Avensis (1997 – 2003) - OEM 55446-20120.

This model is a digital reconstruction based on a 3D scan of an original part with broken clips and mounting brackets. All mounting elements have been fully restored, ensuring a perfect fit and durability identical to or better than the original.

Printing Recommendations:
Designed to be printed in ASA or ABS to ensure necessary temperature resistance for car interiors.

If you are in Bulgaria and need this part printed: 👉 https://3dprintburgas.com

Watch the comparison video: 

https://youtube.com/shorts/kq4TTPsP1zE

Important Note on Material Shrinkage:
Please be aware that parts printed in ABS or ASA have a significant thermal expansion coefficient and tend to shrink slightly as they cool down. This may require minor manual filing or sanding of the button openings to ensure smooth operation. These dimensions were intentionally kept at nominal values (not oversized) to allow for a "Tight press fit" after post-processing.


Висококачествен 3D модел на интериорен панел (рамка за бутони) за Toyota Avensis (1997 – 2003) - OEM 55446-20120.

Този модел е дигитална реконструкция, базирана на 3D сканиране на оригинален детайл със счупени клипси и монтажни конзоли. Всички монтажни елементи са напълно възстановени, осигурявайки перфектно пасване и здравина, идентична или по-добра от оригиналната.

Препоръки за печат:
Проектиран за принтиране от ASA или ABS, за да се осигури необходимата температурна устойчивост за интериора на автомобила.

name: Einstar Rockit Protective TPU Case
description:
The Einstar Rockit is a fantastic scanner, but holding a smooth, expensive piece of plastic for a 30-minute scan can get a little sketchy—especially if your hands get sweaty or you're working in a tight space.

I designed this wrap-around TPU bumper to give the scanner some "armor" and, more importantly, to make it actually comfortable to hold. This probably won't save your device if you drop it from anywhere substantial, but it's more designed to protect it from bumps/scratches while working on scans in less than perfect conditions. I use mine often in my workshop which is dusty, dirty and everything is greasy so I like having the extra protection. 

To install/remove the scanner simply flex the case where the cutouts are and insert/remove. It will be a tight fit, that is by design. 

The Design:
Integrated Side Grips: Those vertical bumps on the sides aren't just for looks. They give your fingers a natural place to lock in, so you can maneuver the scanner at weird angles without feeling like it’s going to slide out of your hand.

Bumper Protection: 
The TPU adds a much-needed layer of shock absorption. It’ll handle the light knocks, table bumps, and "oops" moments that happen in a busy shop.

Full Access: 
I made sure the front sensor array and top interface are completely unobstructed. The fit is snug enough to stay put but flexible enough to pull on and off. It was also important to me to ensure fully usability of the 3 back buttons for quick settings adjustment. Other designs I had seen block these off and limit the use cases of the device. 

Printing Recommendations
This must be printed in TPU (95A is what I used). Don't try this in PLA or PETG; you need the flex to get the scanner inside, and the "grip" comes from the rubbery texture of the TPU.

Walls: 2 walls (helps the side grips feel firm, not mushy).

Infill: 10% Grid (provides the best "bounce" for drop protection).

Supports: Enable "Auto" Tree supports in Orca Slicer/Bambu Studio etc

Stop worrying about scratching your gear and start scanning with a better grip.

name: John Deere AL182044 Reverse Lever Repair Kit - Sticky TPU Fix & PETG Buttons
description:
This project provides a definitive solution for a common "sticky" issue found in John Deere tractors (e.g., 6000 series). The original AL182044 reverse lever features a TPU (rubber) coating that degrades over time due to hydrolysis, becoming extremely sticky and messy.

This repair method replaces the failing rubber with a combination of 3D printed PETG buttons, faux leather upholstery, and a liquid rubber finish for a result that is more durable and premium than the original part.
details:
The Repair Process (Step-by-Step)
Preparation (CRITICAL): Use a knife to completely cut away the old rubber buttons and coating down to the hard plastic frame. Do not leave any TPU residue in the button sockets, or the new 3D printed PETG buttons will not fit or actuate correctly.

Cleaning: Scrape off the remaining sticky layer with a blade, then use Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) to dissolve any residue until the plastic frame is completely clean and dry.

Surface Restoration:

Cut out the buttons down to the orange plastic. 
Important! Before applying the varnish, test the buttons to make sure they aren't sticking.

Sealing: Seal the front sections of the lever (where no upholstery is applied) with a clear coat lacquer to prevent further degradation. 
Important! Clean the surface to remove dust and grease.

Upholstery: Apply a thin layer of faux leather to the sides for a premium feel. Glue the edges of the leather into the recesses.
I recommend this glue: Pattex Universal Super Glue

Assembly: Paste the new 3D printed PETG buttons into place.

3D Printing Settings
Material: PETG (Mandatory! PLA will melt in a hot cabin, while PETG is UV and chemical resistant).

Layer height: 0.12 - 0.16 mm for a smooth fit.

Infill: 50-100% for maximum durability.

Wall lines: 3-4 walls for structural integrity.

Why this mod?
Permanent Fix: PETG and leather will not turn into "goo" like the original TPU.

Cost-Effective: Saves hundreds of dollars compared to buying a new AL182044 unit.

Superior Grip: The combination of faux leather and liquid rubber provides a much better tactile experience than the factory rubber.

Tractor Compatibility List
John Deere 6R Series:
Includes models 6105R, 6110R, 6115R, 6120R, 6125R, 6130R, 6135R, and 6140R. Also compatible with 6145R, 6150R, 6155R (including RH), 6170R, 6175R, 6190R, 6195R, 6210R, and 6215R units.

John Deere 6M Series:
Fits 6105M through 6195M models, specifically: 6105M, 6110M, 6115M, 6120M, 6125M, 6130M, 6135M, 6140M, 6145M, 6155M, 6175M, and 6195M.

John Deere 6030 & 7030 Premium (PR) Series:
6030 PR: 6230PR, 6330PR, 6430PR, 6530PR, 6630PR, 6830PR, 6930PR.
7030 PR: 7130PR, 7230PR, 7330PR, 7430PR, 7530PR.

John Deere 7030 & 7R Series:
Compatible with standard 7030 models (7630, 7730, 7830, 7930) and the 7R range, including 7200R, 7215R, and 7230R.

name: 9N210 Scatterable Submunition with 9E246 Fuze – Full & Cutaway | Inert Training Aid
description:
This premium 3D model recreates the 9N210 scatterable submunition paired with the 9E246 fuze, designed as a high-detail training and technical familiarization aid for EOD instruction, classroom use, and historical ordnance study.

The set includes both a complete external model and a full cutaway, allowing clear visualization of the internal layout, fuze placement, fragmentation body structure, and internal cavity geometry. Every component has been modeled to provide accurate proportions and realistic internal spacing while remaining completely inert and safe for handling.

The 9N210 is widely recognized as a compact Soviet/Russian submunition designed for area coverage and fragmentation effects. Its distinctive spherical/fragmentation body and centrally mounted fuze make it an important reference item for recognition training and technical-intelligence education.

This model is intended for:

EOD familiarization

Technical-intelligence training

Classroom instruction

Museum or display collections

Safe hands-on training environments

All components are non-functional and contain no energetic materials.

Cutaway versions expose internal structure for clear instructional viewing and color-coded training if desired.

Historical Background / Use Case

The 9N210 is a Soviet-designed scatterable fragmentation submunition commonly associated with cluster-delivered payloads intended for wide-area coverage. Compact and efficient in design, it uses a centralized fuze system to initiate fragmentation effects after deployment.

The 9E246 fuze represents the mechanical and timing element associated with this type of munition, making it a frequent subject in EOD recognition and technical analysis. Due to continued appearances of similar submunitions in modern conflicts, accurate inert models are valuable for training, identification, and safe familiarization.

⚠️ DISCLAIMER

This is an inert, non-functional training aid.
It contains no energetic materials and cannot be made functional.
For display, educational, and simulation use only.

• 0.3 mm — minimal play
• 0.5 mm — increased reliability of moving parts separation, ideal for beginners or printers with average precision

Suitable for:
• Soldering connections between two wires
• Holding small components during assembly

This holder is a must-have for anyone who solders frequently — from hobbyist electronics enthusiasts to professional engineers. Just print it without supports, twist the clamps, and start working!

name: Milwaukee M12 Replacement Battery Case
description:
This 3D printable Milwaukee M12 Battery Case is the result of extensive research and testing to create a solution to the common failure areas found with these cases.

I have downloaded many 'Free' files for extrusion only to have them  break on the second or third use. (Sometimes, straight away)

During the development of this drawing I have made and destroyed over 30 models all of which have been tweaked and re-produced to get to this final drawing.

The base of this model is much thicker than that of the original, this is a common area of weakness and tends to crack with use.
The locking tabs are also a common area of failure, fracturing or breaking off completely. (This is extremely common with the single 3D printed alternatives.

This case is made of two separate elements, the actual case itself and 2 tangs that are glued in place.
3D printing the tangs directly onto the model creates a weakness as the deposition of plastic, layer on layer, over a small area, creates a fracture stress point. Printing the tabs in the Horizontal Position gives them greater flexibility reducing the risk of snapping. (Please see photos)
The back of the case is designed to allow the Battery Internals to slide in and then click down into place to enable the screw to hold the two components together. Finally the case has been tweaked so that it fits the receiving tool nicely with minimal gaps.   

I use a generic PETG glue from amazon with only a small qty injected into the tab holes. Excessive glue can make the tabs brittle and they will snap with use.
details:
3D Print
I have an old Prusa Mk3 i3 printer.
This is running 'AnyCubic' PETG.
The base is 90 deg - First Layer, dropping to 85 there after.
The Extruder is 225 deg start to finish.
I have slowed the print speed down to reduce 'Hairy Prints'
I usually print the tangs separately as they can heat warp if left on the bed for the 5-6 hour print time.

name: 2 1/4" OD Steam Pipe (57.15mm) Exhaust Modeling kit
description:
⚠️ WARNING!
THIS KIT MAKES FABRICATING HIGH-END CUSTOM HEADER MANIFOLDS EXTREMELY EASY. PREPARE TO HAVE LOTS OF FUN AND ENJOY THE CRAFT!
⚠️ WARNING!

This kit is designed for modeling exhaust header manifolds and replicating them in steel. It’s highly effective for making length-tuned headers — just count the bends!

Please read this description carefully to understand how each part works and how they come together in the fabrication process.

Photos in the description are for reference only; the actual product may vary slightly from the images.

Why 30 Degrees?

The 30-degree segments offer the best balance between flexibility and fabrication efficiency.
For example, using three segments equals 90 degrees, meaning a full steel mandrel bend can be used without cutting.
If you use one or two segments, only one cut is required — by cutting a single mandrel bend, you’ll get either a 30-degree or a 60-degree bend.
This makes the fabrication process extremely efficient.

Bandsaw Fixture

The bandsaw fixture allows you to align your bandsaw blade precisely with the mandrel’s center axis.
Keeping your mandrel bend flush with the fixture’s marked cutting surface ensures accurate cuts without needing to measure angles or lengths.

The two indicated cutting depths compensate for blade kerf, giving you perfect 30-degree and 60-degree cuts every time (see images).

Note: The bandsaw fixture can also be used without a bandsaw — simply use it as a guide to scribe your cut line and finish the cut with an angle grinder.

Flange Clips

The flange clips mount behind your new exhaust flange and allow you to clip your models directly to the engine block.
This makes removing and reinstalling your mock-up fast and precise, ensuring it goes back in the exact same position every time.

180-Degree Index Marks

Each segment has two 180-degree alignment marks.
These marks allow you to line up each segment precisely and are essential during the fabrication process.

How to Use

Ensure all engine components are installed before starting to avoid clearance issues later.

Apply a small amount of grease to each segment’s clipping surface — this extends their life and improves fitment.

Install the flange clips behind your header flange and model each primary tube all the way to your collector.
(This step takes time and plenty of trial and error.) Once you’ve modeled all the pipes — at least one side — you can start transferring to steel.

Carefully remove each modeled tube without twisting or bending the arrangement. (Distortion at this stage will cause fabrication errors.)

Count your total number of segments and order the correct number of mandrel bends and straight sections.

Mark two centerlines on your straight pipes and all your bend segments, 180 degrees apart.

Set your dividers to the distance between two index marks on your model segments. You’re transferring the chord length between the marks to your steel bends.
(If your index marks are already aligned, skip this step — just tack your bends together with the centerlines lined up, then proceed to Step 9.)

Using your dividers, scribe the distance from Step 7 along the centerline of your mandrel bend — this shows where the next bend’s centerline should align.

Check your alignment as you go and progressively weld your pipes to avoid distortion.

It might sound a bit complicated, but once you start playing with the parts, it’ll click quickly — and it’s actually pretty easy.

Includes:

SR and LR centerline radius (CLR) bend segments in 30 degrees
(e.g., a 1 ⅞" pipe with a 1.5 × CLR has a centerline radius of 1 ⅞" × 1.5)

Straight segments in 100 mm, 50 mm, 25 mm and 20mm lengths

Flange pieces for clipping segments to your exhaust flange

Bandsaw jigs for each CLR size

The segments are designed to print without supports, saving processing time.
All files are pre-positioned on the print bed for convenience — just slice and print as many as you need!

Photos in the description are for reference only; the actual product may vary slightly from the images.
The exhaust manifold shown was built entirely using this kit.

name: Pico 4 Ultra Enterprise radial hinge replacement.
description: The radial hinges on these headsets have an unfortunate tendency to break after a while.  I made these replacement parts for the place I was working at.
details:
These parts are for use with a Pico 4 ultra enterprise with a broken right radial hinge.  Bear in mind that these repairs involve partial disassembly of delicate electronics and are completely at your own risk.  I cannot be held liable for equipment which is damaged or destroyed during installation.  
in addition to the parts included in these STL files you will need

some 3m machine screws 25mm long I prefer the ones with the countersunk heads so that they are flush with the exterior surface
https://www.amazon.com/Smgda-M3-0-5-Socket-Countersunk-Stainless/dp/B0DDTFPYHZ/ref=sr_1_3_pp?

and some 3M nuts
https://www.amazon.com/binifiMux-M1-6-Stainless-Steel-200pcs/dp/B08N68W9SP/ref=sr_1_3_pp?

and if you don't have one a spudger:
https://www.amazon.com/STREBITO-Spudger-Ultimate-Computer-Electronics/dp/B0BHPC2WB5/ref=sxin_18_pa_sp_search_thematic_sspa?

as well as some hex drivers and some sort of drill for 3MM holes and some tweezers.  A screwdriver for precision screws. a screw tray would help too especially a magnetic one.

After printing these files remove the face cushion which should only be held on by magnetic snaps.  Then remove the face plate by removing the eight very small screws and setting them aside somewhere where you will not lose them.  Keep in mind that there is a ribbon cable connecting the face  plate to the rest of the headset near the top center.  Do not fully separate the faceplate from the shell until you have undone the latch holding the ribbon cable to the faceplate.  Next, gently separate the plate from the rest of the shell with a spudger or other tool specifically designed for work on electronics or cell phones.  The plate is thin and fragile and will not come off of the eyepieces easily so be patient and gentle when you remove it.  Now you will be able to see the hinges.  

Get a pair of tweezers and gently remove the molexes plugged from the side of the headband into the main body of the headset.  these are very delicate 30 guage (.3mm) wires and will snap under too much strain.  Next pull the headband on the right side away from the body of the headset, if the heads of the molexes get stuck going through the middle of the hinge guide them through with the tweezers.  

Next pop out the metal radial hinge.  Push it towards the inside of the shell until it comes loose.  

next using a dremel or a jewelers hand drill carfully drill 3 millimeter holes through the headband over the exact spots where the old screws passed through.  try not to stray too far from those or you may hit the speaker or the wires. passing through the back of the shell.

Slide the 3d printed sleeve over the loose end of the headband.  it should fit a little snug.  line up the holes in the sleeve with the holes in the headband.  screw the 25mm machine screws into the holes until they are sticking out the other side of the headband, you can use the end of the screws to alight the radial hinge to the outer piece.

slot two M3 nuts into the Hexagonal holes in the radial hinge.  then carefully place it into the hole where the old radial hinge was pushing it from the inside out.  the slanted portion of the radial hinge should match up to the slanted stopper on the inside of the tube the radial hinge is inside of.  

carefully run the wires through the hole in the center of the hinge using tweezers (this part is a real pain in the butt and if you can think of a better way to do this let me know)

hold the radial hinge in place and turn the screws.  press something against the back of the radial hinge to keep the 3M nuts from popping out.  continue tightening until the bolts are no longer visible from the outside of the joint.  

using tweezers very carefully plug the molexes for the speakers and volume buttons back into their sockets.  this part takes patience and a steady hand. 

replace the the face plate, remember the ribbon cable and all eight screws. then pop the face cushion back on and test for functionality.

name: Planetary Gears Grabber
description:
🦾 3D Printable Planetary Grabber – Support-Free Mechanical Concept STL ⚙️

Discover the beauty of mechanical motion with this 3D printable planetary grabber, a conceptual yet fully functional design inspired by real planetary gear systems. This model is perfect for makers, engineers, and anyone who loves clever mechanical ideas brought to life through 3D printing.

The grabber works using a planetary gear mechanism: when you rotate the center (sun) gear, the surrounding gears move together, causing the grabber jaws to tighten or loosen smoothly. It’s a simple action with a very satisfying result!

Designed with practicality in mind, this model is completely support-free, easy to print, and easy to assemble. All parts are engineered for a press-fit assembly, so no glue, screws, or extra hardware are required.

⭐ Key Features

Functional planetary gear mechanism

Rotate the sun gear to open or close the grabber

No supports required – clean and stress-free printing

No glue needed – simple press-fit assembly

Beginner-friendly yet fascinating for advanced makers

Great as a desk toy, educational model, or mechanical demo

🔧 Perfect For

Learning planetary gear principles

Engineering demonstrations & STEM education

Desk toys and interactive displays

Concept prototypes and mechanical experiments

name: AuditivSound MR4 4" 80x60° Constant Directivity Midrange Waveguide for B&C 4NDF34
description:
This waveguide kit is designed around the B&C Speakers 4NDF34 4" Midrange Driver. 

The kit includes several parts for easy assembly: the MR4 waveguide, phase plug, closed back chamber and a cover for the back chamber. 

It produces very high SPL for the small size of the driver and a flat frequency response,  while providing true constant 80x60° directivity. The waveguide kit provides high-resolution midrange for High-End HiFi systems and small PA systems. The phase plug shape is specifically designed for the membrane profile of the B&C 4NDF34 driver. 

Sensitivity: 100dB 2,83V / 1m
Frequency response: 600Hz - 3Khz
Coverage: 80x60° 
Dimensions: 340mm x 290mm x 120mm

The waveguide is based on the OSSE horn profile from Marcel Batik and designed in the "Hornsculpt" parametric waveguide design software (Sonitos Audio / David Heutmann).

Please read the the instructions file carefully included in the download before printing! If you have any questions don´t hesitate to contact us via Mail or Instagram (links provided in the instructions file).

The last photo shows the prototype together with a matching HF horn.

Files are for personal, non commercial use only!
details:
We recommend printing in PETG or ASA with 5 wall lines and 20% infill. We used a BambuLab H2S printer. 

It is possible to print the waveguide part standing upwards on the shorter side with minimal tree support for the driver mounting flange and a 10mm brim on the buildplate.
