name: ESP32 WLAN + PN532 NFC Module Case [Waterproof]
description:
I designed a waterproof case for the ESP32 WLAN module to protect it in outdoor or damp environments. The ESP32 is widely used for IoT projects due to its powerful features, but it’s not inherently moisture-resistant. This 3D-printed case offers a simple and functional solution to keep your module safe.


What You’ll Need
- ESP32 WLAN module (e.g.: https://amzn.to/40oSfJC *)
- Silicone or rubber gaskets for sealing (optional)
details:
1. Print the Case: The STL file includes a dedicated slot for the ESP32 module, ensuring a snug and secure fit.

2. Install the Module: Place the ESP32 into the slot, aligning cables with the provided openings.

3. Seal and Assemble: Apply silicone or gaskets around the edges and cable ports for additional protection. Secure the case with screws.

4. Test the Seal: Before inserting the ESP32, perform a water test with the empty case to ensure it is leak-proof.




*) Note: The link above is an affiliate link. If you make a purchase through this link, I will earn a small commission at no extra cost to you.

name: Welding machine
description: A 3D model of a welding machine, when printed, serves as a detailed and accurate representation of this essential tool used in various fabrication and construction processes. The model effectively showcases key components such as the welding gun, control panel, and power supply, allowing for a comprehensive examination of the machine's design and functionality. Furthermore, it aids engineers and designers in prototype testing and design validation, helping identify potential improvements before full-scale production. The precision of 3D printing ensures that even the smallest details of the welding machine are faithfully recreated, making it an essential resource for refining and optimizing welding equipment designs.

This printed model is particularly valuable for design validation, educational purposes, and prototype testing, allowing designers and engineers to assess the machine's functionality and ergonomics before committing to production. name: Dust filter holder for Falcon 2 Pro Laser 40W
description:
Hi everyone,
When I came up with the idea for the bracket, I had already sat down with my laser unit and given it a thorough cleaning.
Due to laser operation, combustion particles gradually build up on the fans, in the ventilation channels inside the housing, and on the electronics. Over time, this isn’t good for the laser.
When I saw this, I realized I didn’t want to go through the hassle of replacing it and the resulting expense. So I opened up my 3D modeling software and searched online for the right covers.
I quickly found and ordered them on Amazon.
After a few adjustments to the frame, it was done. The laser is now better protected and therefore less prone to failure. The filters are washed or replaced at regular intervals. The filters do not affect the laser’s performance in any way.

I’ve been using the cover for a few weeks now, and I have to say… it was a good idea… there’s less to no residue left in the laser. 

The covers measure 40x40 mm and 50x50 mm

https://www.amazon.de/dp/B0989GR3B7?ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details&th=1 
https://www.amazon.de/dp/B014U92CAC?psc=1&ref=ppx_yo2ov_dt_b_product_details 

I secured them using the screws provided. All it took was a small 3-mm hole, and they were firmly in place.

All in all, a great solution that’s easy on the laser—and ultimately on my wallet.

name: Tackle Box with 3 Compartments.
description:
I spent about a month designing this unique tackle box. The printed version uses 5mm thick walls, but there’s also a 3mm thickness version available for those who prefer to save on filament.

Dimensions:

Overall Size: 240 mm x 180 mm x 200 mm
Print Volume: Fits within a standard 200 mm x 200 mm x 200 mm print area
Features:

Three Expandable Compartments: Provides ample space for all your fishing gear.
Additional Storage: Plenty of space below the compartments for larger items.
Sturdy Construction: Designed to be durable and practical for everyday use.
Instructions
Parts to Print:

Base
Lid
2 small containers
1 large container
4 small arms
4 large arms
Latch (2 parts: top and bottom)
Assembly:

Arms and Compartments:

Attach the arms to the base and compartments using M5 bolts (8 mm long) and nuts.
Ensure the bolts are tightened enough for the compartments to swing open and hold their position. Optionally, secure the nuts with glue.
Latches:

Print the latch in two parts: the top stationary piece with a pivot and the bottom print-in-place piece that holds the string, wire, or filament.
Secure the top part of the latch to the lid and the bottom half to the base with M5 bolts (12-16 mm long) and nuts.
Use fishing string, wire, or 3D filament to secure the latch by forming a loop through the small hole in the bottom latch piece. The bottom latch will lift to allow the wire to reach the top pivot, then swing down to tighten the lock.
Hinge:

Use a 5 mm rod (180-190 mm long) to secure the lid and base together.
Align the holes in the hinge and slide the rod through. Secure it by gluing or filling the gaps at both ends.

Additional Notes
Materials: The box is designed to be printed in PETG for durability and translucency.
Assembly Tips: Ensure all moving parts can swing freely before finalizing the assembly with glue or securing the nuts.

Download Now: Get this exclusive tackle box design for just $0.99 and organize your fishing gear like never before!

name: Cartographer or Beacon 3D eddy probe mount for Qidi X-Max 3
description:
This Qidi X-Max 3 3D printer modification replaces the rear cover of the print head and provides a mounting location for the Cartographer or Beacon 3D eddy probe.

The cover does not contact any hot components of the printer, but I recommend printing in a thermoplastic or resin that has similar strength and thermo-resistance properties as ABS/ASA, Nylon (PA12), Polypropylene (PP), or Polycarbonate (PC).

You may need slightly longer 2.5mm screws to mount this cover than what comes with the printer or use a drill bit to counter-bore the holes. Reuse the existing toolhead board fan from the original cover.

NOTE: A v2 version of the design has been uploaded to address the narrower mounting hole locations of the Cartographer probe. The Beacon 3D probe holes are approx. 2mm wider apart.

NOTE 2026-02-14: Clarification on above note and recent reports by users. The v2 version is the same as the v1 version but with slots for the mounting screws vs holes to account for variances in screw locations between production runs of the Beacon and Cartographer modules. You would use the v2 for both or a newer released version as applicable. A recent user has reported the height of the X-Max 3 hotend/nozzle may have changed. Waiting for a measurement and I will issue a revised model for download.
details: I recommend that you use 3 layers/perimeters and 15% infill (honeycomb pattern). Use supports as needed depending on preferred orientation of model that best suits your printer.

name: Concealed hinge
description:
While I am making own enclosure for a 3d printer, I wanted to make something different, and to make whole thing more unique I wanted to step away from normal hinges that I usually see people use. Inspiration was a concealed hinge that is used in woodworking for making doors, this is a simplified version. 

Hinge is designed to open up to 180° if that is what you need :)

The model is created in Fusion360 as a parametric model, which allows you to change the overall height of the hinge and to change the thickness of pins needed. You can alter or make own casing to suit your needs. 

As a test print I made it from PETG and used 1,75mm filament pieces for the pins and the hinge works great and even when I applied some force to it, it did not break. 

Uploaded Fusion 360 model, so you can edit it and step file to import into slicer where you can split it.

description:

This model has the Peugeot logo with the top part rounded
details:
I did print this in TPU 64 D from Basf, but any hard TPU should do the job for example Tpu 60D from 3dfils. I don't recommend printing in PETg  because when I fit the part in the wheel, the fittings of it had broken. but you can try to see if it works.


Print settings.

I made two different Gcodes to do this part with different resolutions   0.16mm for the fittings and the top part and for the Peugeot logo 0.08 mm.

Then I mixed the 2 programs  in one gcode file running for example a resolution of 0.16 to the z level of 10 and after that i when with the 0.08 mm of resolution

Also i did print out a support in pla, and then I  paused the print and put the support before printing the top part,  and the resumed the print  I did this technique because the supports in TPU are hard to take of.

name: AC Vertical mold M
description:
Casting mold for metal casting with an inner diameter of


126mm x 105mm and a mold height of 35mm.


The holes can be drilled using the drill plate provided (I planned the hole to be 4mm and used M4 screws with nuts). This can then also be used as a base plate for cast models.





The other openings are planned in 3mm and serve as a template for M4 threaded holes (so that the closed molds can be used as attachments).





ATTENTION: Due to shrinkage, the diameter changes depending on the metal used for casting.


Nevertheless, use the base plate for drilling so that you can use it again later.





For the drill holes, I recommend using the base plate (match plate) for one half and then drilling through the second half using the first half of the mold.





The design of the mold allows them to be stacked on top of each other to increase the size of the mold, in which case we recommend drilling another hole in each case!





I recommend a resolution and layer height of 0.1 mm to simplify reworking.


The model is normally smooth enough for casting with 2-3 layers of varnish.





The enclosed closed mold allows the casting flask to be extended in height.


This can also be used separately as a small casting mold.

name: Alfa Romeo Momo Vega Hubcap
description:
For reasons unknown to anyone but Momo the Vega style hubcaps are held on by nothing but small ridges and as a result, constantly fall off the car.

These replacement hubcaps have so far been tested on two separate vehicles and have worked well, though you will have to buy or print your own emblem for the center.

New:
Added A .step version for easier editing.
Added a version for 98mm PCD wheels
details:
I highly recommend you print these hubcaps from ABS or better, preferably with a carbon or glass fibre reinforcement. ABS is easy to sand and paint while also being able to withstand heat. The fibre will make the part more ridged and prevent stretching over time.

The part is printed in the given rotation but unfortunately, you will need to use supports for the center of the part.

You can use PETG but it is A) Not very impact-resistant and B) will probably slowly bend over time in the sun and C) Doesnt take paint very well.

name: Sunlu Filament Dryer Box S2 Stable Base replacement
description:
I have 3 of these dryers and they work great but I find them to be very unstable on those tiny  legs so I made my own base. in doing so I also reoriented the fan and angle so it blows air in more of a circular direction. It just seems logical to me. The base is about the same width as the overall dryer itself and does not get in the say of the power connector.. Have a look at the pictures for a better understanding.

Its a direct replacement and Uses all original hardware.
Be careful when removing the original base as the fan is attached to it. I would suggest unscrewing the bottom heater and moving it aside carefully to get to the fan screws. Once the fan is unscrewed, remove the base and install the new printed base. once done, flip the dryer over and screw the fan into place with the arrows pointing the same way. make sure the fan wire is out of the way of the fan and neatly tucked away. reinstall the bottom heater and use as  directed.

The screws required to attach the feet are 4pcs or  2x10mm self tapping Flatheads. M2x10mm flathead screws will do as well. To make it easier, always drill out holes before inserting screws. In this the feet holes would require a drill bit size of 1.5mm


Disclaimer:
While its a VERY simple procedure, I am not responsible for damages possibly caused by dismantling or reassembly of the dryer or voided warranties due to tampering or modifications.
details:
Parts are printed as loaded in your slicer and the base requires a minimum bed of 120x220mm. 

I printed mine in PETG for a stronger layer to layer bond

The feet should be printed in TPU but otherwise can be anything you want.

No supports needed
3 perimeters
20% infill

name: SQUARE COLLETS FOR LATHE - PINZAS CUADRADAS PARA TORNO - SQUARE COLLETS FOR LATHE
description:
Holding square bars on a lathe with a three-jaw chuck is always very difficult. For this purpose I have designed this model so that it can be manufactured with a 3D printer.





I have included three files with different sizes, for 6 x 6 mm, 10 x 10 mm and 12.7 x 12.7 mm (1/2 ") bars.


 These models are scalable to the size you need but you must take as reference the size of the bar you want to turn, NOT the general size of the part.





For example, if you want to scale to turn a 15 x 15 mm bar the scale factor is obtained with the following formula:


Scale factor = (15 * 100) / 12.7 which would give a result of 118.11% for the whole part.


This in the case of starting from the model I have uploaded for 12.7 x 12.7 mm bars.


If you wanted to make a clamp for 7 x 7 mm bars, it would be convenient to start from the model for 6 x 6 mm bars. It is always convenient to choose the closest size to scale up from it.





The bar to be clamped should slide smoothly through the square hole, without large clearances, before the clamp is tightened on the lathe chuck.


This will ensure perfect centering, as can be seen in the accompanying photographs.

name: Ender 5 S1 extruder part
description:
It often happened to me that printing stopped because the filament no longer came out of the hotend. There can be many causes, including extruder malfunction.
Hence the idea of having one that allows you to see how the mechanism works, whether it is blocked, whether the filament has dug in, whether the screw has been tightened enough, etc. It is also useful for checking the correct retraction movement and speed.
So I reproduced an extruder cover of my Creality Ender 5 s1 printer that allows you to see through.
It is possible to print it with a transparent material, or simply see through the holes I created in the points less subject to stress.
Being a part subject to wear and a minimum of heat, it is preferable to print it in PETG or ABS.
I'm currently testing it with a clear PETG filament and it's working great.

In the file you will find two versions, one "soft" with less perforation, the other "extreme" with more perforation.
The metal inserts, if you need them, can be inserted in the lower part.
To mount the upper spout you will not need the insert.

My video:

name: CNC Mill G0704 / BF20 Enclosure - All Manufacturing Files
description:
This is the standard enclosure we use for our CNC conversions. It is designed to fit the Grizzly G0704 / Optimum BF20 or clone machines. It fits most off the shelf CNC conversion kits as is, but we have come across a it with a slightly longer Y axis motor that needs a small cut made in the roof sheet metal to clear the column position. Check out the photos and you can see an example of this.

Construction is relatively straight forward, with two options for the base tray - either welded seam (slightly nicer) or riveted seams (somewhat easier for a DIY job).
There are .DXF and .STEP files provided to send to your local CNC laser cut / fold shop. The native Solid Works files are also provided, so you can tweak the design if needed. The acrylic windows have their own .DXF files for laser cutting.

The panels are mostly joined to each other using M5 screws and M5 rivnuts, and the windows are held in place with M4 button head screws and nyloc nuts.

The doors run on SBR16-500L rails, and use the long SBR16LUU bearings. The handles are an off-the-shelf unit with 145mm hole centers.

NOTES:
- The welded machine riser has mounting holes that work with the kits we've fitted. We've seen some variance between machines and kits, so make sure your hole positions are correct for your particular set up.
- The holes to mount the tool racks are not modelled into the side panels. We use self drill / tap screws to fix these in place.
- There is a bank of cable gland holes on the back. Use as many as you need to, and then blank the others with blanking plugs (available very cheaply online).
- We use an M12 Machine foot. If you wish to use a different thread size, just change your bushes to suit.
- There are no engineering drawings included in this package - it's assumed that the parts will just be lasercut & folded and then bolted together, and the 3d model used as a reference if needed. If you get stuck feel free to fire me an email with any questions.
- We use 1.15mm pre-galvanized steel for most of the panels to give improved resistance to flood coolant.

name: Bambu Lab X1 / X1C Lid Riser Spacer for Ventilation
description:
This vented lid riser / spacer for the BambuLab X1 / X1C works with the standard glass lid, or with the glass lid on a lighting upgrade riser.  Top and bottom surfaces of this riser are at the correct angle so the glass lid is properly supported, not just by one edge of the top of the riser.  Lifts the glass lid by about 1 inch for good air flow to fight against heat creep and clogged nozzles during prints with high temperatures.  Has a relief gap in the top center to allow for the screws of the glass lid handle. Also has centering fins on the top so you always place it correctly.  Can be made from rigid materials like PLA, or flexible like TPU 95A (pictures shown are of black TPU 95A).

* Works with lighting upgrade risers, as well as the standard case with glass lid.
* Helps to prevent nozzle clogging (from heat creep) due to high printing or bed temperatures.
* Properly supports the glass lid since the top and bottom surfaces are at the correct angle, not parallel.
* Releif gap in the top center to make way for the lid handle screws.
* Centering fins fit around the lid handle so it is in the right position.
* Prints without the need for supports if the front face is placed down on the printing bed.
* Both STL and STEP file formats are included.

name: Universal Design filament spool holder Flexi Arm
description:
Universal Design filament spool holder Flexi Arm





### The innovative helper for every 3D printing enthusiast





---





**History of our creation:**


Inspired by the need to make 3D printing even more efficient and user-friendly, the Universal Design Filament Spool Holder Flexi Arm was born. Developed in my engineering office, where the passion for precision and functionality is paramount, this model represents the bridge between engineering precision and the desire for universal applicability.





**Origin of the idea:**


It all started with a 2.5 kilogram coil from Polymaker that simply wouldn't fit on conventional holders on our BambuLab fleet. So a simple requirement became a vision - to create a holder that is not only robust and customizable, but also combines design and functionality.





**Use of the object:**


The Flexi Arm is not just a support for filament spools of all kinds - it is a symbol of the fusion of design and functionality. It can be used for all common filament spools up to 2.5 kg in size (Polymaker, BambuLab, Extrudr, etc.) and offers a secure hold without compromising on aesthetics.





**Why is this brilliant?


\- *Universally applicable*: Whether for small hobby printers or large industrial machines, the Flexi Arm delivers what it promises.


\- *Design meets function*: With its modern and sleek design, it blends into any studio or workshop.


\- *Sustainable and durable*: Made entirely from biodegradable PLA, it stands not only for innovation but also for environmental protection.





Experience the next generation of 3D printing accessories with the Flexi Arm filament spool holder - the sturdy, customizable companion for your creative projects.

- **Base coil holder**

### Pressure settings for the arm and pin of the filament spool holder

- **Weight**: ~90g

name: Red Color Mobile Bottle/ Lubricant Bottle
description:
The proper viscosity is the single most important criterion of a lubricating oil. Multiweight oils (such as 5W-30) have polymers added to the oil. The polymers allow the oil to have different weights at different temperatures. Multiweight oils perform a great service of not being too thick at cold startup to provide engine wear protection by flowing more quickly to critical engine parts. The first number, the 5W of the 5W-30 viscosity, for example, indicates the viscosity of the oil at a cold temperature; the second number indicates the viscosity at operating temperatures. The lower the first number the better flow ability at startup, especially at cold temperatures.

You should also be aware that multiweight oils are backward compatible. In other words, an 0W-30 can be used with a 5W-30. The second number is important.

name: Heusinkveld Sprint Dayton Audio TT25 Mod
description:
Heusinkveld Sprint Dayton Audio TT25 Mod





Needed:


2x Dayton Audio TT25 PUCK Tactile Transducer Mini Bass Shaker


8x M4 hexagon nut


8x M4x12 cheese-head screw with hexagon socket





I tried my best to integrate the parts from the pedals into the printed parts. And also to make the prints as simple as possible. If you want to install the mods on the brake and throttle you have to print the following parts.





2x blue part - socket for the Dayton Audio TT25 PUCK


1x green part - mounting adapter for brake


1x white part - mounting adapter for throttle


2x yellow part - Adapter Pin to reduce the diameter for the mounting screw





Please tighten the screws with care otherwise its possible that if u use to much force you will destroy the printed parts. I recut the threads of the hexagon parts to remove the screw locking varnish. So it is easier to mount the screws if you reassemble.





My result you can see in the attached pictures. Maybe its possible with time that the screws will loosen to the shakes, so use a screw locking varnish (medium strength, so you can loosen the screw again) to avoid that.
details:
For the white and the green part I used supports inside to get the shape of the hexagon as accurate as possible, because we insert the hexagon parts into the printed parts.


For the installation of the Bass shakers I used the screws which are inside the package. The holes for the installation should be taller then a diameter of 2,5mm. Otherwise the printed part could crack out. The stl-file is designed with a diamater of 2,8mm. But I recognized that my printed part was always below 2,5mm, so I drilled the parts afterwards.

name: Spur gear 22 teeth - 2 mm module - 10 mm depth.
description:
Spur gears are very useful devices to transmit movement and transform torque and rotation. 
My idea here is to provide a series of spur gears, in several number of teeth for you to print and use in your projects. The bore for the shaft is always 6 mm, which ensures a good resistance when mounted in 6 mm steel rod.
 
Spur gear 22 teeth - 2 mm module - 10 mm depth.
Please note that a pair of spur gears must be same module in order to couple accordingly. I mean, you cannot use a 2 mm module gear to mesh with a 3 mm module gear.  You can couple different number of teeth to achieve different rotation and torque, but the module must be the same! I wish you a good luck in your projects and designs!

name: FLSUN V400 Universal holder for speeder pad, storage tray, tool holder
description:
In my designs, I always make sure that no additional parts that cannot be produced with the 3D printer are required.


My FLSUN V400 universal mount consists of a fastening element that is inserted into the grooves of the printer columns and fixed in place with clamping screws. This makes it quick and easy to adjust the height.


Attention: To insert the fastening elements, the top cover plate of the printer column must be removed by loosening the 2 screws.


Various accessories such as a speeder pad holder, a storage tray and/or a tool holder can then be attached to the fastening element.


As far as possible, there is always a left and a right version of the accessory.


The download contains ALL the required and possible elements, which I will add to as new ideas arise.

name: Spur gear 16 teeth - 2 mm module - 10 mm depth.
description:
GEAR Series 
Spur gears are very useful devices to transmit movement and transform torque and rotation. 
My idea here is to provide a series of spur gears, in several number of teeth for you to print and use in your projects. The bore for the shaft is always 6 mm, which ensures a good resistance when mounted in 6 mm steel rod. 
Spur gear 16 teeth - 2 mm module - 10 mm depth.
Please note that a pair of spur gears must be same module in order to couple accordingly. I mean, you cannot use a 2 mm module gear to mesh with a 3 mm module gear.  You can couple different number of teeth to achieve different rotation and torque, but the modules must be the same!

name: skoda octavia 4 ventilation induction charger
description:
one problem encountered by all octavia 4 users is that the induction charger heats up the phone too much, causing it to lock up and stop charging. To solve this problem, the phone needs to be cooled down, and the air vent is not far away, but skoda has not provided for air to flow down to the charging area.





With this model that I modelled in freecad, the air is sent back to the induction charger underneath, the phone stays cool and charges without a problem.





Here I've modeled the adapter to fit over the passenger vent, leaving the driver vent free.





I'm giving away the freecad files that will allow you to modify the model to your liking and adapt it if you wish.





This model is tested and effective, test on a skoda octavia model IV ....
details:
I printed my model on PETG which makes the model very strong ... a density of 75% gives a very very strong adapter, but you can start your tests with 20% filling, it still works.


I used CURA v5.4 on an ender 5 plus for my model and you ABSOLUTELY have to activate the supports. They are quite difficult to remove in "normal" bracket mode, but you can try the "tree" mode bracket (see photo) which is surely easier to remove.





I took a 1.0 nozzle which is more than enough to minimize printing time, no need to take 0.4 ....





For the direction in which the model is laid, look at the photos, it has to stand up ...





There are 3 versions: the 1.0 differs from the 2.0 just because the 2.0 has longer mounting lugs and is therefore a little more stable ...


The v3.0 adds the name "skoda" as decoration on the exterior of the model.





enjoy this essential accessory for your octavia 4!!!

name: FULL 3D PRINTABLE HEAT EXCHANGER - 254 X 254 PRINT PLATE
description:
HEAT EXCHANGER - 254 X 254 PRINT PLATE - 4 INCH HOSE CONNECTORS

FREE UPGRADE – 02 DEC 2025  - AN ESP32 CONTROLLER CAN BE INTEGRATED TO OPERATE THIS UNIT VIA WIFI WITH YOUR PHONE.   FEATURES: 4 TEMPERATURE SENSORS, WATER LEVEL SENSOR, AND TWO PWM MOTORS. THE ESP32 PROGRAM WAS CREATED WITH AI ASSISTANCE.

FREE UPGRADE - 5 NOV 2025 - A NEW HOUSING VERSION - WITH REINFORCED BOLTS ( IN ORDER TO AVOID VIBRATION DURING PRINTING) ... AND NEW SEPARATION PLAN VERSION - WITH CORUGATION - IN ORDER TO INCREASE EXCHANGE RANDAMENT! 

Reduce your energy bill! 



Thermal analysis (PETG) and Airflow performance for a similar heat exchanger, larger, 300x300 version with 100 separation plans.

Using 2 x 120mm computer fans.

Winter case - outside is   0 °C → room temperature is  22 °C



Plate size: ~268.6 × 268.6 mm, thickness (Z): 2.0 mm, exchange surface 0.40mm

Effective active surface (one side, including corrugation): ≈ 61,106 mm² → 0.0611 m²

Implied inner opening side: ≈ 247.2 mm (so the built-in rim is ~10.7 mm wide, ~85% open — nice!)

With 100 plates → total heat-transfer area (one side count): A ≈ 6.11 m²

Channel gap: 2.0 mm (your stack spacing)

Flow length: ≈ 0.247 m (inner opening side)

Hydraulic diameter: ~3.97 mm

PETG: k = 0.20 W/m·K, thickness in conduction: 0.40 mm

Air: ρ=1.2 kg/m³, μ=1.8e-5 Pa·s, k=0.026 W/m·K, Pr=0.71

Correlation: laminar, thermally developing rectangular channel (Shah–London style)




Sample below for Exchang conditions - Counterflow ε–NTU, balanced flows (Cr≈1), winter case - when outside is - 0 °C → and room temperature is - 22 °C



Highlights (per stream)

20 m³/h: h≈24.3 W/m²K, U≈11.85 W/m²K, UA≈72.4 W/K, ε≈0.915, Q≈135 W, supply out ≈ 20.13 °C, core Δp ≈ 2.0 Pa

30 m³/h: h≈24.7, U≈12.02, UA≈73.5, ε≈0.885, Q≈193 W, supply ≈ 19.47 °C, Δp ≈ 4.6 Pa

40 m³/h: h≈24.9, U≈12.12, UA≈74.2, ε≈0.862, Q≈246 W, supply ≈ 18.91 °C, Δp ≈ 6.8 Pa

60 m³/h: h≈25.2, U≈12.26, UA≈75.1, ε≈0.819, Q≈339 W, supply ≈ 18.02 °C, Δp ≈ 10.2 Pa

80 m³/h: h≈25.4, U≈12.36, UA≈75.8, ε≈0.786, Q≈418 W, supply ≈ 17.32 °C, Δp ≈ 12.2 Pa

What this means for your unit (30–40 m³ room, 24/7)

With 20–40 m³/h per stream (exactly your sweet spot), you get warm supply (≈19–20 °C at 0 °C outdoors) and tiny pressure drops through the core (only a few Pa; filters/ducts will dominate).

STL’s design built-in rim (~10–11 mm, ~85% open) looks ideal—great for sealing and uniform distribution with almost no penalty in UA.

Corrugation level appears moderate: predicted h ≈ 24–26 W/m²K → U ≈ 11.8–12.5 W/m²K, UA ≈ 72–76 W/K for the full 100-plate stack.

	​

 to ≥ 17 °C. In cold weather (0 °C outside), fans will naturally settle around 25–45 m³/h to hold that temperature, which is exactly in the high-efficiency zone above.

For even warmer air at the same flow:

Nudge corrugation to the “balanced” preset - (≈0.25–0.30 mm height, 6–8 mm pitch, 45° chevron, mirrored). Expect h to rise toward 30–33 W/m²K (+20–30%), lifting supply by ~0.6–1.2 °C at the same flow with a modest Δp increase.

New designed separation plans to test and to be publish on the product page!

Free upgrade 5 Jan 2024 : Separation Plan Vers 2024 - a full set of parts with enlarged holes ( from 10.40  to 10.80mm) - in order to allow an easy fitt!

Free upgrade 22 DEC 2023 : A new version of the Connector - with an access porthole for sensor cables was added to the pack!

In order to ensure that your printer have the capabilities to print functional parts... print and test the provided samples!
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/free-print-samples-heat-exchange-full-printable-system

A HEPA Filter System was design to connect and work together with the Heat Exchanger.
https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/large-circular-hepa-filters-housing

To keep the Heat Exchanger clean and free of impurities, it is strongly recommended to filter all the air that passes through the unit!

ASSEMBLING INFO!

Regarding the files you receive, on Cults page are included all the upgrades for this design! Sometime a lot of information, can be a little confusing… therefore … you should look first for the Latest Upgrade files – check releasing date!

In order to assemble one unit you will need:

* Housing Unit - the best housing, is the one what have the Media bolts included as part of the build, and it have the Legs connecting holes!

* Bottom Spacer

* Media - Selecting the Partition Media - can choose from 2mm to 4mm thickness - this will represent also the space between partition media; and also thickness of the :Sheet" ... from 0.4mm to 0.8mm! Small number will give you the best heat transfer... bigger give the strength! 

* Top Spacer

* Cover

* 3D Printed Nuts

* Drain Connector - condensation is going to be the main problem; make sure you position the unit so the condensation can be collected and guided to a drain line!

* Connectors -  look for the Connectors with a Sensor Connecting Point - those will give you the possibility to connect a sensor and have control over the temperature of the exchanger!

* Legs - if unit allows connecting a set of legs!

Strongly recommend filtering all the air entering the unit! See on the Exchanger page the link to an inline filter! Periodical is strongly recommended to dismantle the unit and wash/disinfect all components!

Post your progress with photo and post your impressions, full frontal truth... no hard feelings from my side! If you need additional help... please let me know!

Note: Realistic Expectations! Please be aware that this is a small unit designed to cover a single room. To increase the thermal exchange capabilities of the system, you can connect multiple units in series.

Using an air-to-air heat exchanger is one way to recover lost energy during ventilation. Instead of opening a window and losing heat or cooling from your house, consider using a heat recovery system!

You will want a small and constant flux of air, since unit is small and the time for the air to enter and exit this unit is not very long!

name: 6-in-1 Measuring Tool
description:
This is a 6-in-1 measuring tool that contains a protractor, simple caliper, hex measurer, radius finder, bolt sorter, and bolt length finder.
 

How to use:
 

Protractor (0-180° accurate to 2.5°)
Place the part on the tool and align it up with the aligning bar, move the arm so it lines up with the part you want to measure, then look through the angle viewing window to find the angle.

Simple Calpers (0"-6.25" accurate to .25")
Place the part in between the tip of the arm and the end of the aligning bar. The calipers will measure the distance from tip to tip, so make sure your part is aligned correctly. The measurement will be displayed in the distance viewing window.

Hex measurer (¼"-½")
Place the hex piece into one of the labeled holes. Once the piece fits snugly into one of the holes, that is the correct measurement for that piece.

Radius finder (1/8"-1")
Align the tool against the radius that you are trying to measure. Once it fits snugly against one of the finders, that is the correct radius.

Bolt Sorter (½"-#6)
Place a bolt in one of the bolt sorter slots. Once the bolt fits snugly in one of the slots, that is the correct size of that bolt

Bolt length finder (0"-5" accurate to .125")
Place the bolt so that the head is on the opposite side as the aligning arm and the shaft of the bolt is aligned in the bolt length finder. Use the numbers on the side of the bolt to determine the length of the bolt

description:
Restore the original appearance of your Opel Ampera / Chevrolet Volt Gen1 exterior mirror with this 3D-printable replacement component for the mirror-mounted turn signal indicator.

The mirror indicator is exposed to weather, UV, road debris and accidental damage. Over time, the original plastic component may crack, become damaged or require replacement while the rest of the mirror assembly remains perfectly usable.

This model provides a practical repair option for owners who want to restore the original mirror turn signal assembly without replacing the complete exterior mirror.

COMPATIBILITY

Designed for:

Opel Ampera
Vauxhall Ampera
Chevrolet Volt Gen1 / MK1
Vehicles equipped with the corresponding mirror-mounted turn signal system
OEM / GM REFERENCES

Left Hand / LH:

GM 22791739
Opel 12 23 047 / 1223047

Right Hand / RH:

GM 22791740
Opel 12 23 048 / 1223048

GM catalogs identify these as outside rear-view mirror turn signal lamp repair kits, with 22791739 for the left side and 22791740 for the right side.

FEATURES

✔ Designed around genuine GM mirror indicator geometry
✔ Left and right applications supported
✔ Ideal for repairing damaged mirror indicator components
✔ Helps preserve the original exterior mirror assembly
✔ Useful for increasingly difficult-to-source Ampera / Volt parts
✔ Suitable for restoration and repair projects
✔ Digital replacement part that can be printed whenever required
✔ Avoids replacing an otherwise functional complete mirror assembly

COMMON REASONS FOR REPLACEMENT

This model may be useful when:

The original mirror indicator component is cracked
Plastic housing has been damaged
Indicator trim has deteriorated with age
A used mirror is missing the correct indicator component
The complete mirror is still functional but the indicator section needs repair
PRINTING RECOMMENDATION

Because this component is used on the exterior of the vehicle, a material with good UV, temperature and weather resistance is recommended.

Suitable materials include:

ASA
ABS
PETG
Other durable automotive-grade filament

ASA is particularly suitable for long-term exterior use.

For best results:

Use accurate printer calibration
Check fit before permanent installation
Sand visible surfaces if required
Prime and paint where appropriate
Verify clip and mounting areas carefully
IMPORTANT FITMENT NOTE

Please check the OEM number and compare the model geometry with your existing mirror indicator before printing.

Mirror specifications can differ depending on model year, market and mirror configuration. The Chevrolet parts catalog, for example, lists 22791739/22791740 with turn-signal-equipped export-style mirror configurations, so checking the original part number is much safer than trusting the vehicle name alone.

CUSTOM MODIFICATIONS ARE AVAILABLE ON REQUEST — THE MODEL CAN BE MODIFIED, RESIZED OR ADAPTED TO YOUR SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS.

DIGITAL PRODUCT ONLY

name: BarberShop Clipper Guard Organizer – Barber Station Storage | 3D Printable
description:
Give your clipper guards a dedicated place on your workstation. An open-top organizer with separate compartments, a rounded profile and raised BarberShop lettering.

A more organized workstation starts with the small tools you reach for every day.

This BarberShop clipper guard organizer keeps guide combs together in a single, easy-to-see row. Separate compartments let you arrange compatible guards in your preferred order, while the open top makes it straightforward to take one out and return it after use.

The rounded rectangular body and raised BarberShop lettering bring a distinctive barber-themed finish to your counter. The printed samples show a purple body with white lettering and a white body with multicolored lettering, offering inspiration for your own print finish.

## Features

- Separate compartments to keep compatible clipper guards arranged in a row.
- Open-top access for taking out and returning guards.
- Keeps small attachments together instead of scattered across the work surface.
- Rounded body with raised BarberShop lettering.
- A practical display and storage idea for barber stations, salon counters and home haircut setups.

## Included files

- Main body project: barber shop卡尺主体.3mf
- Front panel mesh: barber shop卡尺盒面板.stl

## Please note

This listing is for digital 3D-printing files, not a physical product.

Clipper guards, clippers and other styling tools shown in the images are demonstration props and are not included.

Fit depends on the dimensions and shape of your guards; universal compatibility is not claimed.

Images include real printed samples captured from video and AI-generated salon scenes marked "AI SCENE". Use the real photos and model dimensions to assess the actual design and fit.

The purple/white and multicolored samples illustrate possible finishes; the available parts and printing method depend on the files provided.
details:
Printing / manufacturing notes

The supplied files are intended for FDM 3D printing. The main body is provided as a 3MF project and the front panel as an STL mesh.

Recommended starting point: print with PLA or another suitable rigid filament using your printer manufacturer's standard profile. Use the orientation shown in the slicer preview and inspect the complete toolpath before printing. The exact layer height, wall count, infill, supports, print time and material usage depend on the printer, nozzle and filament selected.

Please verify the dimensions and fit of your own clipper guards before printing multiple copies. Check the preview for the lettering and compartment walls, and adjust scale only if your tested guards require it.

The files may require separate color changes, multi-material setup or post-processing to reproduce the sample colors and raised BarberShop lettering. Any assembly, finishing or color-change steps should be confirmed from the supplied files and your own printer setup.

name: Renault Clio 2 MK2 3rd Brake Light Frame Trim / Bezel - High-Resolution 3D Scan (STL)
description:
High-Resolution 3D Scan of Rear 3rd Brake Light Outer Frame / Surround Trim for Renault Clio 2 MK2 (1998-2005)

This listing includes a precise, high-density 3D scan of the original rear third (3rd) brake light outer frame trim / bezel for Renault Clio 2 (MK2, 1998–2005 models).

Located at the top of the rear tailgate, this plastic frame trim frequently degrades, warps, or cracks due to constant sun exposure and weather elements. This scan offers an exact 1:1 digital baseline, capturing the original tailgate curve and alignment tabs for reverse engineering or 3D printing custom replacement frames.

Key Features & File Details
Direct OEM Scan: Scanned directly from an original genuine Renault tailgate brake light frame.

High Detail & Accuracy: Accurately maps the outer body profile, edge bevels, and mounting point locations.

CAD & Reverse Engineering Ready: Ideal digital reference mesh for Fusion 360, SolidWorks, or Rhino to design custom trim, modify clip tabs, or adapt aftermarket brake light units.

File Formats Included: .STL
details:
Adjustment Recommended: This file contains scanned 3D mesh data. Due to variations in printer tolerances, material shrinkage, and tailgate alignment, minor CAD tweaking, scaling, or light sanding may be required for the 3D printed frame to fit perfectly flush.

Recommended Printing Materials: Exterior tailgate parts require high UV and thermal resistance. Printing with PETG, ABS, or ASA is strongly recommended.

name: Mini Clamps
description:
These mini clamps pack a big punch in a compact package. Unlike most other fully 3D printed clamps, these use standard, off-the-shelf fasteners for the screw mechanism. This adds significant strength and lifetime to your fixtures while adding minimal or negligible cost. The smallest and strongest version can easily hold over 40 kg (90 lbs). There are also configurations included that have mounting holes on the back side of the C-clamp body to allow for modular mounting of many other components or designs using M6 fasteners on 25 mm spacing.

The design includes three heights of clamp and versions of each with back side mounting holes or without. The clamp foot also comes with three configurations, a standard height, a tall height, and a V-block (for clamping round stock).

The 50H can clamp 0- 35 mm (1 - 3/8") thick surfaces
The 75H can clamp 0- 60 mm (2 - 3/8") thick surfaces
The 100H can clamp 0- 85 mm (3 - 3/8") thick surfaces


Standard, non-locking nuts press-fit into the clamp body.

The screw you need for the clamps can be either a metric M8 or and imperial 5/16". The best option is threaded rod, cut to length with a lock nut/double nut on the far end. There is a wing nut model included that works for double nut/threaded rod configurations.  Socket head cap screws also work, you can use whatever you have available to you. The best screws are long, fully threaded configurations, but you can make do with partially threaded versions. Recommended screw lengths are:
50H - 60 mm
75H - 80 mm
100H - 100+ mm

I recommend printing the smallest clamp you can get away with as it will be the strongest and deflect the least.

Combine the Mini Clamps with some of my compatible accessories:
Vertical Storage Trays https://cults3d.com/:4823593
Headphone Holder https://cults3d.com/:4823555
Paper Towel Holder https://cults3d.com/:4823508
details:
Mini Clamp Body or Wing Nut:
Lay flat on build plate. 5+ wall loops - 25+% infill - gyroid - tree support optional but suggested. The weight tested version was done with PLA. However, for sustained clamping, you want a material with good creep resistance. CF/GF (fiber filled) filament or polycarbonate will be your best options here.

Mini Clamp Foot:
5+ wall loops - 100% infill - tree support optional but suggested.

description:
This bracket is designed to help achieve a perfectly aligned 90° corner when bonding two marble, porcelain, ceramic, or stone tiles with 45° mitered edges.

Even with accurately cut tiles, a small gap or misalignment can appear along the outside corner during assembly. This tool allows you to eliminate that gap by making fine adjustments before the adhesive fully cures.

The bracket is temporarily attached to the tiles using hot glue, allowing it to be removed easily after the adhesive has hardened without damaging the surface.

Features

* Designed for 45° miter-cut tile joints.
* Creates precise 90° outside corners.
* Fine adjustment using thumb screws.
* Eliminates visible gaps along the corner.
* Helps keep both tile faces perfectly flush.
* Reusable for multiple projects.
* Easy installation using hot glue.

How it works

1. Apply a small amount of hot glue to the bracket.
2. Attach the bracket to both tiles.
3. Tighten or loosen the thumb screw to gradually adjust the joint.
4. Close the gap until both tile edges are perfectly aligned.
5. Allow the tile adhesive to cure.
6. Remove the bracket by carefully separating the hot glue.

This system provides controlled, repeatable adjustment without excessive force, making it much easier to achieve a professional-quality mitered corner.

Version: V1.0.0

Shopping list and printing instructions:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Y4e6zgP-2D29INYxxV4nH0MRyC73qnD8/view?usp=sharing

name: Section 8 Designs StoneCrab LCG Transmission for the TRX4M
description:
Stone Crab LCG Transmission for the TRX4M

After months of testing, I am finally ready to release my Stone Crab LCG Transmission for the TRX4M.

This transmission mounts into almost any TRX4M chassis. When using a stock-style skid plate, all of your links will mount just as they did with the factory transmission.

When using the LP skid plate, the lower links mount in the factory upper-link location, and the upper links must be mounted directly to the chassis. This may increase your wheelbase, so be sure to check your driveshaft length.

Extra side and corner plates are included to help seal the transmission from dust and debris, but they are optional. Only the top plate is required for assembly.

The motor can be mounted facing either forward or rearward, depending on chassis clearance and personal preference.

I also plan to release a fully enclosed version of the transmission. Once it's complete, I'll add it to this listing.

Assembly (Photos Included)

Begin by inserting the output gear into the rear plate.

Install the middle gear, making sure it meshes properly with the output gear.

Install the input gear as shown in the photos.

Once all the gears are installed in the rear plate, slide the front plate onto the bearings.

Secure the top plate using four M2×6 mm button-head screws to hold the transmission together.

Install the completed transmission into the skid plate using four 
M2×8 mm flat-head socket cap screws.

On the stock-style skid plate, the fit is intentionally snug and may require a little force during installation.

On the LP skid plate, there is additional clearance, making installation much easier.

Optional

Install the optional side and corner plates to help seal the transmission and provide additional protection from dust and debris.

Finally, install the transmission into your favorite chassis and continue building your rig!

Materials Needed

8 × M2×6 mm button-head screws
https://a.co/d/09eD4tTD

4 × M2×8 mm flat-head socket cap screws
https://a.co/d/0bctRLKO

1 × TRX4M transmission gear set of your choice (This transmission was designed around a 40.3:1 gear set but is compatible with most TRX4M gear sets.)

6 × 3×6×2.5 mm bearings (Some gear sets do not include bearings. These are standard TRX4M replacement bearings if needed.)

Thank you for purchasing the Stone Crab LCG Transmission! I truly appreciate your support and hope you enjoy building and running it as much as I enjoyed designing it.

If you have any questions, run into any issues, or have suggestions for future improvements, please don't hesitate to reach out. I'm always happy to help and appreciate any feedback that can make future designs even better.

Happy crawling!
details: All Part should be printed in PETG-CF filament or something of similar strength.  Front Plate, Rear Plate and the skid plates.  should be printed with 100% infill for strength.  Other parts can be printed in 50% or more Infill for strength.

name: PCBite Case for SQ10, SQXXX, and Base Plate
description:
This is a modular case design that can store a wide variety of PCBite probes and complete PCBite kits, including the base plate and PCB holders. It consists of an outer shell, the "Rugged Case", and "Inserts" that actually hold the PCBite kits.

There is one insert for 4x SQ10 probes and one for 2x SQXXX oscilloscope probes. The inserts are sized so that they can also store the large base plate (DIN A4), which means the 4x SQ10 insert is compatible with and will fit the complete "[PCBite kit with 4x SQ10 probes and test wires](https://sensepeek.com/pcbite-kit-with-4x-sq10-probes-and-test-wires)", and the 2x SQXXX insert will fit any of the "[PCBite kit with 2x SQXXX handsfree oscilloscope probes](https://sensepeek.com/pcbite-kit-with-2x-sq200-200-mhz-handsfree-oscilloscope-probes)" kits (where XXX stands for the bandwidth in MHz, such as 200 MHz, 350 MHz, or 500 MHz). That also means that the rugged case parts require a printer bed size of **244 mm x 316 mm**. It may be possible to split, print, and assemble the parts, but I haven't tested that.

The rugged case basically comes in two variants:

- "One Insert" variant, which holds one insert in the bottom part. The top part is a lid with an "Empty Top Insert" that prevents the base plate in the bottom part from moving.
- "Two Insert" variant, which holds two inserts, one in the bottom part and one in the top part. This means the case is larger, but it can hold twice twice the amount and is even compatible with the "Mixed Signal Kits" that come with 2x SQXXX and 4x SQ10 probes, like the "[PCBite kit with 2x SQ200 200 MHz and 4x SQ10 handsfree probes](https://sensepeek.com/pcbite-kit-with-2x-sq200-and-4x-sq10-handsfree-probes)".

There are two probe-head widths, so please measure the width of your probe first [see picture]. This only affects the inserts. The default files, including those in `PCBite Case (Bambu Studio).3mf`, are designed for 17.4 mm-wide probe heads. For 16.0 mm-wide probe heads, please use the files in `Probe Head 16.0mm.zip`.

Concerning the **Base Plate**, all inserts come in a "No Base Plate" and "With Base Plate" variant, so you can choose if you want the ability to store a base plate on top of that specific insert. This is especially useful for the larger "Two Insert" variant, where you might want to store one base plate, usually in the bottom part, and specifically opt for the `No Base Plate` option for the top part, which closes the gap and holds the base plate securely when the case is closed.

It is recommended that you use ferromagnetic washers, basically just steel washers, in the cavities below the probe feet and below the PCB holder. You can access them from the side (probe feet) or from the bottom (PCB holder). Install the probe feet and PCB holder first. Then simply use a bit of glue and place any washer that fits into the cavities; the installed parts will keep the washers in place while the glue cures.

There is also the option to use magnets to hold the base plate. This is not really necessary, as the base plate is held in place when the case is closed. But if you really want to store the base plate in the top part and have it stay attached when opening the case, you can use 4x 5x2 mm magnets on each side.

The rugged case is based on [this model](https://www.printables.com/model/793850-parameterized-rugged-box-openscad-with-tpu-gasket) by maxelman, which is based on a [model by OK1HRA](https://www.printables.com/model/716371-parameterizable-rugged-box-in-openscad) (License: CC BY-SA 4.0). I have published my version with all my improvements [here](https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/parameterized-rugged-case-box) (Cults), [here](https://www.printables.com/model/1772194-parameterized-rugged-case-box) (Printables), and [here](https://makerworld.com/en/models/3011541-parameterized-rugged-case-box#profileId-3382436) (MakerWorld; with online configurator). If you like, you can even use the OpenSCAD script to create a rugged case with other options, or use a completely different case as long as the inserts fit. The inner size should be 215 mm x 302 mm x 35 mm. The empty top insert needs a Z height of 14 mm. The corner radius should be 4.1 mm, and the bottom of the inserts has a 0.6 mm chamfer, so that should be slightly smaller inside the case.

## Assembly Instructions

Extra materials needed:

- 6x M3x30mm screws
- 1x washer for each probe (max. thickness: 2 mm; max. diameter: 16 mm)
- 1x washer for each PCB holder (max. thickness: 3 mm; max. diameter: 10 mm)
- [optional] 8x 5 mm magnets (2 mm thickness) for the base plate



1. **Choose the Case**: You need the `Bottom` part. Depending on which `Top` part you choose, the case can either hold one insert (`* One Insert.stl`) or two inserts (`* Two Inserts.stl`), each of which can hold a PCBite kit. Don't forget the two `Clips`. The TPU `Seal` is optional.
2. **Choose the Inserts**: Depending on the PCBite kits you would like to store, choose either `PCBite Kit 4x SQ10 Insert` or `PCBite Kit 2x SQXXX Oscilloscope Probe Insert`. You also have to choose if you want to store a DIN A4-sized base plate on top. `With Base Plate` has the recess for the base plate, while the `No Base Plate` version does not have this recess and should be used as the counterpart in the top part of the case. If you chose the `One Insert` case and want to add a base plate, you should also print `PCBite Empty Top Insert - No Base Plate` for the top part of the case. Lastly, make sure you select the inserts for the correct probe-head width. Measure the width of the probe [see picture]. If it is approximately 17.4 mm, you can use the default files. If it is approximately 16.0 mm, please use the files in `Probe Head 16.0mm.zip`.
3. **Choose the Storage Box Lid**: Each insert has an accompanying `Box Lid` to prevent the accessories inside from falling out. For a start, I would choose the `Normal` version. If your print is too loose or too tight, you can also choose the `Loose` or `Tight` variant to compensate for that.
4. **Choose the BNC Connector Clip**: This is only relevant for the `PCBite Kit 2x SQXXX Oscilloscope Probe Insert`. BNC (or SMB) connectors can have different diameters, so flexible connector clips are available for approximately 9 mm, 16 mm, and 19 mm diameters. Choose the clip that fits your connector best. The clip can slide along the guide rails to accommodate different connector lengths and positions.
5. **[optional] Color Paint**: If you want to color paint your print as well, you can of course do that. I used the `Fill` and `Edge detection` options. The case has a 0.01 mm extruded logo, so you can catch those features as well, which doesn't affect the print when it is not colored. The models in the `.3mf` for Bambu Studio are already painted for your convenience. 
6. **Print Your Case, Inserts, Storage Box Lid, and BNC Connector Clip**: I used PLA (black and yellow) with the default settings and a 0.2 mm layer height. No settings were changed, except for the BNC connector clips: use the `Arachne` wall generator (also make sure they are printed on their sides).
7. **Assemble the Case**: Now you need the 6x M3x30mm screws. [See pictures] Start with the 2x front screws on the bottom part. In general, you will probably need a screwdriver, but I don't recommend tightening them too much. Then place the top part on top and add the 2x screws for the hinge. In the front, you can now attach the two clips with the remaining 2x screws.
8. **Glue the Washers**: The washers are between the inserts and the case, and to prevent them from rattling, I recommend gluing them in with a small amount of glue. [See pictures] You'll need one washer per probe. They are placed in the teardrop-shaped recess on the front of the inserts, after adding a drop of glue. The washers for the PCB holder are added from the back side, again after adding a drop of glue. For both, I recommend placing the probe or PCB holder in the insert so the washer stays in place while the glue is curing.
9. **[optional] Glue the Magnets**: If you want to prevent the base plate from falling out when the case is open, when opening it while it is in the top part of the case, or if you just want to have the base plate secured a bit better, you can add a couple of small magnets on both sides. [See pictures] For me, 4x magnets on each side were enough to prevent the base plate from falling out when turning the insert upside down. The magnets are added near the center of the base plate, in my case in the center two of the four slits. If you want to add more, you can continue outward from there. I placed the insert on its side and temporarily kept the magnets toward the back with a washer, so I could easily place a drop of glue. Then remove the washer and add the base plate to keep the magnets secure while the glue is curing.
10. **Final Assembly**: Place the inserts into the case. They usually stay in there pretty well, but you can also add some glue if you like. Store the accessories in the storage box. Place the probes with the feet first, then the head, and then use the cable guide to store the cable. The exit of the cable guide is a clip that holds the end of the cable. For the oscilloscope probes, slide the selected BNC connector clip into the guide rails and adjust its position to fit the connector. Place the PCB holder in their dedicated spots. Place the base plate on top. The base plate is easily removed by pressing down in the front and then lifting the angled plate up.

**Enjoy your PCBite Case!**



For **commercial use**, please take a look at [this page](https://cults3d.com/en/3d-model/tool/pcbite-case-for-sq10-sqxxx-and-base-plate-commercial-use).

Manufacturing Technology
FDM 3D printing (filament‑based additive manufacturing)

Resistant to oils and lubricants

Slight flexibility prevents cracking under pressure

Suitable for repeated use during engine maintenance

Printer Settings
Layer height: 0.20 mm

Nozzle diameter: 0.4 mm

Wall thickness: 1.6–2.0 mm (4–5 perimeters)

Top/bottom layers: 4–5

Infill: 20–30% (Grid or Gyroid recommended)

Required only for the internal thread overhang

Use “Support on build plate only”

Support density: 10–15%

Model Orientation
Print vertically, with the threaded end facing upward

Minimizes risk of layer delamination

Produces a smooth internal funnel surface for clean oil flow

Post‑Processing
Remove supports carefully to avoid damaging the thread

Lightly deburr the thread using a soft tool or brush

Do not sand the internal funnel surface

name: ZF 8HF45, 8HP70 Valve Body Leak Testing Tool - Test Plate
description:
ZF 8HP45 / 8HP70 Test Stand

A test stand specifically designed for inspecting and testing ZF 8HP45 and ZF 8HP70 automatic transmissions. It allows for quick installation on a test bench to verify the operation of various hydraulic components, as well as for maintenance and development work.

Features:

* Compatible with ZF 8HP45 and 8HP70
* Quick installation
* Ideal for workshops, tuning shops, and training centers

For the ZF 8HP45 and 8HP70, pneumatic tests are primarily used to verify:
* piston seals,
* proper clutch travel,
* the absence of excessive leakage at the valve body.
Recommended pressure
* Compressed air: 2 to 4 bar (30 to 60 psi)
* It is best to start at around 2 bar, then increase if necessary.
* Higher pressure generally offers no benefit and can make interpretation more difficult.
Expected behavior
Port	Clutch    Normal behavior
A    Clutch A    Crisp engagement with a distinct “click,” followed by sustained pressure. Very little audible leakage.
B1    Clutch B    Distinct click and rapid piston movement. A slight residual leak is normal.
B2	Secondary Circuit B / NIC    More subtle movement, less pronounced noise. A small amount of leakage is acceptable.
C    Clutch C    Crisp engagement with a sharp click. Pressure must remain stable for several seconds.
D    Clutch D    Immediate engagement. If the piston returns immediately, suspect an internal leak.
E    Clutch E	Same behavior: smooth movement and sustained pressure with very little loss.
 
⸻
 
What you should hear
✅ Normal
* A “click” or “thump” as the piston moves.
* Followed by a slight, continuous hiss—very faint.
* If you cut off the air, the piston returns slowly.
⚠️ Minor leak
* A constant, faint whistling sound.
* The piston remains engaged, however.
* Often acceptable on a slightly worn assembly.
❌ Defect
* A loud, continuous hissing sound.
* You cannot feel the piston engaging.
* The piston barely moves or not at all.
* The pressure never builds up.
This generally indicates:
* a worn piston seal,
* a crack in the piston,
* a leak in the drum,
* a problem with the separator plate or valve body.
 
⸻
 
Handy tip
By placing a hand on the drum or the test plate:
* A, C, D, and E normally produce a very distinct click that’s easy to feel.
* B1 is slightly more muted but still clearly perceptible.
* B2 is the quietest; on some versions, there is only a slight movement accompanied by a faint hiss.
 
⸻
 
Hold time
With a valve body in good condition:
* After actuation, the piston must remain engaged for several seconds as long as air is present.
* A very gradual loss of pressure is normal.
* If the piston drops immediately or if air escapes rapidly as soon as pressure is applied, there is an abnormal leak.

name: Reusable Filament Spool for Refills | Honeycomb Masterspool (71mm)
description:
Save money and reduce plastic waste with this Reusable Filament Spool, perfectly optimized for Samlu and other 71mm inner core filament refills.

This model features a lightweight, material-saving honeycomb (hex) pattern on the side flanges, which not only looks great but also allows you to easily see how much filament you have left. The spool is split into two interlocking parts with a robust, easy-to-use threaded center. Simply slide your new Samlu filament refill onto the main core, screw the top half into place, cut the zip ties on your refill, and you are ready to print!

Key Features:

Perfect Fit for Samlu: Designed specifically to accommodate 71mm filament refills, making it fully compatible with Samlu brand refills.

Eco-Friendly & Cost-Effective: Stop buying plastic spools and switch to environmentally friendly masterspool refills.

Threaded Design: Secure, screw-together assembly that takes seconds to lock in place—no extra hardware required.

Lightweight Honeycomb Structure: Uses less plastic to print while maintaining high structural rigidity.

Support-Free Print: Designed to be easily 3D printed without any supports.
details:
For a durable and perfectly functioning spool, please follow these guidelines:

Recommended Material:PETG, or ABS/ASA. Stiff materials are best to ensure the spool holds its shape under the weight of a full 1kg filament roll. PETG is highly recommended if you plan to dry your filament while it is on this spool.

Orientation: Place both halves flat on the build plate (outer honeycomb faces touching the bed).

Supports: No supports required! The threads and overhangs are optimized to print cleanly without them.

Infill: 15% - 25% (Gyroid or Cubic).

Wall/Perimeter lines: 3 or 4 walls to ensure the threaded center section is incredibly strong and won't snap under tension.

Layer Height: 0.2mm is recommended for clean and smooth threads.

Assembly Note: Thread the two pieces together and unscrew them a few times empty to wear in the threads for a perfectly smooth fit before loading your first refill.

Note: The model shown in the preview images was 3D printed using ABS filament.

name: BMW F30 air scoop for F20 F21 F22 F23 F30 F32 F31 F34 F35 F36
description:
# BMW Air Scoop

Improve intake airflow and help reduce intake air temperatures with this upgraded Air Scoop, designed to integrate seamlessly behind the factory kidney grille on a variety of BMW models. The scoop channels cool outside air from the grille area toward the intake, helping provide a more consistent supply of fresh air to the engine.

**Note:** If installing on the opposite side of the grille, mirror the model in your slicer as needed.

## Required Hardware

* 2x M4x8 or M4x10 screws
* 2x M4 washers

## Features

### Improved Airflow Management

Directs cooler ambient air toward the intake tract for a more consistent supply of fresh air.

### Sharper Throttle Response

Helps provide a smoother, more linear, and predictable throttle feel.

### OEM-Inspired Fitment

Designed to blend naturally with the factory grille and engine bay appearance.

### Easy Installation

Simple bolt-on design requiring minimal modification.

### High-Speed Stability

Reinforced mounting structure helps ensure durability at highway and track speeds.

### Intercooler Friendly

Engineered to maintain unobstructed airflow to the intercooler.

## Installation

1. Remove the factory kidney grille.
2. Remove the factory plastic mesh piece
3. Position the Air Scoop and slide it into place. (Making sure it is fully installed on the rubber)
4. Attach the TPU mounting bracket to the V-brace support bar and scoop.
5. Secure the assembly using the M4 screws and washers. Do not overtighten.
6. Reinstall the grille and verify proper fitment and clearance.

## Disclaimer

This product is intended for off-road and motorsport use only. The user is responsible for verifying fitment and ensuring that the component is installed securely before operating the vehicle.
details:
Recommended materials:
1: ASA (Best overall)
2: PETG-CF
3: ASA-CF
4: ABS
5. Regular PETG 

1: TPU 90A
2: TPU 95A

(Be careful of warping and steep overhangs. Need a printer with adequate cooling and preferably a heated enclosure)

3 walls, high % gyroid infill, inner/outer wall order. Lower layer height for desired quality. 0.12 is recommended. Adaptive layer height can be used, but be mindful of surface defects. Took around four hours on a Bambu lab machine.

Il s'agit d'un clip de réparation pour lève-vitre conçu avec précision pour les modèles BMW E90 et E91, porte arrière gauche.

Ce clip est utilisé à l'intérieur du mécanisme du lève-vitre (régulateur) et relie le support de vitre au système de régulation actionné par câble. Il s'agit d'un point de défaillance courant sur les systèmes de vitres arrière des BMW E90/E91, où le curseur ou l'attache en plastique d'origine peut se fissurer, entraînant la chute de la vitre ou un dysfonctionnement.

Relier la vitre au mécanisme du régulateur
Guider le mouvement vertical de la vitre
Rétablir le bon fonctionnement du système de levage par câble
Remplacer les glissières en plastique d’origine cassées ou usées
Éviter le remplacement complet du régulateur
❌ Symptômes courants de défaillance

Lorsque le clip est endommagé :

La vitre tombe dans la portière
Le moteur tourne mais la vitre ne bouge pas
Bruit de grincement ou de cliquetis à l'intérieur de la portière
Vitre mal fixée dans le cadre de la portière

Plastique cassé visible à l'intérieur du lève-vitre

Il s’agit d’un petit clip en plastique, situé à l’intérieur de la portière arrière de la BMW, qui relie la vitre au mécanisme de levage ; lorsqu’il se casse, votre vitre cesse de fonctionner.

name: 2009-2014 Ford F150/F250 Turn Signal Switch Fix Kit
description:
Hardware Required: 3MM Hex and 3mm Variety Socket Head M3 

2009 - 2014 Ford F150 Turn Signal Switch Bracket Fix Kit .

The function of this Fix-Kit is to remount the turn signal switch assembly (male) into the main steering wheel circuitry housing (female) after a common issue with the plastic mounting threads cracking/breaking with extended use of the turn signal/high beams. As you use the switch it jerks the plastic housing around causing fractures. (Ford has these plastic housings made via NAFTA in Mexico.) When this happens you'll find loss in function in the switch for signaling turns, high beams, & operating the windshield wipers. Sometimes the switch will just break right off leaving you without crucial safety functions while operating a vehicle & could lead to fix-it tickets. With this kit you can remount your turn signal quickly return to driving safely & legally while saving money & time at the mechanics!

DIY FRIENDLY!! All hardware is easy & cheap to find 3mm

6 Piece Kit: Upper & Lower Brackets . 3 Locking Blocks. Switch Connector Reinforcement. Hardware & Tool Included.

Pictures show how the wedge and locking blocks uses specific areas for securing be sure before buying to disassemble & check that those areas are clear for this Kit to work correctly. There is maybe 3 Philip screws underneath your steering wheel once removed the plastic trim covers around the wheel will just unclip with a little tug. This will allow you to get a visual on the area of damage.


Assembly Order:

1. Remove Steering Wheel Cover, Determine Orientation of the mounts in correct slots, remove old & broken housing Upper Half

2. Install the Top Mount first

3. Install your switch & secure it to the top mount

4. Slide Bottom Mount into available slot over the bottom switch hole (Screw threads from inside/out)


- Top Mount uses rectangular backing to wedge & fasten securely in the open slot on top of the circuitry housing. The Top Mount replaces the top plastic over the steering wheel circuitry where your turn signal switch threads into the housing. You must remove the broken upper housing top portion that cracks so this kit can take the place of that top plastic. The top of the housing removes with little clips in various parts of the housing, wiggle the top portion around to determine the locations of the clips. Some material in this area will need to be removed with snips/razor blade. The housing is already broken so we can’t break it anymore! Compare the top mount to the area where it’ll go to judge how much material may need to be removed. If you’re having problems accessing the area while the steering wheel is on, try turning the wheel & looking for the sweet spot that gives you the most working space. The Top Mount screws in through the front of the switch into the hex nut in the back of the Mount. A drill may be required for making a hole for mounting one of the screws.


It is recommended to start with the Top Mount first as the Bottom Mount will slide into its dovetail/slot over the mounting hole of the turn signal switch. Be very careful not to push too hard or incorrectly on the switches input connectors these can be fragile if not carefully handled.


Optional: Lightly super glue the reinforcement cover for the input pegs to the other piece of plastic around the input pegs this adds strength back to your switch if it happen to crack when it disconnected from your housing circuitry. Be sure not to cover the input pegs on your switch.


- The Bottom Mount uses a slot where Ford has situated the Adjustable Foot Pedal Switch (Dovetail/Square Slot). If you have adjustable foot pedal switch you may not need the bottom mount as the switch itself reinforced the mounting area that cracks. Again, be sure to unclip/remove the upper half of the housing that breaks so this mount can fit. It screws in from the back with hex tool because the steering wheel will not give you enough clearance to effectively put the screw in from the front.

In the pictures I have a photo of the FORD part with part number to aid in information for understanding your steering assembly. There is 2 different endings to the parts number depending if you have adjustable foot pedal switch from factory this distinction is

 DA:  WITH adjustable pedals

CA:   w/o adjustable pedals

PART NUMBER:  DL3Z-3F791-CA

https://www.ebay.com/usr/rebelonesolutions

name: Universal EV Charger Wall Hook & Type 2 Plug Holder
description:
Overview
Keep your garage organized and your EV charger protected with this 2-in-1 wall-mounted holder. This design combines a secure dock for your charging nozzle and a sturdy hook to manage your heavy charging cables, preventing trips and keeping the connector off the ground.

Features

Secure Fit: Designed to hold standard EV connectors (Type 2 / J1772) firmly in place.

Cable Management: The integrated lower hook is wide enough to hold long and thick EV cables without causing stress on the wires.

Durable Design: Reinforced mounting holes for 3-point wall attachment to ensure it stays level even with heavy cables.

Protective Cover: The top "hood" design helps prevent dust and debris from entering the connector pins.

Mounting Holes: 4.5 mm diameter.

Compatible Screw Sizes: Optimized for M4 (4 mm) or 3.5 mm screws.

Countersunk Design: The holes are specifically designed with a countersink (tapered entry) to ensure that flat-head screws sit flush with the surface for a clean, professional look.

Installation Tip: Using a standard 6 mm wall plug (dowel) with M4 screws will provide the most secure fit for heavy EV cables.

name: Intex Replacement Part Single Button Spring for 10381 Swimming Pool Frame
description:
Intex Replacement Part Single Button Spring for 10381 Swimming Pool Frame

Деталь под номером #10381 — это одинарная пружинная кнопка (Single Button Spring), предназначенная для сборных бассейнов Intex. Она используется для фиксации металлических балок каркаса, защелкиваясь в соединительных отверстиях. 

Основные характеристики и совместимость
Назначение: Запасная часть для фиксации каркасных трубок в бассейнах серий Ultra Frame, Ultra XTR Frame и Prism Frame.
Материал: Пластик белого или серого цвета.
Размеры: Примерные габариты составляют около 68 x 60 мм, диаметр самой кнопки — около 0.9 см.
Количество: Обычно в комплекте идет 1 штука, но также продаются наборы по 4 или 8 штук.
details:
To achieve a functional and durable 3D-printed replacement for the Intex #10381 Single Button Spring, you should prioritize mechanical strength and flexibility over aesthetics. This part needs to act as a spring, so the material and orientation are critical.

Recommended Print Settings
Setting	Recommended Value	Why?
Material	PETG or ASA/ABS	PLA is too brittle and will snap when compressed. PETG offers the necessary "spring" flex and handles outdoor UV exposure better.
Orientation	On its side	Printing it flat on the grid (as seen in your CAD image) ensures the "layers" run the length of the frame. This prevents the button from snapping off under tension.
Infill	40% - 100%	Higher infill (specifically Gyroid) provides better structural integrity for spring-like tension.
Wall Count	4 - 6 Walls	Increasing wall loops is often more effective than infill for parts that need to bend without breaking.
Supports	Required	Since the cylindrical button hangs over the frame, you will need supports (use Tree Supports for easier removal).
Pro-Tips for Success:
Layer Adhesion: If using PETG or ASA, ensure your cooling fan is low (20-30%) to maximize bond strength between layers, preventing the spring from delaminating.
Fitment: The original part is roughly 68mm x 60mm with a 9mm button. Print a small test piece of just the button first to ensure it fits through your pool frame's hole.
Post-Processing: Lightly sand the top of the button to ensure it slides smoothly into the locking hole without catching.

name: Peugeot 307/206/207 1.6 HDI AirDoser delete kit
description:
Easy to print in standard FDM printer Airdoser delete kit (egr throttlebody delete kit) for 1.6 hdi engines (16v) that inculdes:
- elbow connecting intercooler to intake manifold with precise holes made for intake sensors (MAP and AIRTemp) so that you can use original orings,
- elbow connecting turbocharger to intercooler in 2 versions.

The outside diameters of the parts are exact as the ones being replaced so original hoses will fit althought i recommend using a plug and play silicone hose kit fot that engine.

Ispired by 1.6 hdi egr throttle body delete kit made with metal pipes but more accesible.  

Works in peugeot 307/206/207 and everywhere where there is airdoser shown in picture nr. 1.

Good printing.
details:
I included ready to print files with my own settings.

It is crucial is to use smallest possible layer hight as better the surface better the seal between 3d print and silicone connectors.

I recommend to use high temperature resistant epoxy on inside walls and outside area where the silicone hose will be clamped and sensors put in to make the seal air tight.
Epoxy is also recommended to cover area circled with blue color to make silicone pipe conections air tight (if not done oil will sip throught under clamps).

To get more clearence in sensor holes you can use hole compensation set at 0.1 or 0.2 for looser fit (if orings start to leak oil you can just use rtv silicone to seal the sensors).

Print "elbow_intercooler_intake manifold" with ASA or ABS, use 100% infill to prevent prints from warping by clamping force. 
For the "elbow_turbo_intercooler" you have to use higher heat resistant material like nylon with carbon (PA-CF, higher carbon amount the better but cost of the filament also goes up) fiber due to high temperature of the air exiting turbocharger (abs and asa will warp and crack over time).

For ASA or ABS set bed temp to 110 or 120 degrees celsius and warm up printer beforehand or use glue to prevent warping (long model).

Print requires supports.
