name: Spinning Wheel Bobbin compatible with WooLee Winder Regular for Ashford Joy
description:
Expand your bobbin collection easily with this custom designed DIY 3D printable bobbin made specifically for the Ashford Joy spinning wheel using a WooLee Winder flyer system. Whether you're spinning fine laceweight or bulky art yarn, this durable bobbin offers smooth, consistent performance with a modern twist. It's perfectly sized to fit the WooLee Winder Regular model for both the Joy 1 and Joy 2, and matches both the dimensions and weight of the wooden bobbins.

These bobbins also have a clever keyhole system that catches a knot on the end of your leader yarn and locks it in place as you begin spinning. Each bobbin has two keyholes, one on each side, to suit all spinning preferences.

Due to the difference in materials, these 3D printed bobbins may require much less tension than wooden bobbins; the exact difference may vary depending on the material of your brake band. Looser tensions may also introduce vibrations in the springs, so if you get any rattling, just check the alignment of the brake band, and wrap some loose fiber around the spring to dampen it. You can also run a graphite pencil around the brake band groove on the bobbin every so often as a sort of lubricant, if you want to use more tension.

Please note that my logo and branding information is located on the outer side of the bottom of the bobbin. If you would like your own logo, a convention logo, or other design debossed into the bobbin, please message me for details.

- Retraction: Properly configured to avoid threads of material between small parts.

name: PRESS TYPE C
description:
Estructura general:

Tiene una forma parecida a una letra "C", lo que le da su nombre. Este diseño permite un acceso fácil al área de trabajo y una buena visibilidad durante el prensado.

La parte curva de la "C" es gruesa y robusta, ya que es la encargada de soportar la presión que se aplica.

Partes principales:

Cuerpo o marco (en forma de C):

Impreso en una sola pieza sólida con paredes gruesas.

Recomendado imprimir con filamento de alta resistencia como PETG, ABS o incluso nylon.

Para usos de mayor fuerza, puede reforzarse con varillas metálicas o fibra de carbono en el diseño.

Husillo o tornillo de presión:

Se ubica en la parte superior del arco de la "C".

Este tornillo se gira para aplicar presión hacia abajo.

Puede imprimirse en 3D con rosca funcional, pero es mejor si se usa un tornillo metálico para mayor resistencia.

Base o yunque:

Parte inferior de la C, opuesta al husillo.

Es el área donde se coloca la pieza a trabajar.

Debe ser plana y firme.

Mango o manivela:

Se conecta al husillo para facilitar el giro y la aplicación de presión.

Puede imprimirse y luego añadirse un recubrimiento de goma o silicona para un mejor agarre.

I've used these:
MOTOR: https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005007591133504.html?spm=a2g0o.cart.0.0.71ea38daeDyQ5f&mp=1&pdp_npi=5%40dis%21EUR%21EUR%203.26%21EUR%203.26%21%21%21%21%21%40211b613917439386275286600e707a%2112000045893462506%21ct%21PT%211733909905%21%211%210

DC Power Jack (DC005): https://www.aliexpress.com/item/1005006827429781.html?spm=a2g0o.cart.0.0.71ea38daeDyQ5f&mp=1&pdp_npi=5%40dis%21EUR%21EUR%201.24%21EUR%201.24%21%21%21%21%21%40211b613917439386275286600e707a%2112000038431063959%21ct%21PT%211733909905%21%211%210

This motor can use a 12v power source.  
You may choose the dc power socket you want to use: There are 3 diferent DC slots to print. Just use the one you need. I've used the DC_slot3 for a DC005 power socket.
This motor has a 2.3mm shaft.  Print the motor_rotor_2 for this shaft. I've used savaged motor from an old printer so, used the motor_rotor_1.
The screw is attached only to motor_rotor. It must be loose on the Paint Arm or it will not rotate.

name: Universal motorcycle speed regulator - Cruise speed regulator for motorcycles
description:
Regulador de velocidad para motos

Mecanismo de control del acelerador impreso en 3D, que permite al piloto ajustar el acelerador a la posición deseada.

Instalación muy sencilla, tornillo/tuerca de acero inoxidable para apretar en el puño original de la moto.

Uso:

Para enganchar: Con la mano en el acelerador, puedes accionar el bloqueo con el dedo índice inclinando la pieza contra la palanca de freno. El rozamiento es suficiente (gracias al apriete del tornillo) para frenar el acelerador, y mantenerlo en la posición deseada.

Para reducir la velocidad: basta con reducir el acelerador, la pieza se desliza y mantiene la posición deseada.

Para desembragar: reduzca completamente el acelerador o presione la cruz de la parte inferior. La pieza vuelve entonces a su posición inicial.

name: Buzzy Bee Watering Station
description:
It was a sunny afternoon, and I was in the garden pretending to weed (translation: avoiding actual work). Suddenly, a low hum filled the air. I looked up to see a squadron of bees and bumblebees flying toward me with the urgency of late-night pizza delivery drivers.  

Their leader, a rather large bumblebee with a slightly dented fuzz, landed dramatically on my garden table. "Human!" he buzzed in a voice that somehow sounded both commanding and wheezy. "We need your help!"  

I blinked. "Uh, sure. What's the problem?"  

"We’re on a mission to save the world," he explained, puffing out his tiny chest. "Pollinating plants, feeding ecosystems, all the usual hero stuff. BUT…" He paused, glancing back at his buzzing comrades. "We forgot our water bottles."  

"Forgot your water bottles?" I repeated, trying not to laugh.  

"Yes," another bee chimed in, this one smaller but clearly more annoyed. "Barry was supposed to pack them. He forgot."  

"I thought someone else was bringing them!" Barry buzzed defensively.  

"Now we're dehydrated," the leader groaned, "and we can't carry on saving the world if we're about to pass out in your petunias."  

I scratched my head, trying to process this surreal situation. "Okay, so… what do you need from me?"  

"A watering station," said the leader. "Something practical. And stylish. We’re heroes, not heathens."  

"Right." I nodded, already brainstorming. I grabbed my Vernier caliper (of course, it’s my go-to tool in emergencies involving small creatures and precision measurements) and began sizing up some materials.  

I sketched out a plan for a bee-friendly watering station—something with little platforms for them to land on while they drank, shallow enough to avoid accidental bee drownings. Then, I fired up my 3D printer and got to work.  

As the printer hummed, the bees watched like construction foremen, occasionally buzzing out suggestions.  

“Make sure it’s non-slip!”  
“Can you add a cupholder?”  
“No cupholder, Barry!”  

After what felt like hours but was probably 20 minutes, the watering station was ready. It was a masterpiece of functionality and flair: tiny platforms for landing, shallow pools for drinking, and even a little bee-shaped flag on top (because why not?).  

I filled it with fresh water and placed it in the garden. The bees swarmed around it, inspecting every detail like it was a five-star hotel.  

"This is amazing!" the leader buzzed, taking a long sip. "You, human, are an honorary member of the Bee Brigade."  

"Uh… thanks?"  

The bees rehydrated and, within minutes, were buzzing with energy again. Barry gave me a sheepish thumbs-up (or at least I think he did—I might have imagined it).  

Before they flew off, the leader turned back. "We’ll remember this, human. You’ve done your part to save the world today."  

And with that, they were gone, off to continue their pollinating heroics.  

Now, every time I see a bee in my garden, I wonder if it’s one of them, stopping by to grab a sip and save the world. Maybe next time, I’ll print them a snack bar, too.

name: Pen Parts: Lamy Safari Ballpoint Tip
description:
I present my alternate tips for the Lamy Safari Ballpoint pen.
The issue with the Lamy M16 refill is that the tip diameter is only 2.2mm, while other refill like the D1 Mini are 2,3mm, while the Parker G2 has a 2.5mm tip. This means that Lamy pens that take the M16 have a tip hole that is too narrow for other refills. It could be drilled out, but that requires specific tools and is irreversible.

I've made replacement tips with either a 2.4mm or 2.6mm tip hole, so these tips, paired with my M16 refill adapters; should allow for some interesting alternative refill options.

I've also made an adapter part that allows the Safari pen to use the refill and tip from a Uni Signo 307 pen.
details: These parts need to be printed in resin or SLS plastic. FDM just doesn't have the dimensional accuracy needed (or at least it didn't used to).

name: 2-3/8 Inch Pipe Notch Pack
description:
This is a pack of tools for notching tubing 2-3/8 Inch in diameter and also drawing centerlines on them and attaching them to a tube of the same size.

Use the guide to mark the tube and then remove the material which is not covered by the 3D printed tool, the tube will then perfectly mate with the other tube at the selected angle, it has slots at 10 degree intervals so it can be aligned with the centerline drawn on a tube or angled to suit your needs.

There are two versions of the centerline tool, one will mark two centerline at 180 degrees from the other, the second will draw three lines at 90 degrees from the other, it will accept a pen up to 14mm in diameter and uses an M4 x 20mm bolt to fix the pens, using a lighter or soldering iron heat the bolt and then thread into to hole to make the threads, I have included knurled knobs to fix to either a hex or allen bolt for ease of adjustment without the use of tools(If a larger size bolt is wanted please message me)

CASE FEEDER STATICO A TUBO SINGOLO "ON TOP" 9mm

Da montare sulla pressa Lee Six Pack Pro (o Lee pro 6000) , rimane solidale con il telaio della Pressa.

A differenza della versione originale non sale e scende con il carry, ma rimane fisso,  liberando l'are di lavoro.

https://youtu.be/xZfiuCtdtEk?si=rcl5qt_Zlzh8MybU

Il sistema necessita anche di un case slider dedicato.
Purtroppo dalle prove fatte su varie presse, ho trovato una tolleranza fino a 2 mm della posizione del carry a fine corsa.
Una volta stampato il case feeder, occorre quindi scegliere quale case slider usare in base alle misure della propria pressa,
Ho incluso 3 misure di case slider, che dovrebbero coprire tutte le casistiche.

Oltre alla stampa occorrerà anche procurarsi la seguente minuteria metallica:

1) Molla 0,7x10x5mm:
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_oB5OMHv
https://amzn.to/3OX70g4

2) Perno acciaio 2x20mm
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_oFXVT8T
https://amzn.to/4ixMcsZ

3) Bullone M10x50mm con rondella
https://amzn.to/4fiavZk
https://amzn.to/3DqgSfz
https://amzn.to/4fdhnXK
https://amzn.to/41zoKWr

4)  Molla 0.5x15x6
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_oFY7tvL

5) Dado M3  autobloccante acciaio DIN985
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_onsmauz
https://amzn.to/4i9mevo

6) Vite testa cilindrica a brugola M3x35 (15mm parte liscia)
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_opTFf2z
https://amzn.to/3FKShDm

Istruzioni:
1) Stampare la base del  case feeder in PETG (infil 100%) utilizzando i supporti ad albero dal solo piatto.
2) Stampare la testa del case feeder anches enza supporti.
3) Stampare la leva e allargare il foro della leva con una punta da 2mm.
4) Verificare che il perno da 2 mm scorra bene nel foro della leva, , senza attrito, eventualmente allargare il foro a 2,5 mm.
5) Ripulire ed eventualmente ripassare il foro sulla base, inserire la molla da 15mm e la vide M3x35.
6) Inserire i 5 pistoncini a sfera nella testa (eventualmente ripulire e ripassare i fori con una punta da mm)  e far passare la vide m3x35 in modo da accoppiare le due parti (Eventualmente ripassare il foro per la vite con una punta da 3mm)
7) Avvitare il dado autobloccante alla vite, accoppiando le due parti (testa e base ) in modo che scorrano opportunamente sui pistoncini a sfera.
8) Inserire la leva nella base del feeder dalla parte bassa, inclinandola a 45° circa, in modo che la molla da 10mm possa essere posizionata agevolmente.
9) Comprimere la molla e posizionare la leva nel suo alloggio.
10) Inserire nel condotto dei bossoli uno spessore, in modo da allineare il foro sul case feeder con quello sulla leva.
11) Inserire ad incastro il perno nel case feeder (usando un martello), ma facendo in modo che la leva sia libera di muoversi sull'asse del perno.
12) Rimuovere lo spessore dal condotto dei bossoli e verificare il funzionamento della leva.
13) Inserire nella testa del feeder 5 tubi standard Lee (vanno bene quelli del case feeder universale incluso con la pro 6000), caricare dei bossoli e verificare che tutto funzioni a dovere
14) Misurare la distanza tra la testa della pressa e la slitta su cui scorrono i bossoli, per scegliere il case slider da stampare:

d=35,5 -> stampare Case slider base.
d=36.5 -> stampare Case slider +1 mm
d=37.5 -> stampare Case slider +2 mm

Per effettuare la misura rimuovere i dies e portare la leva della pressa alla sua massima estensione in modo che lo shell plate sia nella posizione più alta, e la leva della pressa completamente abbassata.
15) inserire il case feeder nel foro presente sulla testa della pressa, fissandolo con il bullone, avendo cura di inserire la vite dalla parte inferiore assieme alla rondella.Stringere il dado nella parte superiore.
16) Sostituire il case slider, usando il foro piu' esterno.
17) Caricare qualche bossolo nel tubo e verificare il funzionamento del case feeder.

Per qualsiasi dubbio potete contattarmi dal blog: WWW.TARGETFUN.IT o dal canale youtube @TARGETFUN
----------------------
To be mounted on the Lee Six Pack Pro press (or Lee Pro 6000), it remains fixed to the frame of the press.

Unlike the original version, it does not move up and down with the carrier, but stays in place, freeing up the working area.

https://youtu.be/xZfiuCtdtEk?si=rcl5qt_Zlzh8MybU

The system also requires a dedicated case slider.
Unfortunately, from tests conducted on various presses, I found up to 2 mm tolerance in the carrier's end-of-stroke position.
Once the case feeder is printed, you’ll need to choose which case slider to use based on your specific press’s measurements.
I’ve included 3 sizes of case sliders, which should cover all possible scenarios.

In addition to 3D printing, you will also need to get the following metal hardware:

Spring 0.7x10x5mm:
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_oB5OMHv
https://amzn.to/3OX70g4

Steel pin 2x20mm
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_oFXVT8T
https://amzn.to/4ixMcsZ

M10x50mm bolt with washer
https://amzn.to/4fiavZk
https://amzn.to/3DqgSfz
https://amzn.to/4fdhnXK
https://amzn.to/41zoKWr

Spring 0.5x15x6
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_oFY7tvL

M3 self-locking nut, steel DIN985
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_onsmauz
https://amzn.to/4i9mevo

M3x35 socket head screw (15mm smooth section)
https://s.click.aliexpress.com/e/_opTFf2z
https://amzn.to/3FKShDm

Instructions:

Print the base of the case feeder in PETG (100% infill) using tree supports from the build plate only.
Print the feeder head without supports.
Print the lever and enlarge the lever hole with a 2mm drill bit.
Ensure the 2mm pin slides smoothly into the lever hole without friction; if needed, enlarge the hole to 2.5mm.
Clean and possibly rework the hole on the base, insert the 15mm spring and the M3x35 screw.
Insert the 5 ball plungers into the head (clean and rework the holes with a drill bit if needed), and pass the M3x35 screw through to couple the two parts (rework the screw hole with a 3mm drill bit if necessary).
Screw the self-locking nut onto the screw, joining the two parts (head and base) so they slide properly on the ball plungers.
Insert the lever into the base of the feeder from the bottom, tilting it about 45°, so the 10mm spring can be positioned easily.
Compress the spring and place the lever in its seat.
Insert a spacer in the case conduit to align the hole in the case feeder with the one in the lever.
Press-fit the pin into the case feeder (using a hammer), making sure the lever can move freely on the pin axis.
Remove the spacer from the case conduit and check the lever's movement.
Insert 5 standard Lee tubes into the feeder head (those from the universal case feeder included with the Pro 6000 are fine), load some cases and check if everything works correctly.
Measure the distance between the press head and the slide rail where the cases move, to choose which case slider to print:
d=35.5 -> print Base Case Slider
d=36.5 -> print Case Slider +1mm
d=37.5 -> print Case Slider +2mm

To take this measurement, remove the dies and fully extend the press handle so the shell plate is in its highest position, with the press handle completely lowered.
15) Insert the case feeder into the hole on the press head, securing it with the bolt, making sure to insert the screw from the bottom with the washer. Tighten the nut on the top.
16) Replace the case slider, using the outermost hole.
17) Load a few cases into the tube and test the case feeder’s operation.

For any questions, feel free to contact me through the blog: WWW.TARGETFUN.IT or on the YouTube channel @TARGETFUN

name: OrbiTable12 – The Ultimate Rotating Platform for Creators
description:
🚀 Your 3D prints deserve the spotlight! 🚀

Tired of static shots that don’t do your work justice? OrbiTable12 is here to elevate your content game! This motorized, 3D-printable turntable is designed for makers, photographers, and 3D printing enthusiasts who want to showcase their models in cinematic, smooth rotation. Whether you’re creating epic product shots, mesmerizing timelapses, or simply flexing your latest print, this is the ultimate tool to bring your designs to life!

For the showcase, I had the honor of using incredible 3D-printed Star Wars figurines, generously provided by [UTSAV_GENESIS](https://cults3d.com/en/users/Utsav_Genesis). If you love highly detailed 3D models, go check out his work at and give him a follow! 🔥

**🌀 Features:**
• Direct gear drive for smooth and stable rotation.
• USB-powered (5V) with an optional switch for forward/reverse motion.
• Compact 20 cm diameter – ideal for small to medium-sized objects.
• PETG, ASA, or ABS recommended for best durability.
• Snap-in assembly for printed parts, with minor soldering required for the motor (switch optional).


**🏗️ Assembly Instructions:**
1️⃣ Print all parts according to the recommended settings.
2️⃣ Insert one 623ZZ bearing tightly into the center hole of the base (press-fit).
3️⃣ Attach four additional 623ZZ bearings as wheels, using M3x10 or longer screws.
4️⃣ Solder the power wires to the Mini N20 motor (switch optional).
5️⃣ Press-fit the motor into the holder (tight fit).
6️⃣ Press-fit the gear onto the motor shaft.
7️⃣ Use a recycled USB cable for power (ideally, but a new one can be used if necessary – we support upcycling! ♻️).
8️⃣ Snap-in the legs, then glue the cable cover (hot glue or CA glue recommended) for secure attachment.
9️⃣ Plug it in and enjoy seamless rotation!

**📂 Included STL Files:**
orbitable12-platform-by-ondrahaa.stl → Rotating platform
orbitable12-base-by-ondrahaa.stl → Main base
orbitable12-motor-mount-by-ondrahaa.stl → Motor and cable holder
orbitable12-gear-motor-by-ondrahaa.stl → Gear for direct drive
orbitable12-legs-by-ondrahaa.stl → Snap-in support legs
orbitable12-switch-cover-by-ondrahaa.stl → Cover for the micro switch
orbitable12-cable-cover-by-ondrahaa.stl → Cover for the USB cable exit

**📌 Ideal For:**
✅ 3D printing hobbyists & makers
✅ Product photography & videography
✅ Showcasing figurines, collectibles, and small models

🔽 Download now and upgrade your content game with smooth, automated rotation!

**Notes:**
• This model is designed for the Mini N20 DC motor with USB 5V power.
• Switch is optional – the motor runs fine without it.
• Requires 4× 623ZZ bearings + 1× press-fit 623ZZ bearing in the center.
• Ensure all parts fit snugly before running the motor.
• USB power cable must be salvaged from an old device (ideally, but new cables can be used if needed).
• Cable cover should be glued in place for best results (hot glue or CA glue recommended).
• I personally scavenged the switch from a child’s old Star Wars projector. 💀✨

name: Soft Plastic Bait Mold Curlytail
description:
Soft Bait Mold – Single Cavity

Long - 2''

This is a single cavity soft bait mold designed to create curly tail grub lures in one smooth injection. The mold ensures a well-defined tail shape that enhances the bait's swimming action, making it ideal for various fishing conditions. The final lure has a lifelike, fluttering tail movement, mimicking injured baitfish or worms to attract predatory fish effectively.

Key Features:
Curly tail design for enhanced swimming action.
Optimized cavity for consistent bait shaping.

Injection Tips:
This is a 3D-printed/CNC-milled mold, so be mindful of temperature and injection pressure.
If using a 3D-printed version, PLA+ or high-temp resins are recommended.
Plastisol should be injected at around 300°F (150°C).
Use gentle, steady pressure to avoid damaging the mold. Applying excessive force can lead to leaks or misformed baits.
If you're new to soft bait molding, I recommend watching tutorial videos on how to properly inject plastisol into 3D-printed or CNC-milled molds before purchase.

Happy bait making, and tight lines! 🎣

details:
Parámetros Básicos de Impresión 3D – Organizador de Cables de Red CAT6

Para obtener la mejor calidad y resistencia en la impresión de este organizador, se recomienda utilizar los siguientes parámetros:  

- **Material recomendado:
 PLA, PETG o ABS (según las condiciones de uso).  
- Altura de capa: 0.2 mm (para un buen equilibrio entre calidad y tiempo de impresión).  
- Densidad de relleno:15-30% (suficiente para brindar rigidez sin desperdiciar material).  
- Número de perímetros: 3 (para mayor resistencia).  
- Temperatura de impresión: 
  - PLA: 190-220°C  
  - PETG: 220-250°C  
  - ABS: 230-260°C (requiere cama caliente y recinto cerrado)  
- Temperatura de cama: 
  - PLA: 50-60°C  
  - PETG: 70-80°C  
  - ABS: 90-110°C  
- Velocidad de impresión: 40-60 mm/s.  
- Retracción: Habilitada (ajustar según el material para evitar hilos).  


Orientación de Impresión
Para evitar el uso de soportes y mejorar la calidad de las ranuras, se recomienda imprimir el organizador

 -Colocado sobre la parte inferior o superior.
 De esta manera, las aberturas quedarán bien definidas y se reducirá el tiempo de impresión sin necesidad de limpiar soportes.  

Este diseño es fácil de imprimir y optimizado para obtener una pieza funcional y duradera en cualquier entorno de redes o telecomunicaciones.

They commonly have B399A on them, but not always. Locksmiths have the blank, but why pay $6 and $10 USD each for them? Well here's an alternative -- just print your own!

Should be 1.625" long, so 41mm should do it.

There's a version with "TP" embossed on it for people who use it for things that start with letters like that.

The current orientation will work well without supports, and print very cleanly. PLA is fine, because these really aren't high-tolerance locks, but I do recommend something like PETG so they last a while.  Even the metal keys break off in our TP dispensers every few months.

name: BMG Phaetus Dragon HF/UHF Direct Drive for Creality Ender 3 (Pro/V2) & CR-10
description:
This is a new version of my popular BMG E3D V6 direct drive for the Creality Ender 3, Ender 3 Pro, Ender 3 V2, and CR-10, now designed for Phaetus hotends (HF and UHF). 

**Key Features**
- **Designed in France**
- **Optimized for high-speed printing and Klipper Firmware** : The high stiffness of the printhead reduces vibrations and allows high accelerations/decelerations.
- **Easy to print, install & maintain** : High accessibility with no adjustments required. Only 3 parts to print. Can be fully disassembled and reassembled in minutes without needing to readjust anything. Ensures the highest accuracy and repeatability. No need to periodically change the PTFE tube thanks to the all-metal hotend.
- **Perfect retractions and improved print quality** : The hotend is directly connected to the extruder, ensuring more responsive extrusion, cleaner starts & stops, and perfect retractions.
- **Compatible with flexible filaments/TPU**
- **Minimalist, compact & lightweight design**
- **Optimized & highly efficient cooling** : Achieve high print speeds (up to 150 mm/s) while maintaining perfect bridges and overhangs.
- **Clean cable management** : Cables secured with zip ties for a cleaner setup, reduced noise, and fewer vibrations.
- **Excellent nozzle visibility** : Easily monitor the first layer and fine-tune the Z-offset in real-time.
- **No reduction in print volume** : Maintains full 230x230x250 mm print capacity.
- **Easy to print** : Can be printed support-free with only 3 parts to print.

**Assembly**
For assembly instructions, check the attached PDF and this video: https://youtu.be/qMe2saso00Y

name: Sweetheart Yarn Bowl
description:
Just in time for Valentine’s Day, the sweetest companion for your knitting and crochet is here! Each bowl is crafted to hold a skein of worsted yarn and then some :).
